items.desc: At Flexion, we're building the intelligence layer powering the next generation of humanoid robots. Our mission is to accelerate the transition from fragile prototypes to real-world humanoid deployment. We are founded by leading scientists in robot reinforcement learning (ex-Nvidia, ex-ETH Zürich), and backed by leading international VC firms. In just months, we’ve gone from our first line of code to deploying real humanoid capabilities. The role As our VLA/WAM Research Engineer, you'll develop the foundation models that power our humanoid robots, spanning model architecture, large-scale pre-training, adaptation, and post-training. You will work across the model lifecycle: designing VLA and World-Action Model architectures, training foundation models on large and diverse embodied datasets, developing methods for efficient adaptation to new tasks and embodiments, and using robot experience to continuously improve model capabilities. In particular, we are looking for researchers and engineers with deep experience in one or more of the following areas: VLA/VLM or multimodal model architecture, large-scale foundation-model pre-training, world models and predictive learning, robot learning, or post-training and continual learning. If you have strong depth in one of these areas and are excited to work across the broader problem of building general-purpose robot foundation models, you will be a strong fit for the role. Key responsibilities VLA/WAM Architecture: Design and develop multimodal foundation models combining vision, language, robot state, actions, and temporal context for general-purpose robotic control. Foundation Model Pretraining: Develop and execute large-scale pretraining across diverse robot embodiments, teleoperation, egocentric human data, and simulated experience. Training Recipes & Scaling: Improve data mixtures, training objectives, optimization strategies, and distributed training workflows to deliver increasingly capable foundation models on a regular cadence. World-Action Models: Develop predictive world and action models for representation learning, future-state prediction, planning, and robot policy improvement. Adaptation & Mid-training: Develop methods to efficiently adapt pretrained models to new tasks, environments, embodiments, and capabilities. Post-training & Reinforcement Learning: Improve models using real-world and simulated robot experience, including imitation learning, RL, reward/value-guided learning, and specialist-to-generalist distillation. Continual Learning: Develop methods to learn from autonomous rollouts, failures, interventions, and recoveries while retaining existing capabilities and avoiding catastrophic forgetting. Evaluation & Research: Design rigorous experiments, evaluate models in simulation and on real robots, and use results to guide architecture and training decisions. Requirements Strong Python and PyTorch skills, with hands-on experience developing and training modern deep-learning models. Research or engineering experience in one or more of the following: VLA/VLM architectures, multimodal foundation models, world models, large-scale pretraining, robot learning, or RL/post-training. Experience owning substantial model development or training experiments, including architecture choices, training objectives, optimization, and evaluation. Solid understanding of modern deep-learning architectures, representation learning, and the relationship between data, training objectives, and model performance. Ability to design rigorous experiments, diagnose training failures, and use empirical results to guide research decisions. Familiarity with large-scale datasets, model training workflows, and the challenges of generalization across tasks, environments, or embodiments. Ability to critically evaluate recent research and translate promising ideas into working models and experiments. Comfortable working across model architecture, training, and adaptation while bringing particular expertise in at least one of these areas. Additionally, the following are a plus but not required: Experience training VLA, VLM, diffusion, flow-matching, video/world models, or other multimodal generative architectures. Experience with distributed training, multi-node GPU systems, large-scale data mixtures, and foundation-model training optimization. Experience with reinforcement learning, offline RL, reward/value learning, specialist distillation, or continual learning. Experience with predictive world models, video generation, latent dynamics, or self-supervised representation learning. Experience with multi-embodiment robot learning, action representations, or adapting policies across different robot platforms. Experience working with teleoperation, egocentric video, simulation, autonomous rollouts, or other large-scale embodied datasets. Experience evaluating learned policies on real robots, particularly humanoids or dexterous manipulation systems. Benefits Competitive compensation …

items.desc:
Our Mission
Aleph Alpha is one of the few companies in Europe doing serious foundation model pre-training like our recently released Kolibri-1 model https://huggingface.co/Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1. Our customers - in finance, manufacturing, public administration - need models that understand German, meet European regulatory requirements, and work reliably in high-stakes settings. We're building that in Heidelberg.

We are hiring an AI Researcher (f/m/d) to join our Pre-training team and help advance the architecture and training of our next generation of foundation models. If you are excited about how large models learn, want to run experiments that feed directly into production training runs, and want hands-on time on large-scale clusters (thousands of NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs), we would love to hear from you.

Team Culture
We foster a culture built on ownership, autonomy, and empowerment. Teams and individual contributors are trusted to take responsibility for their work and drive meaningful impact. We maintain a flat organizational structure with efficient, supportive management that enables quick decision-making, open communication, and a strong sense of shared purpose. We collaborate closely on complex technical problems, working in pairs or using mob programming to resolve challenging issues. New team members learn through real work: from your first weeks you will pair with experienced researchers on live problems, and take on more ownership as you grow into it.

About the Role
As an AI Researcher in Pre-training (f/m/d), you will work on the technical levers that determine the success of our next-generation models: architecture, optimization, stability, and scaling.

Working at the intersection of research and engineering, you will learn to translate mathematical reasoning and empirical observations into principled training decisions, from small-scale proxy experiments to multi-thousand-GPU runs. You will start with well-scoped problems alongside senior researchers and progressively take ownership of larger parts of the training recipe.

We are looking for someone with strong fundamentals, sharp experimental instincts, exceptional skills, and the drive to go deep fast. You learn as much from a failed run as from a paper, you write code others can build on, and you want to become an expert in large-scale pre-training.

Your Responsibilities

 - Recipe & Architecture Experiments: Design and run ablations on core elements of the training recipe (optimizers, schedules, initialization), and implement PyTorch-based architectural changes. Evaluate their effect on convergence, stability, and training efficiency.

 - Scaling Experiments: Run and analyze small-scale proxy experiments, and contribute to the hyperparameter scaling laws and scale-up methods we use to predict behavior at multi-thousand-GPU scale.

 - Run Monitoring & Debugging: Help monitor large-scale training runs and investigate convergence issues such as loss spikes and divergence. Work with the team to track down distributed training failures.

 - Research to Practice: Follow the literature, reproduce promising results at small scale, and bring ideas worth testing to the team.

 - Cross-Team Collaboration: Work with the Compute Performance, Data, Evaluation, and Post-Training teams to understand how hardware constraints and the rest of the model lifecycle shape pre-training decisions.

Core Qualifications

 - You are proficient in Python and have hands-on experience with PyTorch.

 - You have a strong foundation in machine learning, shown through research (e.g., a PhD, a strong MS'c thesis, or publications), open-source contributions, or substantial professional or substantial personal projects.

 - You have a solid mathematical background (linear algebra, probability, optimization) and enjoy reasoning formally about why models train the way they do.

 - You understand how transformers work and have pre-trained LLMs from scratch yourself, even at small scale.

 - You design experiments carefully, report noisy and negative results honestly, and can explain clearly what your evidence does and does not show.

 - You have a track record of picking up unfamiliar technical areas quickly and going deep, for example by reimplementing papers, ramping up on a large new codebase, or debugging a problem well outside your comfort zone.

 - You write clean, maintainable code and care about reproducible experiments.

 - You communicate clearly, raise problems early, and actively seek out and act on feedback.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Distributed Training: Experience training models on multi-GPU or multi-node setups, or familiarity with distributed frameworks (e.g., Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, torchtitan) and parallelism strategies (data, tensor, pipeline, expert).

 - Training Dynamics: Familiarity with scaling laws, hyperparameter transfer (e.g., µP), or recent work on optimizers and training stability.

items.desc: About Us Albs is an AI research lab building real-time multimodal intelligence for machines, enabling them to see, hear, reason, and interact. We treat model architecture, inference, and runtime as one system. Our purpose-built models and optimized runtimes unlock the full potential of each device within defined limits for hardware cost, power consumption, and response time. Companies can adapt our technology to their own machines without building the underlying AI from scratch. We founded Albs at the intersection of LLM architecture research and on-device engineering, and we are currently in stealth, but well funded, with dedicated compute for large-scale training and experimentation. Publishing is a core part of our research culture, and we contribute our work to top venues. We share more details about the company, the team and our backing in the first conversation. Who we're looking for This is a Staff / Senior IC role. We are looking for experienced researchers and engineers, typically with a PhD and several years of research or industry experience or an equivalent track record. The exact scope of each role depends on your background: some people go deep on one part of the stack, others shape the technical direction of a whole area. We agree on scope together with you during the interview process. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, age, ethnic origin, religion, disability or sexual orientation. What you'll work on Work across the pre-training stack, including data pipeline, model architecture, model optimization, training and evaluation. Develop and evaluate novel ideas across architecture, optimizers, and training algorithms. Make training run efficiently on multi-node GPU clusters, down to low-level system optimizations. Design for the hardware from the start: co-design architectures with the hardware optimization team so our models run efficiently on-device. Publish at top venues and help shape our research agenda in LLM architecture and optimization. What we're looking for You hold a PhD in a relevant field and have several years of research experience after it, in academia or industry, or an equivalent track record. You are an expert in LLM architectures and/or deep learning optimization, with design decisions that measurably improved model quality or efficiency. You have pre-trained LLMs on budgets of 100k+ GPU hours, with large-scale distributed training (FSDP, TP, PP, CP). You have a strong research track record in the field (e.g. NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR). You have deep Python and PyTorch proficiency and are comfortable reading and modifying low-level training code. How We Work Together We are a small, focused team of experts. You would join early, work directly with the founders, and help shape how we build. Fast iteration, short lines of communication, and in-person discussion matter a lot to us. Our culture is built around the office in Freiburg, Germany, with a default of three days a week on site. Alternatively, you can work remotely and join us on a regular cadence. We will discuss what works best for you during the interview process. We hold ourselves to a high standard: the research must be rigorous, the understanding deep, and the product well crafted. Ideas are judged on their merit, not on who proposed them, credit belongs to the team, and no task is beneath anyone. We make ambitious bets and ship early instead of waiting for perfect conditions. Above all, we care about each other, because initiative only works when it comes with respect for the people around you. What we offer Expect a competitive base salary plus equity, and dedicated compute for your research and experiments. We give you the time and support to publish and present at top conferences, and flexibility in how you work, whether on site or remote with regular in-person visits. With flat hierarchies and short decision paths, good ideas move from discussion to experiment quickly. And yes, the coffee is excellent, and we regularly get together as a team outside of work. We go through compensation and all other details with you early in the process.

items.desc: About REVEL REVEL is an AI robotics company developing physical intelligence for general-purpose humanoid robots. We capture the force, dexterity and intent of human work with our Neural Gambit wearable, and use it to train RAI, the intelligence that powers our robots. Our R&D and engineering facilities are in Prague, Czech Republic. This role is on-site with our team in Prague. The intent layer is REVEL's core differentiator: reading neuromuscular signals 30 to 100 ms before motion. We're looking for a scientist to decode high-density surface EMG into force and intent. The role We are looking for a scientist to develop methods for decoding high-density surface EMG (HD-sEMG) into continuous measures of human movement, force and motor intent. A central research question is how much information about forthcoming movement and mechanical output can be extracted from neuromuscular activity before observable movement occurs. You will investigate this temporal relationship experimentally and develop models that can exploit it under realistic conditions. This is a highly experimental role. You will work with real human data, noisy physiological signals, wearable hardware and evolving data-collection protocols, while translating scientific findings into models that can ultimately support robotic intelligence. Responsibilities 3+ years of relevant professional experience Develop signal-processing and machine-learning methods for decoding HD-sEMG into continuous force, joint kinematics and motor intent. Characterise the temporal relationship between neuromuscular activity and mechanical movement, including the potential 30 to 100 ms anticipatory window. Design experiments to quantify the reliability, information content and limits of anticipatory information in sEMG. Develop preprocessing and signal-quality methods for multi-channel EMG, including filtering, artefact handling, normalization and channel-quality assessment. Investigate the effects of sensor placement, electrode contact, motion artefacts, fatigue, physiological variability and session-to-session drift. Evaluate model robustness across operators/subjects, sessions, movements and sensor configurations. Develop methods for cross-operator, cross-session and cross-condition generalisation, including efficient calibration where necessary. Design capture and labelling protocols together with the data-collection team. Define data-quality criteria and experimental metrics that enable reliable downstream ML. Collaborate closely with the robotics ML team to translate biosignal representations and decoded intent into inputs suitable for RAI. Prototype and evaluate models in real-time or near-real-time settings where appropriate. Communicate experimental results clearly and use them to guide the next iteration of the sensing, modelling and data-collection system. Requirements 3+ years of relevant professional experience Hands-on experience with EMG or electrophysiological biosignals, including signal acquisition, preprocessing and quantitative analysis. Strong understanding of signal processing for noisy, non-stationary physiological signals. Experience developing machine-learning models for time-series or sequential data. Strong Python skills and practical experience with PyTorch or JAX. Experience designing, executing and analysing controlled experiments. Ability to reason quantitatively about temporal alignment, latency, prediction, signal quality and model generalisation. Experience working with real-world biological data where signal characteristics vary across people and sessions. Strong scientific judgement and the ability to distinguish genuine physiological information from artefacts, leakage and experimental confounds. Bonus Qualifications PhD or equivalent research experience in biomedical engineering, neuroscience, electrical engineering, biomechanics, computer science, machine learning or a related field; alternatively, an MSc with 2 to 3+ years of highly relevant research or industry experience. Experience with high-density sEMG / electrode arrays. Experience with multi-channel EMG decomposition, motor-unit activity or neuromuscular physiology. Experience decoding force, torque, joint kinematics or motor intention from biosignals. Background in motor control, biomechanics or human movement science. Experience with wearable sensing and human-subject experiments. Experience with domain adaptation, calibration or cross-subject generalisation. Familiarity with real-time inference and latency constraints. Experience deploying ML models outside purely offline research environments. Why REVEL Work That Ships: We capture how skilled humans work, their force, touch, and judgment, and our robots do the work. You put robots on a paying customer's floor, not in a demo loop The Team: Colleagues from NVIDIA, SpaceX, and Neura Robotics, and founders you work with directly. No layers, no process between you and the decisions Your Own Hardware: A top-spec GPU …

items.desc: About REVEL REVEL is an AI robotics company developing physical intelligence for general-purpose humanoid robots. We capture the force, dexterity and intent of human work with our Neural Gambit wearable, and use it to train RAI, the intelligence that powers our robots. The role We are looking for an experienced computer vision engineer to build the perception that lets our humanoid robot, GENESIS, see and understand its workspace in real time. You will turn REVEL's recordings of skilled human work, captured with several cameras and the Neural Gambit wearable, into models that track hands, tools, and objects in 3D. Then you will get those models running on the robot. Every manipulation skill the robot learns depends on seeing hands, tools, and objects accurately. Perception errors show up as failed grasps on a customer's floor. You will join a small Perception team in Prague and work closely with our Robot Learning and Data Collection teams. Most of the team is early in their careers, so you will help set how we build, evaluate, and ship models, and support the junior engineers along the way. What You'll Do Build hand, tool and object tracking in 3D from our multi-camera and wearable recordings of people doing manual work. Develop detection, segmentation, pose estimation and 3D scene understanding for the robot's manipulation skills. Calibrate and synchronise multi-camera and depth setups in the lab and on the robot, and keep them accurate over time. Build training and evaluation pipelines that anyone on the team can rerun months later: data, labelling, dataset versioning and experiment tracking. Design evaluations around what the robot needs, not only benchmark scores, and find out why a model fails on real data. Get models running in real time on the robot's onboard GPU (ONNX, TensorRT, quantisation or similar). Work with Robot Learning and Data Collection on what to record and what perception the next skill needs. Help set engineering standards in a small, young team. Who We're Looking For 3+ years of hands-on computer vision work in industry or research, with models you trained yourself running on real camera data, not only on benchmarks. Strong Python and PyTorch. Solid Linear Algebra and 3D Computer Vision fundamentals. Deep-learning fundamentals for vision (detection, segmentation, pose estimation or 3D vision) and rigorous evaluation. Experience with real cameras and real-world data: calibration, multi-camera setups, noise, lighting and latency. Experience taking a model from training to real-time inference on a robot or an edge device. Good engineering practice: Git, Linux, clean code and reproducible experiments. Honesty about what you know. You say "I don't know" when you don't, take criticism of your ideas well, and still defend a good idea with evidence. Fluent English for daily work with colleagues in Prague and the US. Able to work full-time on-site at our Prague lab. Bonus Points, But Not Essential Hand and body pose tracking, or egocentric video. Depth sensors, point clouds or 3D reconstruction. Experience with IMU and sensor fusion. Visual SLAM, VGGT and any other modern NN-based methods in computer vision. Hands-on hardware: you have integrated sensors on a real robot or product prototype. Image processing pipeline: from raw sensor data to .jpg. ROS 2. OpenCV, numpy, scipy, pandas/Polars. Vision-language-action or foundation models. Publications in computer vision, ML or robotics. What This Role Is Not This is not a research-only role. Success means models that work on the robot, and getting them there is part of your job. This is not a benchmark role. You will work with real cameras, real lighting and messy recordings every day. This is not a junior or internship position. We are looking for someone who can own a perception problem from the data to the robot. What You'll Get Out Of It The chance to build the eyes of a humanoid robot, trained on REVEL's own recordings of skilled human work. Data most computer vision engineers never get: multi-camera recordings of real manual work, together with what the Neural Gambit wearable captures. Your models run on robots in the same lab where you work. Real ownership of the perception stack, and room to take on broader responsibility as the team grows. Why REVEL The Team: Colleagues from NVIDIA, SpaceX and Neura Robotics, in a small team with short paths to decisions. Real Technology: You see the robots in the lab every day, not just in a pitch deck. A Fast-Growing US Startup: Founded in 2025 and building its team in the Czech Republic. What we offer Competitive compensation based on experience. Unlimited Paid Time Off: Real flexibility to take time away when you need it. We trust our people to own their work, their time and their results. Lunch, On Us: Complimentary lunch every working day, plus coffee, snacks and drinks whenever you …

items.desc: About Us Albs is an AI research lab building real-time multimodal intelligence for machines, enabling them to see, hear, reason, and interact. We treat model architecture, inference, and runtime as one system. Our purpose-built models and optimized runtimes unlock the full potential of each device within defined limits for hardware cost, power consumption, and response time. Companies can adapt our technology to their own machines without building the underlying AI from scratch. We founded Albs at the intersection of LLM architecture research and on-device engineering, and we are currently in stealth, but well funded, with dedicated compute for large-scale training and experimentation. Publishing is a core part of our research culture, and we contribute our work to top venues. We share more details about the company, the team and our backing in the first conversation. Who we're looking for This is a Staff / Senior IC role. We are looking for experienced researchers and engineers, typically with several years of research or industry experience or an equivalent track record. The exact scope of each role depends on your background: some people go deep on one part of the stack, others shape the technical direction of a whole area. We agree on scope together with you during the interview process. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, age, ethnic origin, religion, disability or sexual orientation. What you'll work on Build the data platform behind our models: ingestion, storage and processing for pre-training, post-training and evaluation. For small on-device models, data quality is one of the biggest levers on model quality. Build and scale pipelines for petabyte-scale text corpora: crawling, extraction, deduplication, model-based quality filtering and decontamination against our benchmarks. Build synthetic data and rephrasing pipelines together with the research team, and measure whether they actually help. Make data reproducible and compliant: versioning, lineage, dataset cards, licensing and PII handling, so every training run can be traced back to the exact data it saw. Keep the GPUs fed: high-throughput data loading and streaming for multi-node training, together with the pre-training team. Build dataset visualization and QA tooling so researchers can inspect, slice and compare data before they train on it. Work directly with the research team on data mixtures and ablations, and turn data hypotheses into experiments that run within days. What we're looking for You have several years of experience building large-scale data systems, in industry or research. You write strong Python, plus e.g. Rust or C++. You have run distributed data processing (Spark, Ray, Dask, Beam or similar) on terabyte to petabyte datasets, with object storage and columnar formats (Parquet, Arrow), and you know how to make it fast and cheap. You have built data pipelines for ML training, ideally for LLM pre-training, including tokenization and GPU-based filtering or scoring models. You care about data quality as much as throughput, and you write tests and monitoring for your pipelines. Bonus: experience with multimodal data, synthetic data generation, or data governance under GDPR and the EU AI Act. How We Work Together We are a small, focused team of experts. You would join early, work directly with the founders, and help shape how we build. Fast iteration, short lines of communication, and in-person discussion matter a lot to us. Our culture is built around the office in Freiburg, Germany, with a default of three days a week on site. Alternatively, you can work remotely and join us on a regular cadence. We will discuss what works best for you during the interview process. We hold ourselves to a high standard: the research must be rigorous, the understanding deep, and the product well crafted. Ideas are judged on their merit, not on who proposed them, credit belongs to the team, and no task is beneath anyone. We make ambitious bets and ship early instead of waiting for perfect conditions. Above all, we care about each other, because initiative only works when it comes with respect for the people around you. What we offer Expect a competitive base salary plus equity, and dedicated compute for your research and experiments. We give you the time and support to publish and present at top conferences, and flexibility in how you work, whether on site or remote with regular in-person visits. With flat hierarchies and short decision paths, good ideas move from discussion to experiment quickly. And yes, the coffee is excellent, and we regularly get together as a team outside of work. We go through compensation and all other details with you early in the process.

items.desc: Chi siamo Siamo una giovane azienda con una profonda esperienza nell’intelligenza artificiale e nell’analisi di dati scientifici. Sviluppiamo sistemi proprietari e brevettati di AI per l’analisi di dati spettroscopici, in particolare di risonanza magnetica nucleare, e collaboriamo con clienti internazionali su problemi scientifici e industriali complessi. Siamo un piccolo gruppo di persone altamente qualificate. Apprezziamo il pensiero intelligente, concreto e rigoroso. Crediamo nelle relazioni umane, nell’onestà intellettuale e nella libertà di svolgere un lavoro serio senza burocrazia inutile. Vogliamo costruire un’azienda ad alta densità di talento, nella quale persone capaci possano realizzare il miglior lavoro della propria carriera. Se ti riconosci in questo ambiente, continua a leggere. Il ruolo Cerchiamo una persona capace di lavorare all’intersezione tra chemiometria, chimica analitica e machine learning. Utilizzerai metodi statistici multivariati, machine learning e deep learning per estrarre informazioni chimicamente significative da dati scientifici complessi, con particolare attenzione alla spettroscopia NMR. Collaborerai con chimici, data scientist e software engineer per trasformare problemi scientifici reali in sistemi computazionali affidabili. Dovrai saper comprendere la natura del dato, scegliere un approccio quantitativo adeguato e valutare i risultati non soltanto attraverso le metriche, ma anche sulla base della loro plausibilità chimica. Non è un ruolo nel quale si addestra un modello per poi passarlo a qualcun altro. Seguirai l’intero percorso: dalla comprensione del problema e dalla preparazione dei dati fino alla ricerca sul modello, alla validazione scientifica e al suo utilizzo in produzione. Cosa farai In concreto, ti occuperai di: comprendere problemi chimici e tradurli in obiettivi quantitativi e computazionali; analizzare dati NMR e altre tipologie di dati spettroscopici o scientifici; progettare strategie di preprocessing, normalizzazione, allineamento, correzione della baseline e riduzione dimensionale; sviluppare modelli chemiometrici, statistici e di machine learning; progettare, implementare e addestrare reti neurali complesse per l’analisi di spettri e segnali scientifici; contribuire allo sviluppo di foundation model per la spettroscopia NMR; lavorare su strategie di pretraining, fine-tuning, transfer learning e apprendimento auto-supervisionato; sviluppare rappresentazioni generali di spettri, strutture molecolari e relazioni tra struttura e segnale; sperimentare con architetture neurali differenti, scegliendo quelle più adatte alla struttura dei dati e al problema scientifico; confrontare modelli neurali avanzati con approcci classici come PCA, PLS, PLS-DA, clustering, classificazione e regressione multivariata; costruire dataset di grandi dimensioni e pipeline riproducibili per l’addestramento dei modelli; definire criteri di validazione solidi dal punto di vista statistico, computazionale e chimico; analizzare interpretabilità, generalizzazione, robustezza e dominio di applicabilità dei modelli; individuare errori, bias, fenomeni di data leakage e limiti dei dataset; curare qualità, tracciabilità e consistenza dei dati; contribuire allo sviluppo di pipeline e servizi di machine learning pronti per la produzione; ottimizzare modelli e processi di inferenza per il loro utilizzo in ambienti reali; collaborare con software engineer, ricercatori, partner scientifici e clienti; contribuire alle decisioni tecniche relative ai nostri prodotti e ai progetti realizzati per i clienti; seguire progetti in settori differenti, senza limitarti a un unico caso d’uso. Il nostro stack tecnologico Il nostro stack è in evoluzione, ma attualmente potresti lavorare con: Python; PyTorch e/o TensorFlow; scikit-learn, NumPy, SciPy e pandas; strumenti per l’elaborazione di spettri, segnali e dati chimici; strumenti per il monitoraggio degli esperimenti, il versionamento dei modelli e la gestione dei dataset; piattaforme cloud come AWS, GCP o Azure; GPU, container e strumenti backend; pipeline distribuite per l’elaborazione dei dati e l’addestramento dei modelli. Nvidia H100 e Nvidia Spark Requisiti essenziali Laurea magistrale, dottorato o esperienza equivalente in chimica, chimica analitica, chemiometria, chimica computazionale, chimica farmaceutica, fisica, machine learning scientifico o un ambito affine. Solida comprensione dei principi fondamentali della chimica e dell’analisi quantitativa dei dati. Esperienza pratica nell’applicazione di metodi chemiometrici o di machine learning a dati chimici, spettroscopici, fisici o biologici. Conoscenza dei principali metodi statistici multivariati. Solida conoscenza di Python e dell’ecosistema scientifico associato. Esperienza con PyTorch, TensorFlow o framework equivalenti. Capacità di progettare, addestrare e valutare reti neurali, oltre il semplice utilizzo di modelli preesistenti. Comprensione dei principi di rappresentazione dei dati, …

items.desc: About Us Albs is an AI research lab building real-time multimodal intelligence for machines, enabling them to see, hear, reason, and interact. We treat model architecture, inference, and runtime as one system. Our purpose-built models and optimized runtimes unlock the full potential of each device within defined limits for hardware cost, power consumption, and response time. Companies can adapt our technology to their own machines without building the underlying AI from scratch. We founded Albs at the intersection of LLM architecture research and on-device engineering, and we are currently in stealth, but well funded, with dedicated compute for large-scale training and experimentation. Publishing is a core part of our research culture, and we contribute our work to top venues. We share more details about the company, the team and our backing in the first conversation. Who we're looking for This is a Staff / Senior IC role. We are looking for experienced researchers and engineers, typically with a PhD and several years of research or industry experience or an equivalent track record. The exact scope of each role depends on your background: some people go deep on one part of the stack, others shape the technical direction of a whole area. We agree on scope together with you during the interview process. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, age, ethnic origin, religion, disability or sexual orientation. What you'll work on Work on post-training of our LLMs end to end: data curation, reward models, SFT, preference optimization, and RL methods such as GRPO. Post-train models that run on-device: on-policy distillation from larger teachers, and alignment that holds up under quantization and tight latency budgets. Build evaluations that find gaps in capability, alignment and safety, and close them through targeted research. Build high-throughput post-training and evaluation infrastructure so the whole research team can iterate quickly. Work with the speech and vision teams to bring post-training into our multimodal model without regressing text performance. Publish at top venues and help set our research agenda in post-training. What we're looking for You hold a PhD in a relevant field and have several years of research experience after it, in academia or industry, or an equivalent track record. You have post-trained LLMs at scale, with deep expertise in at least one of SFT, preference optimization, reward modeling or RL, and working knowledge of the rest. You have a strong publication record (e.g. NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR) or post-training work that shipped in a widely used model. You are highly proficient in PyTorch and write clean, well-structured research code that teammates can extend. You want your research to make it into the product, with improvements users actually notice. Bonus: experience with on-device models, personalization, or multimodal post-training. How We Work Together We are a small, focused team of experts. You would join early, work directly with the founders, and help shape how we build. Fast iteration, short lines of communication, and in-person discussion matter a lot to us. Our culture is built around the office in Freiburg, Germany, with a default of three days a week on site. Alternatively, you can work remotely and join us on a regular cadence. We will discuss what works best for you during the interview process. We hold ourselves to a high standard: the research must be rigorous, the understanding deep, and the product well crafted. Ideas are judged on their merit, not on who proposed them, credit belongs to the team, and no task is beneath anyone. We make ambitious bets and ship early instead of waiting for perfect conditions. Above all, we care about each other, because initiative only works when it comes with respect for the people around you. What we offer Expect a competitive base salary plus equity, and dedicated compute for your research and experiments. We give you the time and support to publish and present at top conferences, and flexibility in how you work, whether on site or remote with regular in-person visits. With flat hierarchies and short decision paths, good ideas move from discussion to experiment quickly. And yes, the coffee is excellent, and we regularly get together as a team outside of work. We go through compensation and all other details with you early in the process.

items.level: Machine Learning ICT4 – Machine Learning ICT5
items.desc:
Join the Computational Music Technologies team, where we build the audio intelligence behind some of Apple’s most distinctive listening experiences. We shipped AutoMix, intelligent DJ-style transitions between tracks, and the Music Understanding Framework, our on-device audio feature extraction system. We’re now building the next generation of generative audio technology, including the foundational models that will underpin a range of new experiences for music lovers and creators across Apple.
Music is our passion, and so is doing the research right: rigorous evaluation, careful attention to artist and listener trust, and a bias toward shipping. Our team sits close to partners in research and engineering across Apple, and we’re given the resources and access to large GPU clusters to enable us to pursue ambitious, foundational work.
As a Machine Learning Researcher on the team, you’ll conduct research in generative audio using diffusion or flow-matching models, with a focus on one or more of the following areas: voice generation, researching vocal and speech synthesis alongside related audio and signal processing techniques; post-training and alignment techniques to improve output quality, controllability, and adherence to human preference; and realtime generation, developing architectures and distillation methods that bring generation latency down to the point where it can run live, including few-step and streaming approaches.
Alongside this, you’ll help build the foundations that everything above depends on: evaluation methodology, benchmarking against the state of the art, and questions of attribution. You’ll run experiments at scale on our own infrastructure, work closely with engineering, product, and design partners to turn research into real listening experiences, and stay connected to the broader research community.
Is this you? If so, we’d love to hear from you.
A PhD in computer science, statistics, applied mathematics or related field
Peer-reviewed publications at venues such as ICASSP, ISMIR, Interspeech, NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML or related
Expertise in generative modelling, machine learning, music information retrieval or speech and audio processing
Industry experience of coding in Python and PyTorch or JAX
Excellent communication and presentation skills
Deep expertise in one of the following areas: audio generation and editing, post-training of diffusion models, voice synthesis
Experience integrating machine learning models into consumer-facing applications
Love of music

items.desc: Deine Mission & Herausforderungen Verantwortung für das Ergebnis am Roboter: Du treibst die Entwicklung kognitiver Robotik-Anwendungen mit Physical AI und der NeuraGym-Plattform voran. Du verantwortest das Ergebnis auf dem Roboter beim Kunden, nicht nur das Modell im Repo. Training & Fine-Tuning modernster Modelle: Du machst aus Foundation Models produktionsreife Roboterintelligenz. Dafür setzt du die komplette NeuraGym-Pipeline um, von Teleoperation und Datenannotation über Training und Simulation bis zu Deployment und Validierung, jeweils zugeschnitten auf reale Robotik-Anwendungen. Modelle performant auf den Roboter bringen: Du bringst Policies vom Checkpoint in die Echtzeit-Regelung im geschlossenen Regelkreis. Dazu gehören Distillation, Quantisierung, Action Chunking, Latenzbudgets und On-Device- bzw. Edge-Inferenz, immer unter den Taktzeit- und Zuverlässigkeitsanforderungen des Kunden. Das Gesicht von NeuraGym für unsere Kunden: Du bist der zentrale technische Ansprechpartner für Kunden, die Physical AI einführen. Du baust vertrauensvolle Beziehungen auf, verstehst ihre Anwendungen und begleitest sie vom Kickoff bis zur Übergabe. Hands-on Robotik: Du arbeitest direkt an MAiRA, MiPA, LARA und unseren humanoiden Plattformen, gemeinsam mit interdisziplinären Engineering-Teams. Deine Themen sind Endeffektoren und Werkzeugwechsler, Auswahl und Montage von Sensoren, Kalibrierung, elektrische und Feldbus-Schnittstellen sowie die mechanische Realität der Zelle. Customer Champions aufbauen: Du befähigst Schlüsselpersonen beim Kunden, ihre eigenen Kolleginnen und Kollegen zu schulen. So werden unsere Kunden eigenständig. Customer Enablement & Support: Du begleitest Nutzer beim Onboarding auf NeuraGym. Du prüfst Trainingspipelines und Skripte, erkennst Probleme in der Datenqualität, analysierst das Modellverhalten und löst hartnäckige Blocker direkt vor Ort. Bereichsübergreifende Zusammenarbeit: Du bist eine zentrale Schnittstelle zwischen dem Cloud- und dem AI-Team. Du sorgst für reibungslose Zusammenarbeit, technische Abstimmung und effiziente Problemlösung über Fachgrenzen hinweg. Evaluation & Zuverlässigkeit: Du baust Eval-Harnesses, Success-Rate-Benchmarks und Regressionstests auf. Sie entscheiden, ob eine Policy bereit für die Übergabe ist, und machen Fehlerbilder sichtbar, bevor der Kunde sie entdeckt. Feedback-Schleife für Produkt & Forschung: Du übersetzt Erfahrungen aus dem Feld und Kundeneinblicke in konkretes Feedback für die NeuraGym-Produkt-Roadmap und die NEURA Core-AI-Roadmap. Was du mitbringst Master oder Promotion in Informatik, Robotik, Elektrotechnik oder einem vergleichbaren Fach. Praktische Machine-Learning-Erfahrung in der Robotik: Du bist stark in mindestens einem der Bereiche vision-basierte Manipulation, Reinforcement/Imitation Learning oder multimodale Modelle und hast Lust, dir den Rest anzueignen. Nachweisbare Erfahrung im Fine-Tuning großer vortrainierter Modelle für Robotik oder eine andere Domäne: PEFT/LoRA und Full Fine-Tunes, Datensatz-Kuratierung, Distillation und Evaluation. Kenntnisse im offenen VLA- und Policy-Learning-Ökosystem (z. B. π0/π0.5, OpenVLA, LeRobot, Diffusion Policies) sind ein großes Plus. Sehr gute Python-Kenntnisse (C++ von Vorteil) und praktische Erfahrung mit PyTorch oder TensorFlow. Nachweisbare Erfahrung in technischen Rollen mit Kundenkontakt (z. B. Solution Engineering, Field AI Engineering, technische Beratung), auch mit mehreren Kunden parallel. Fundiertes Verständnis von Roboter-Hardware: Antriebe und Gelenkmodule, Drehmomentsensorik und Encoder, Endeffektoren, Sensorintegration, Kalibrierung, elektrische und Feldbus-Schnittstellen (z. B. EtherCAT) sowie Konzepte der funktionalen Sicherheit. Vor Ort kannst du damit ein Modellproblem von einem Maschinenproblem unterscheiden. Ausgeprägte Problemlösungskompetenz, die Fähigkeit, mehrere Projekte parallel zu steuern, sowie ein starker Umsetzungswille und hohes persönliches Engagement. Du nimmst Deployments persönlich, lässt dich von Rückschlägen nicht aufhalten und misst dich daran, was beim Kunden läuft. Du kommunizierst klar und übersetzt zwischen Forschenden, Ingenieurinnen und Ingenieuren sowie Endanwendern. Du sprichst gut Englisch und Deutsch (Niveau B2–C1). Bereitschaft zu häufigen Reisen zu Kunden und NeuraGyms (ca. 40–60 %).

items.desc: The Machine Translation and Multilingual AI team is looking for research interns to explore open problems in speech-to-speech translation: how to build models that let people talk naturally with anyone, in any language, in real time. Description Speech-to-speech translation is moving from cascaded pipelines to end-to-end models that listen, translate, and speak in a single system. Many core questions remain open. How do you translate simultaneously, before the speaker has finished? How do you keep translated speech natural and expressive? How do large multimodal models best combine speech understanding, translation, and speech generation? And how should these systems be evaluated? As an intern, you will own a focused research project on one of these questions, working closely with researchers and engineers on the team. You will have access to large-scale data and compute, and we encourage publishing results at top venues. Example Research Directions Include Streaming and simultaneous speech translation: policies for when to listen and when to speak, and the trade-off between quality and latency. Speech generation for translation: natural, expressive and prosodically appropriate output, including speech tokenizers and audio codecs. Multimodal foundation models for speech: how pre-training, fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning shape speech-to-speech ability across languages. Multilingual scaling: extending to new languages and handling code-switching and unknown source languages. Evaluation: automatic metrics and human evaluation methods that reflect real conversational experience. Responsibilities Define a research question with your mentor, review related work, and propose an approach. Design and run experiments on large-scale speech and translation models. Analyze results rigorously and share findings with the team. Write up your work, with the goal of a publication or a reusable research contribution. Preferred Qualifications Research experience in speech-to-speech or speech-to-text translation, especially end-to-end, streaming, or simultaneous approaches. Research experience in text-to-speech or speech generation, such as neural TTS, speech tokenizers, audio codecs, or expressive and multilingual synthesis. Experience training or fine-tuning large language models or multimodal (audio + text) models. Familiarity with speech and translation evaluation, such as WER, BLEU/chrF/COMET-style metrics, MOS, and human preference studies, and latency metrics. Publications at relevant venues (e.g. Interspeech, ICASSP, ACL, EMNLP, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR). Excellent spoken and written communication skills. Minimum Qualifications Currently enrolled in a PhD or Master's program in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Linguistics, or a related field. Research experience in at least one of: speech recognition, speech synthesis, machine translation, NLP, or multimodal learning. Hands-on experience with deep learning toolkits such as PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow. Strong programming skills in Python.

items.desc:
Are you passionate about pushing the boundaries of what robots can do? Amazon is looking for a creative and driven Applied Scientist to help build intelligent robotic manipulation systems powered by reinforcement learning. In this role, you will research, design, and deploy machine learning solutions that enable robots to interact with the physical world in increasingly capable ways. You will tackle complex, ambiguous problems where textbook answers don't exist, working backwards from real-world needs to invent new approaches. Your work will directly influence how automation systems learn, adapt, and perform at Amazon's scale — and you will see your research come to life on real hardware.
Key job responsibilities
- Research and develop reinforcement learning methods for robotic manipulation, advancing the state of the art in sim-to-real transfer, contact-rich control, and adaptive grasping strategies.
- Design, implement, and evaluate machine learning models and algorithms, leveraging deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow to train policies that generalize across varied manipulation tasks.
- Build and maintain production-quality code that integrates scientific prototypes into larger robotics systems, making thoughtful tradeoffs between complexity, performance, and maintainability.
- Collaborate with cross-functional engineering and science teams to define simulation requirements, validate model performance, and iterate on solutions informed by real-world hardware feedback.
- Contribute to the team's scientific roadmap by identifying new research directions, mentoring fellow scientists, and publishing results at peer-reviewed venues when appropriate.
A day in the life
You might start your morning reviewing overnight training runs, analyzing reward curves and failure modes from your latest reinforcement learning experiments. After a quick sync with robotics engineers, you shift to refining a simulation environment to close a gap you spotted between sim and real performance. In the afternoon, you pair with a teammate to design a new evaluation framework, then wrap up by drafting a short write-up of your findings to share with the broader team.
About the team
Our team sits at the intersection of machine learning research and real-world robotics, focused on teaching robots to manipulate objects with precision and adaptability. We combine reinforcement learning, physics-based simulation, and hands-on hardware validation to deliver solutions that work beyond the lab. We value intellectual curiosity, collaborative problem-solving, and a shared commitment to turning ambitious research ideas into tangible impact. If you are excited about building intelligent systems that learn from experience and operate at scale, this is the team for you.
- Master’s degree or higher in a relevant field such as Engineering, Robotics, or Machine Learning.
- A minimum of five years of industry or research experience, with PhD experience applicable.
- Strong deep learning fundamentals, including supervised and self-supervised learning techniques, and reinforcement learning, including Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), neural network architectures, policy optimization algorithms, model-based vs. model-free RL, exploration-exploitation strategies, value function methods, transfer learning, domain adaptation, sim-to-real transfer, etc.
- Strong background in robotics including autonomy and/or manipulation.
- Experience with deploying artificial neural networks on hardware platforms.
- Ability to write production-level code in modern C++.
- Ability to prototype algorithms and train deep neural networks in Python.
- Strong background in robotic manipulation, including dynamics, grasp synthesis, and trajectory optimization.
- PhD degree in Robotics, Engineering, Computer Science, Machine Learning or a similar discipline, or an equivalent amount of research experience.
- Publications at top-tier conferences (e.g., ICRA, IROS, CoRL, RSS) specifically focusing on robotic manipulation, grasping, or contact-rich RL.
- Demonstrated experience working with tactile sensing, multi-fingered robotic hands, or bimanual manipulation.

ABB offers an inspiring work environment with excellent opportunities for professional growth and long-term career development.

Company: 
Qualcomm Technologies Netherlands B.V. 
 Job Area: 
Interns Group, Interns Group > Interim Intern 
 General Summary:
 At Qualcomm AI Research, we are advancing AI to make its core capabilities – perception, reasoning, and action – ubiquitous across devices. Our mission is to make breakthroughs in fundamental AI research and scale them across industries. By bringing together some of the best minds in the field, we’re pushing the boundaries of what’s possible and shaping the future of AI.
 We have multiple positions available for our 4-month Deep Learning Research internship program.
As a Deep Learning Research Intern, you will develop, prototype, and implement new fundamental and impactful methods in one of our research areas. The internship program gives you a unique opportunity to advance the state of the art in artificial intelligence and publish at scientific conferences. You will join a team of talented and experienced researchers and engineers and become part of our collaborative and interdisciplinary environment.
 Our research areas include:
 Model Efficiency : Advancing efficiency of generative models and architectures with innovations in, e.g., model quantization, compression, sparsity, conditional computation (e.g., mixture of experts), application to LLMs/LVMs/multi-modal models.
 Generative Vision : Research on efficient generative modeling of visual and multimodal data using diffusion, flow-matching, autoregressive methods, Gaussian Splatting, VLMs, and MLLMs.
 Agentic AI & Reasoning : Research on agentic AI system and algorithms, long horizon planning, inference time compute, RL training of reasoning LLMs, generative reward models and LLM sampling techniques.
 Embodied AI : Research on manipulation (Vision-Language-Action models, diffusion), loco-manipulation on humanoid robots, learning-from-human-videos, and reinforcement learning applied to these topics.
 Robustness & Alignment : Research on robust & efficient methods to align models for safe, reliable, and resource-constrained edge, emphasizing controllable generation, uncertainty quantification, guardrails and on-device adaptation techniques.
 Requirements
 We welcome applications from motivated PhD candidates. Applicants must be enrolled in their PhD degree program for the duration of the internship. Ideal applicants are currently pursuing a PhD with focus on machine learning, artificial intelligence, computer vision, or foundation models (LLMs/LVMs) and have proven research ability, e.g., having published at relevant academic conferences (NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV etc.).
 Why join us
 At Qualcomm AI Research, you will be part of a team with a wide range of backgrounds that values innovation and creativity. You will be part of a global company (headquartered in San Diego) and work closely with exceptional researchers and engineers that publish at major conferences.
You will work on-site at our office located at the campus of the University of Amsterdam and live in a scenic, vibrant city with high living standards, numerous cultural activities, and plenty of green spaces.
Qualcomm offers interns flexible start dates between November 2026 and July 2027, a competitive salary, relocation assistance, and holiday & sick pay.

Our R&D and engineering facilities are in Prague, Czech Republic. This role is on-site with our engineering team in the Czech Republic. items.desc: Description Are you passionate about pushing the boundaries of what robots can do? Amazon is looking for a creative and driven Applied Scientist to help build intelligent robotic manipulation systems powered by reinforcement learning. In this role, you will research, design, and deploy machine learning solutions that enable robots to interact with the physical world in increasingly capable ways. You will tackle complex, ambiguous problems where textbook answers don't exist, working backwards from real-world needs to invent new approaches. Your work will directly influence how automation systems learn, adapt, and perform at Amazon's scale — and you will see your research come to life on real hardware. Key job responsibilities Research and develop reinforcement learning methods for robotic manipulation, advancing the state of the art in sim-to-real transfer, contact-rich control, and adaptive grasping strategies. Design, implement, and evaluate machine learning models and algorithms, leveraging deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow to train policies that generalize across varied manipulation tasks. Build and maintain production-quality code that integrates scientific prototypes into larger robotics systems, making thoughtful tradeoffs between complexity, performance, and maintainability. Collaborate with cross-functional engineering and science teams to define simulation requirements, validate model performance, and iterate on solutions informed by real-world hardware feedback. Contribute to the team's scientific roadmap by identifying new research directions, mentoring fellow scientists, and publishing results at peer-reviewed venues when appropriate. A day in the life You might start your morning reviewing overnight training runs, analyzing reward curves and failure modes from your latest reinforcement learning experiments. After a quick sync with robotics engineers, you shift to refining a simulation environment to close a gap you spotted between sim and real performance. In the afternoon, you pair with a teammate to design a new evaluation framework, then wrap up by drafting a short write-up of your findings to share with the broader team. About The Team Our team sits at the intersection of machine learning research and real-world robotics, focused on teaching robots to manipulate objects with precision and adaptability. We combine reinforcement learning, physics-based simulation, and hands-on hardware validation to deliver solutions that work beyond the lab. We value intellectual curiosity, collaborative problem-solving, and a shared commitment to turning ambitious research ideas into tangible impact. If you are excited about building intelligent systems that learn from experience and operate at scale, this is the team for you. Basic Qualifications Master’s degree or higher in a relevant field such as Engineering, Robotics, or Machine Learning. A minimum of five years of industry or research experience, with PhD experience applicable. Strong deep learning fundamentals, including supervised and self-supervised learning techniques, and reinforcement learning, including Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), neural network architectures, policy optimization algorithms, model-based vs. model-free RL, exploration-exploitation strategies, value function methods, transfer learning, domain adaptation, sim-to-real transfer, etc. Strong background in robotics including autonomy and/or manipulation. Experience with deploying artificial neural networks on hardware platforms. Ability to write production-level code in modern C++. Ability to prototype algorithms and train deep neural networks in Python. Strong background in robotic manipulation, including dynamics, grasp synthesis, and trajectory optimization. Preferred Qualifications PhD degree in Robotics, Engineering, Computer Science, Machine Learning or a similar discipline, or an equivalent amount of research experience. Publications at top-tier conferences (e.g., ICRA, IROS, CoRL, RSS) specifically focusing on robotic manipulation, grasping, or contact-rich RL. Demonstrated experience working with tactile sensing, multi-fingered robotic hands, or bimanual manipulation. Amazon is an equal opportunities employer. items.desc:
Location 
ESRIN, Frascati, Italy 
 Our team and mission 
 You will be part of the ESA Φ-lab. Our mission is to accelerate the future of Earth Observation (EO) by embracing disruptive innovation and being the catalyst for disruptive/transformative innovation in the sector.
 Our vision is to become an “EO innovation hub” connecting EO with a growing ecosystem of disruptive and transformative innovation like AI, ML, Quantum Computing, Edge Computing, Metamaterials, Photonics, etc. Many of the challenges posed by new technologies still need to be tackled at scientific, application and capability levels to deliver the maximum value from satellite-derived EO assets for our climate, society, and economy. The Φ-lab will bring together early career and senior researchers from a variety of disciplines across EO and disruptive/transformative innovation to contribute to developing innovative EO solutions.
 We offer:
 a stimulating multinational, interdisciplinary and open work environment;
 access to high-performance computing infrastructure and unparalleled EO and technology expertise;
 a unique opportunity to work on innovative solutions to address global challenges;
 freedom and focus to conduct creative research while making an impact in relation to ESA’s strategy;
 a wide network of relationships and collaboration with top academia, industry and research centres;
 the opportunity to contribute to the Φ-lab strategy and activities.
 Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int 
 Field(s) of activity for the internship 
 Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming Earth Observation (EO) by enabling the extraction of actionable insights from vast and complex datasets. ESA’s Φ-lab is at the forefront of this transformation through its active exploration of cutting-edge AI4EO technologies, spanning application-specific AI models, generative models, foundation models, and autonomous AI agents, with applications ranging from ground-based analytics to onboard satellite payload data processing (i.e., edge computing). 
 You can choose among the following topics: 
 1) Topic 1: AI for Earth Observation 
 As part of this internship, you will actively engage with Φ-lab researchers, staff, and Visiting Researchers and support a set of Φ-lab AI4EO research activities, including Geospatial Foundation Models (GFMs) for EO. 
You’ll gain hands-on experience across a number of steps of the AI development cycle: from EO data preparation and model training to benchmarking and testing of developed models. 
 Tasks may include: 
 preparing EO datasets for AI pipelines;
 training and benchmarking AI models for EO applications;
 supporting AI design and optimisation;
 supporting the ideation, preparation, and hosting of Φ-lab Challenges related to AI4EO.
 2) Topic 2: Agentic AI for Earth Observation 
 As part of this internship, you will develop and evaluate agentic AI for Earth Observation, contributing to research on how agents discover and access EO resources, plan and execute multi-step workflows, interact with external tools, and produce results that are scientifically grounded. 
 Tasks may include: 
 designing agentic workflows that decompose high-level EO objectives into sequences of analysis and processing steps;
 integrating EO tools and data services into agentic systems — data discovery, retrieval, processing, and interaction with specialised models;
 investigating reasoning, planning, and tool-use strategies that let agents adapt workflows to intermediate results and resource availability;
 building and testing prototype EO assistants, combining language models, geospatial foundation models, scientific models, and external tools as needed;
 benchmarking agentic systems on task completion, tool selection, reliability, efficiency, robustness, and scientific correctness;
 contributing to analysis, technical documentation, and scientific dissemination of results.
 You will gain hands-on experience in agent design, tool integration, scientific workflow automation, and evaluation for geospatial applications — and develop a working understanding of what it takes to make autonomous AI systems reliable, transparent, and scientifically trustworthy in Earth Observation.

 You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

items.desc: Your next mission Train the intelligence behind our radars – turning complex signal data into instant, real-world detection. You work side-by-side with AI, Software Engineering, Hardware, and Product Management colleagues – translating abstract radar signal modalities into models that spot small airborne objects in noisy environments. Test model robustness under diverse field conditions and document design choices clearly. Our radars and software protect military sites, borders and critical infrastructure from drone threats, and also help prevent bird strikes in aviation and reduce the impact of wind farms on wildlife. Our work shows up at defence and security sites, airports and wind farms around the world. We're one of the top 10 fastest-growing companies in the Netherlands, with a crew of bright minds across 30+ nationalities. items.desc:
Company: 
Qualcomm France S.A.R.L. 
 Job Area: 
Interns Group, Interns Group > Interim Intern 
 General Summary:
 Opportunity Overview: 
Join our Compiler Labs team in Strasbourg, France, for an internship focused on compiler and runtime techniques for efficient Generative AI inference on modern AI accelerators.
 Generative AI models increasingly require sophisticated optimization to achieve high performance within the compute, memory, and power constraints of edge devices. Traditional ML compilation approaches typically
 decompose a model into individual operators and optimize or schedule them separately. An alternative approach is to optimize larger portions of the model jointly, enabling more coordinated decisions about computation, data
 movement, memory usage, and hardware resources.
 During this internship, you will investigate compiler and performance-optimization techniques for these larger-scale, highly optimized execution models. Depending on your background and the direction of the project,
 the work may involve automatic exploration of optimization strategies, compiler-driven code generation, intermediate representations, memory planning, or performance analysis.
 Representative Projects: 
 Explore automatic optimization and auto-tuning techniques for high-performance AI kernels.
 Investigate compiler techniques for generating and optimizing specialized implementations from model or intermediate representations.
 Develop profiling-guided approaches for evaluating and selecting alternative implementation strategies.
 Explore efficient management and reuse of on-chip memory using compiler analysis of tensor lifetimes and data dependencies.
 Analyze the interaction between computation scheduling, data movement, memory usage, and model structure.
 Evaluate new optimization techniques on representative Generative AI workloads and accelerator architectures.
 Develop experimental compiler or performance-analysis infrastructure to guide future optimization work.
 The exact research direction will be selected according to the candidate's background and interests, together with the technical opportunities available at the beginning of the internship.
 Toolchain & Environment 
 The internship may involve technologies such as:
 C++ and Python
 LLVM and MLIR
 PyTorch and related model representations
 AI accelerator programming and toolchains
 Performance profiling and benchmarking tools
 Compiler optimization and code-generation infrastructure
 Candidate Profile 
 We are looking for a student in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field with a strong interest in some combination of:
 Compilers and program optimization
 Machine learning systems
 High-performance computing
 Parallel programming
 Computer architecture
 Generative AI and Large Language Model inference
 Experience with C++, Python, LLVM/MLIR, GPU or accelerator programming, or ML frameworks is valuable, but experience in all of these areas is not required.
The ideal candidate is curious, comfortable investigating open-ended technical problems, and interested in understanding the interaction between machine-learning workloads, compiler transformations, memory systems, and hardware execution.
 What You Will Gain 
 Hands-on experience with compiler and performance-engineering problems for modern Generative AI workloads.
 Exposure to intermediate representations, code generation, accelerator execution, and quantitative performance analysis.
 The opportunity to build and evaluate a focused research prototype within an experienced compiler team.
 Experience translating experimental results into practical engineering recommendations.

items.desc: A propos de Pasqal Pasqal conçoit et développe des processeurs quantiques (QPUs : Quantum Processing Units) et les outils logiciels associés. Notre technologie innovante permet de traiter des cas d’usage qui sont à ce jour hors de portée des plus puissants des supercalculateurs ; ces cas peuvent concerner des défis industriels applicatifs aussi bien que les besoins des sciences fondamentales. Au-delà de la puissance de calcul exceptionnelle qu’ils apportent, les QPUs sont d’une très grande efficacité énergétique et contribueront à réduire fortement l’empreinte carbone de l’industrie du calcul intensif. Description Du Poste Dans le cadre de notre forte croissance, nous recrutons un AI scientist - Quantum system performance optimization pour renforcer notre équipe Systems Performance. Au sein de l’équipe System Performance, nous mesurons et optimisons les performances des QPU. Nous sommes responsables de l’implémentation et de la validation de nouvelles fonctionnalités, et nous travaillons à pousser le système à son plus haut niveau de performance. Nous ouvrons un poste dans l’équipe afin de démarrer une nouvelle activité d’amélioration des performances atomiques des QPUs basée sur l’utilisation d’algorithmes d’IA. Dans Ce Cadre, Vos Missions Principales Seront Contribuer à des projets transverses à l’échelle du QPU Collaborer étroitement avec les membres de l’équipe pour comprendre les processus physiques en jeu Comprendre les données atomiques prises sur les QPUs et l’impact des paramètres expérimentaux Analyser les performances (via le développement de modèles mathématiques et physiques simples, ainsi que de simulations) afin d’identifier les limitations majeures des designs actuels S’approprier les problématiques de performance et de réglage des QPU afin de proposer, développer et valider de nouvelles approches s’appuyant sur les méthodes d’IA existantes Contribuer à la mise en place de maintenance prédictive sur nos QPUs Collaborer étroitement avec les experts métiers d’autres équipes du département hardware Communiquer les résultats scientifiques au sein de l’équipe et à l’extérieur A propos de vous M2 en science des données / machine learning / IA ou utilisation approfondie de méthodes d’IA pendant un doctorat de physique Bonne maîtrise des principales méthodes de Machine Learning (régression, classification, clustering, réduction de dimension) et des architectures de Deep Learning (MLP, CNN, Transformers, autoencodeurs), ainsi que de leurs domaines d'application. Expérience pratique du développement et de l'entraînement de modèles de bout en bout : préparation des données, constitution des jeux d'entraînement/validation/test, entraînement sur GPU (PyTorch, JAX ou autre framework équivalent), optimisation des hyperparamètres, adaptation des architectures et losses, évaluation et analyse des performances. L'expérience du calcul distribué et de SLURM est un plus. Capacité à adapter les modèles ML aux contraintes de systèmes expérimentaux : données bruitées ou limitées, robustesse, latence d'inférence et intégration dans des pipelines de traitement et de contrôle. Toute connaissance sur l’accélération / compression de modèles est un plus Des connaissances en physique expérimentale sont appréciées mais non indispensables : curiosité et adaptabilité les remplaceront ! Avoir déjà implémenté un ou des modèles sur un système expérimental Être à l’aise dans (ou attiré par) un cadre expérimental : bricoleurs bienvenus ! Être à l’aise avec les outils de développements (Linux, git, ssh…) Qualités attendues Autonomie, rigueur et sens de l’organisation Bonnes capacités de communication et d’écoute Capacité démontrée à collaborer avec des experts métiers Être motivé pour défricher un nouveau sujet : vous seriez le premier de l’équipe sur cette thématique! Vous avez un bon niveau d’anglais à l’écrit comme à l’oral, et un niveau de français suffisant pour évoluer au quotidien, avec une volonté de progresser. Nous nous engageons à créer un lieu de travail diversifié et inclusif, car l'inclusion et la diversité sont essentielles à la réalisation de notre mission. items.desc: Your next mission Train the intelligence behind our radars – turning complex signal data into instant, real-world detection. As our Deep Learning Engineer, you develop, optimize, and deploy neural networks that enhance real-time radar performance. You work side-by-side with AI, Software Engineering, Hardware, and Product Management colleagues – translating abstract radar signal modalities into models that spot small airborne objects in noisy environments. You report to the Team Lead AI, and your models directly safeguard critical sites around the globe. What You'll Do Model design and architecture: Design, train, and optimize deep learning models for detection, segmentation, and classification. Tailor neural networks to process abstract, non-natural 3D, 4D, and 5D radar imagery. Target classification and tracking: Build advanced neural network architectures to detect and track small objects like birds and drones. Ensure models perform reliably despite real-world background noise and weather. Data engineering and automation: Prepare, preprocess, and augment large-scale radar datasets for training pipelines. Implement automated labeling strategies to streamline data preparation at scale. Edge optimization and deployment: Optimize trained neural networks for high-performance inference on edge computing hardware. Collaborate with Software Developers and Radar Specialists to integrate models seamlessly into production systems. Research and field validation: Evaluate emerging deep learning techniques to continuously lift our radar capabilities. Test model robustness under diverse field conditions and document design choices clearly. Our radars and software protect military sites, borders and critical infrastructure from drone threats, and also help prevent bird strikes in aviation and reduce the impact of wind farms on wildlife. Our work shows up at defence and security sites, airports and wind farms around the world. Growth doesn't mean we lose the plot – eyes on the skies, feet on the ground. Our values keep us grounded: WE TRUST. WE OWN IT. WE AIM HIGH. items.desc: À propos de nous Grande École du Numérique créée en 1936, l’Efrei est un acteur indépendant majeur de l’enseignement supérieur et de la transformation numérique. Installée à Paris ainsi qu’à Bordeaux, l’Efrei forme 6 000 étudiants dans son programme Grande École d’ingénieurs et dans ses Programmes Experts du numérique (bachelors, mastères…), et propose également une offre de formation continue. Rejoindre l’Efrei, c’est bien plus que rejoindre simplement un leader de l’enseignement supérieur de premier plan, c’est vouloir s’engager dans un projet pédagogique et humain centré sur les étudiants, avec l’assurance d’avoir les moyens de ses ambitions tout en vivant dans un cadre professionnel exceptionnel au sein de nos campus. Leader indépendant reconnu d’intérêt public par l’État (EESPIG), l’Efrei est habilitée par la Commission des titres d’ingénieurs (CTI) et fait partie de la Conférence des Grandes Écoles. Depuis janvier 2022, l’Efrei est établissement composante de Paris Panthéon-Assas Université. Mission Au sein de l' Efrei Research Lab , le/la doctorant(e) participera à un projet de recherche consacré au développement d'une architecture d' intelligence artificielle agentique appliquée à l'apprentissage fédéré médical , avec pour enjeux la personnalisation des modèles et la préservation de la confidentialité des données de santé. Introduction et objet de la thèse Les établissements de santé se distinguent par le volume et la répartition de leurs données, leurs équipements ainsi que leurs ressources de calcul et de communication. Certaines maladies graves, telles que le mélanome et le cancer du foie, restent rares dans certains établissements. Pour y remédier, le partage des données est essentiel afin de favoriser une prise de décision éclairée. Toutefois, les données de santé étant sensibles et confidentielles, leur partage nécessite des solutions garantissant la protection de la confidentialité, telles que l'apprentissage fédéré. L'objectif de cette thèse est de développer une architecture d'intelligence artificielle agentique pour une fédération médicale , en s'appuyant sur les travaux déjà réalisés par l'équipe de recherche. Il s'agira notamment de proposer une méthode de personnalisation par distillation adaptative , guidée par la fiabilité du modèle pour chaque classe. Un agent d'exécution devra, à chaque cycle d'apprentissage, sélectionner les participants, adapter la personnalisation des modèles et les mécanismes de protection des échanges, puis choisir une méthode de compression compatible avec les ressources disponibles. Résultats attendus La thèse débutera par un approfondissement de l'état de l'art, comprenant une étude détaillée de la personnalisation fédérée, des agents d'exécution en apprentissage fédéré, des mécanismes de protection de la confidentialité et de la compression des mises à jour. Cette première étape sera suivie par la définition d'un cadre conceptuel permettant de structurer les décisions de l'agent. De premiers cas d'usage seront ensuite proposés afin de valider la faisabilité de l'approche. Compétences acquises à l'issue de la thèse Analyser les problématiques de recherche liées à la préservation de la confidentialité dans un environnement collaboratif d'aide à la décision. Proposer des approches adaptées aux problématiques étudiées. Conceptualiser, implémenter et évaluer les approches proposées, identifier leurs limites et définir de futures pistes de recherche. Profil Diplômé(e) d’une école d’ingénieurs ou titulaire d’un Master 2 (ou diplôme équivalent) en informatique, cybersécurité, cryptographie ou intelligence artificielle , vous souhaitez vous engager dans un projet de recherche ambitieux. Une première expérience ou des connaissances dans les domaines suivants seront particulièrement appréciées : Systèmes distribués et intelligence artificielle distribuée ; Programmation en Java et Python ; Développement sur des environnements Cloud et Edge Computing ; Probabilités, statistiques et optimisation. Vous maîtrisez l’ anglais scientifique , notamment à l’écrit et en lecture, et démontrez un réel intérêt pour la recherche, l’expérimentation et la valorisation scientifique des travaux menés. L’Efrei est engagée en faveur de l’égalité des chances et encourage les candidatures de personnes en situation de handicap. Tous nos postes sont ouverts à tous les talents.
