items.desc: Description How does Amazon decide which fulfillment center ships your order, which truck carries it, and how to keep promises across hundreds of millions of packages daily? How does it decide how many trucks and how much labor are required to ship orders across the network? SCOT Fulfillment Optimization (FO) owns the optimization and forecasting science behind these decisions. We are seeking Applied Scientists to join the FO Science & Tech team in Barcelona (alternatively: Luxembourg or London) with a strong academic background in optimization, machine learning, and/or time-series forecasting. You will design and build state-of-the-art machine learning and optimization models that power Amazon's fulfillment decisions at an unprecedented scale across two core scientific pillars: Large-Scale Optimization and Planning: Designing planning systems for order assignment and resource utilization, while balancing multi-objective cost-speed tradeoffs to enable controllers to steer millions of shipments per hour optimally. Demand Forecasting & Predictive ML: Developing time-series forecasts for customer demand, incorporating contextual information (weather, sales, order properties), and modeling uncertainty for core planning systems. Basic Qualifications PhD in Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field (or equivalent experience) Strong programming skills (Python preferred; experience with optimization solvers a plus) Research experience in one or more: Large-scale mathematical programming (LP, MIP, decomposition methods) Combinatorial optimization (assignment, scheduling, network flows) Multi-objective optimization and control Large-scale time-series forecasting (GenAI models, probabilistic forecasting, uncertainty quantification) Causal inference (spatiotemporal causal modeling, offline policy evaluation) Preferred Qualifications Experience building optimization systems that run in production at scale Being comfortable with ambiguity and fast iteration cycles Publications in relevant venues Key job responsibilities Design and implement optimization and forecasting models for large-scale fulfillment problems, from order assignment to network flow control. Build research prototypes end-to-end: from problem formulation through scalable implementation to production validation. Analyse complex tradeoffs (cost, speed, capacity, accuracy) and translate findings into actionable recommendations for leadership and operations teams. Collaborate with engineers to bring science solutions into production systems serving millions of customer orders daily. A day in the life You formulate an optimization or forecasting problem on a whiteboard with teammates, then prototype it in Python with real data by the afternoon. You run experiments against production-scale datasets, iterate on the model, and present results to stakeholders who will use them to make network decisions next week. Some days you dive deep into solver performance; other days you're explaining a Pareto frontier to an operations leader. You collaborate with large engineering and product teams to bring your solutions into systems serving millions of customers. Alongside fast-turnaround prototypes, you own long-term research bets, the kind that reshape how Amazon's fulfillment network operates at scale. Your work goes live. We decide how orders get assigned to warehouses, how capacity is allocated across the network, and how cost and speed tradeoffs are managed in real time, at global scale. Our models influence billions of euros in annual operational spend. They protect sites from overload during peak, reduce transportation costs and CO2 emissions, and ensure customers receive their packages when promised. Leadership relies on our science to make investment decisions worth hundreds of millions. We are practitioners of large-scale optimization: MIP formulations, decomposition methods, approximation algorithms, and parallelisation. We use machine learning where it sharpens our decisions, including forecasting, learned heuristics, and multi-armed bandits. We pick the right tool for the problem, not the fashionable one. You will work alongside Senior and Principal scientists, and collaborate with Amazon Scholars and academic partners who bring frontier research into our applied problems. We code our prototypes to be production-ready and collaborate with large engineering teams to ship systems, not papers. Above all, we have fun solving hard real-world problems at real-world speed, failing, learning, and shipping along the way. items.desc: Join QuTwo, a European AI lab for the quantum era, on our quest to bridge classical AI and quantum computing systems. A trained model is only half the story. The other half is making it run fast, lean and reliably on the hardware where it actually has to live. As an ML Engineer you will take models from our research team and clients and turn them into efficient, production-ready systems. You will join a small team that cares about every millisecond and megabyte. If you are a humble learner, curious about what sits beneath the framework, we encourage you to apply. Role Description You will sit where research becomes something people can use. You take trained models from our researchers and clients and make them run within real memory, latency and hardware limits, all the way to deployment in client environments and in QuTwo OS, the intelligence layer for industrial AI. You will work closely with our researchers, engineers, and client teams in a fast-moving environment, taking initiative to bring research into production. Qualifications Model compression in practice. You have applied quantisation, pruning and knowledge distillation to real models, and know how to recover accuracy afterwards through fine-tuning, retraining or other healing methods. Profiling, not just benchmarking. You can find where a model spends its memory, bandwidth and compute, and turn that into concrete optimisation decisions. Hardware-aware optimisation. You have optimised models for specific accelerators such as GPUs, NPUs or TPUs, and understand the trade-offs that come with each. Open-weight models. You are fluent with today's open-weight model families and the tooling around them. Domain adaptation harnesses. You have built the scaffolding that makes a general model useful in a specific domain, such as retrieval pipelines, tool integrations, structured prompting or agent loops, and know when that beats fine-tuning. Python and C/C++. Python to work with research code and model artefacts; C/C++ for low-level optimisation where Python overhead is not an option. Industry experience. Several years of hands-on work shipping models to production, in industry or in an applied research lab Comfort with change. You enjoy switching between projects and hardware stacks, and you take ownership from first idea to final deployment. Experience in one or more of the following areas is a plus but not a requirement: Custom kernel development with CUDA, Triton, HIP/ROCm or Metal On-device and edge ML, for example on NVIDIA Jetson, mobile SoCs or embedded hardware Optimising concurrency, parallel execution and memory bandwidth for efficient inference Model serving and deployment at scale Generating synthetic data to fine-tune or heal compressed models

Role Overview As a Member of Technical Staff, Infrastructure in Harvey Research, you’ll build the systems that power how we adapt and improve leading open-weight models for legal work. We recently post-trained our first model built for legal work, and we’re now building the team to scale up our post-training efforts. You’ll own the infrastructure behind that effort: distributed training, RL rollout systems, the environments where models learn to use tools and complete complex legal workflows, and the internal systems the team uses to manage data, run evals, and launch and track training jobs. You’ll help decide what we build, what we adopt, and how the pieces fit together. You’ll join a small, high-bar team of hands-on engineers and researchers, where each person owns a large part of the stack. We’re looking for research engineers who have built demanding ML or distributed systems, can debug across the stack, and want to work closely with researchers to make training faster, more reliable, and easier to iterate on. Learn more about our work at harvey.ai/research. What You'll Do Scale our post-training stack, supporting SFT and RL on leading open-weight models. Build distributed rollout infrastructure that coordinates model inference, tool execution, and collection of training experience for long-horizon tasks. Build the infrastructure for reproducible agent environments where models can interact with documents, tools, and external systems during training and evaluation. Own the performance and reliability of training runs, including GPU utilization, checkpointing, failure recovery, and observability. Identify and remove bottlenecks across training and inference to shorten the path from research idea to useful result. Integrate models into production, including serving, latency, cost, and online evaluation, so research reaches customers quickly and safely. Partner closely with researchers to turn experimental workflows into dependable systems while keeping room for rapid experimentation. Practical judgment about what to build versus adopt, and the ability to partner with researchers and ship quickly as needs evolve. We are hiring for this role across multiple levels. items.desc:
TomTom is a global leader in navigation, mapping, and traffic information. Join our dynamic team and vibrant culture to contribute to shaping the future of location technology.

We are looking for an Applied Scientist to shape how AI understands and uses TomTom's location data. You'll develop machine learning models and design the systems that let LLMs reason accurately over maps, traffic, points of interest and routing. You'll turn open-ended product questions into well-defined scientific problems, validate solutions with rigorous evaluation, and work with AI and software engineers to bring them to production.

What you'll do: :
LLM–data interfaces: Research and design how LLMs access and reason over TomTom's data. This covers retrieval strategies for structured and geospatial data, tool and API designs that LLMs can use reliably, text-to-query approaches, and grounding techniques. 
 Data representation: Develop representations that make location data usable by AI, such as embeddings for geospatial entities, knowledge graphs and structured context formats. 
 Evaluation science: Define how we measure whether LLM-powered systems are right. Build benchmarks, factuality and hallucination metrics, and evaluation datasets for location-grounded tasks, and work with engineers to automate them. 
 Model research and development: Design, train and fine-tune ML and deep learning models, including LLMs, computer vision, time-series and graph-based methods, using large-scale, multi-modal data. 
 Problem framing: Work with product managers and stakeholders to identify high-impact opportunities and turn them into well-defined scientific problems with clear success metrics. 
 Research to production: Write production-quality code and work with AI and software engineers to take solutions from prototype to production, balancing accuracy, latency, cost and scalability. 
 State of the art: Keep up with the latest research in LLMs, retrieval and agentic systems, and adapt promising techniques to TomTom's problems. 
 Knowledge sharing: Communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, and help build a strong scientific culture. External publications and patents are encouraged.
What you'll need::
Bachelor’s, Master's or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, Mathematics, Physics or a related quantitative field, or equivalent professional experience. 
 Strong foundations in machine learning, deep learning, statistics and optimization. 
 Hands-on experience with modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX, and with the Python scientific stack (NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn). 
 Experience with one or more of: LLMs and generative AI, computer vision, time-series forecasting, graph neural networks, or reinforcement learning. 
 Proven ability to design experiments, define meaningful metrics and draw sound conclusions from data. 
 Experience working with large-scale datasets and distributed computing (e.g., Spark, Databricks, or cloud ML platforms on Azure, AWS or GCP). 
 Ability to write clean, maintainable code and to work with engineers toward production deployment. 
 Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical ideas to diverse audiences. 
 A track record of publications at top-tier venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, KDD) is a plus. 
 Experience with geospatial, mapping, mobility or sensor data is a plus, but not required.
What we offer 

A competitive compensation package, of course.  

Time and resources to grow and develop, including a personal development budget and paid leave for learning days, as well as paid access to e-learning resources such as O’Reilly and LinkedIn Learning. 

Time to support life outside of work, with enhanced parental leave plus paid leave to care for loved ones and volunteer in local communities.  

Work flexibility, where TomTom’ers, in agreement with their manager and team, use both the office and home to focus, collaborate, learn and socialize. It’s all about getting the best out of both worlds – we ask TomTom’ers to come to the office two days a week, and the remaining three are free to be worked in either location.

Improve your home office with a setup budget and get extra support with a monthly allowance. 

Enjoy options to work from your home country and abroad for a set number of days each year, to visit family and friends, or to simply explore the world we’re mapping.  

Take the holidays you want with a competitive holiday plan, plus an extra day off to celebrate your birthday. 

Join annual events like our  Hackathon and DevDays to bring your ideas to life with talented teammates from around the world. 

Become a part of our inclusive global culture and have the chance to collaborate with a diverse community – we have over 80 nationalities at TomTom! 

Find out more about our global benefits and enjoy additional local benefits tailored to your location.

items.desc: Are you an expert in computational multiphysics modelling looking for a new opportunity? Would you like to develop advanced modelling methods with colleagues at the forefront of their fields and create impact in international research and customer projects? VTT might be just the place for you. VTT is one of the leading applied research organisations in Europe. What unites us are curiosity, a passion for learning, and a purpose: to solve the biggest challenges of our time and turn them into sustainable growth and well-being. Our cross-disciplinary community of over 2000 brilliant minds from 55+ different nationalities focuses on creating impact through science-based innovation. In recent years, we have created ground-breaking innovations such as the world's fastest and most accurate radiation detector, a cancer-sniffing sensor device for smartphones, and a headphone set entirely made of microbial materials. Get to know us further by exploring VTT's tech & infra . We are now looking for a Research Scientist specialized in FEM to join our soft materials modelling team In this role, you will develop advanced multiscale and multiphysics models to predict moisture and heat transfer, biological deterioration, and the long-term durability of wood and other bio-based materials and composites, as well as the mechanics of polymers and bio-based composites. You will combine finite-element modelling, data-driven methods, and experimental observations to build and validate the project’s multiphysics modelling framework. Our growing and diverse team, ProperTune Soft Condensed Materials, develops advanced modelling methods at the forefront of materials science and contributes to VTT’s ProperTune concept for integrated computational materials engineering. We combine computational approaches, experimental insight, and interdisciplinary collaboration to accelerate materials development and create measurable impact. You will work with highly skilled colleagues and international partners while continuously expanding your own expertise. As a Research Scientist, you will: Develop computational models for coupled moisture transport, heat and mass transfer, fungal growth, and degradation in wood and bio-based materials, as well as constitutive models for polymers and bio-based composites Implement and validate finite-element and multiphysics and multiscale formulations using experimental datasets. Integrate model parameters derived from molecular simulations, imaging data, and laboratory observations. Calibrate models, identify parameters, and assess uncertainty to improve predictive capability. Analyse computational and experimental data and collaborate closely with experimental and machine-learning researchers. Use high-performance computing environments and develop efficient, reusable scientific workflows. Contribute to open modelling tools, scientific publications, research reports, and international project collaboration. Who we are looking for: An MSc or PhD in Computational Mechanics, Materials Science, Civil or Mechanical Engineering, Applied Physics, Computational Science, Applied Mathematics, or another relevant field. Strong expertise in finite-element modelling, computational multiphysics, and the numerical solution of coupled partial differential equations. Understanding of moisture, heat, and mass transport in porous materials. Scientific programming skills in Python or Julia; experience with C++, MATLAB, or similar tools is an advantage. Experience in model calibration, parameter identification, and uncertainty analysis. Experience with wood, bio-based materials, composites, or other heterogeneous porous materials. Good written and spoken English and the ability to collaborate effectively in multidisciplinary and international environments. Experience in multiscale modelling, physics-informed neural networks, machine learning, surrogate modelling, biological growth simulations, high-performance computing, or 3D imaging data is considered an advantage. As a person, we hope that you are: Curious, proactive, and eager to learn, with the ability to work independently while collaborating closely across disciplines. Motivated to translate scientific questions and customer needs into clear modelling objectives and practical results. Open-minded, solution-oriented, and able to move work towards concrete outcomes within clearly defined goals. With VTT, you’ll enjoy: Visionary work in technology. We offer positions at the cutting-edge of technology and engineering, from next-generation microelectronics and quantum technology to automation and robotics, energy systems, and more. Our research agenda is dedicated to creating sustainable growth by solving systemic and technological challenges, so your work will go towards creating a real, positive impact. It all starts at the top of the funnel: finding the people who aren't looking, and getting them to look. You're the front line of how Genesis wins talent. Building pipeline that converts. Map markets, build target lists, and keep healthy, calibrated pipelines moving for every active search. Hand recruiters and hiring managers candidates worth their time. Building the machine. Stand up scalable, well-organized sourcing in Ashby, and automate the parts that don't need a human (list building, enrichment, sequencing) so you spend your time on judgment and outreach. You can read a technical profile and tell signal from noise: whose papers matter, whose GitHub is real, who's actually exceptional. You write outreach that sounds like a human who did their homework, not a template. You think in systems and automation: you'd build an AI workflow than run the same manual search twice. You're a self-starter who brings structure to ambiguity and moves fast without dropping quality. You read data well, including response rates, pipeline health, and where searches stall, and you adjust. Bonus points You've sourced Research Scientists, robotics, or deep-tech engineers specifically. You've sourced across UK and France. You've used AI tooling to genuinely speed up sourcing, and have opinions about what works. You've been early at a startup and built something from zero. items.desc: About VAT Group At VAT, we change the world with vacuum solutions. As the world’s leading supplier of high-performance vacuum valves, we have been driving innovation for more than 60 years. With over 3,200 employees worldwide, we operate from our headquarters in Haag, Switzerland, with manufacturing sites in Switzerland, Malaysia and Romania, as well as sales and service hubs around the world. We guided by our passions integrity, teamwork, customer centricity, and innovation – always working together as #oneVAT. Joining us means becoming part of a passionate, international team where your voice is heard, your ideas matter, and your career growth is supported. Your Challenge: Our products are key components in semiconductor processing equipment worldwide. To support the development of intelligent vacuum systems, we are looking for an intern who wants to combine hands-on experimentation with data science and machine learning. During your internship, you will investigate gas dynamics in a vacuum process chamber using advanced sensor technologies. You will contribute to the complete development cycle, including experimental planning, data collection, preprocessing, feature engineering, time-series modelling, and model validation. Your responsibilities will include: Become familiar with vacuum technology, gas dynamics, process chambers, and sensor systems. Support the setup and execution of experiments in our vacuum test laboratory. Plan experiments using a structured Design of Experiments approach. Key responsibilities Join the assigned session at the exact date, time, and time zone provided. Discuss assigned topics naturally with the other speakers in the session. Speak regularly, respond to others, ask and answer questions, and contribute a fair share of the conversation. Follow the topic guidance and keep the discussion interactive rather than reading a script or giving a formal speech. Use natural conversational reactions, including brief overlaps and backchannels when appropriate. Candidate requirements Comfortable speaking and interacting in a group conversation. Available for the full assigned session time and time zone. Willing to speak and contribute actively; simply joining and remaining silent is not acceptable. Able to follow instructions and discuss topics naturally without using a script. Able to provide the required recording environment and microphone setup. Required microphone setup A proper external microphone with wired headphones is preferred. However, a good-quality wired headset with a built-in microphone is also acceptable if it provides clear, muffle-free audio. A basic or low-quality headset alone is not sufficient. Laptop speakers, Bluetooth earphones, or open speakers are not acceptable during recording. Use the same microphone, headphones, and device for the session which you will be using for the audio sample submission during job application. Record in a quiet room without TV, music, fan noise, traffic, pets, or other people talking. Position the microphone consistently and speak clearly at a natural volume. Avoid echo, reverb, distortion, clipping, typing, tapping, or handling the device near the microphone. items.desc: Le descriptif de l’offre ci-dessous est en Anglais Type de contrat : CDD Contrat renouvelable : Oui Niveau de diplôme exigé : Thèse ou équivalent Fonction : Ingénieur scientifique contractuel A propos du centre ou de la direction fonctionnelle The Inria research centre in Lyon is the 9th Inria research centre, formally created in January 2022. It brings together approximately 410 people in 20 research teams and research support services. Its staff are distributed in Villeurbanne, Lyon Gerland, and Saint-Etienne. The Lyon centre is active in the fields of software, distributed and high-performance computing, embedded systems, quantum computing and privacy in the digital world, but also in digital health and computational biology. Contexte et atouts du poste In the QINFO team in Lyon under the supervision of Omar Fawzi. Mission confiée We are seeking a research engineer to develop and evaluate encoding and decoding strategies for noisy quantum systems. The goal is to identify quantum error-correcting codes and practical decoding methods that protect quantum information under realistic noise models. The position combines quantum information, numerical simulation, and machine learning. Working closely with the research team, the successful candidate will build computational tools to explore candidate codes, optimize encoding strategies, and design efficient decoders. Principales activités Develop and implement methods to search for quantum error-correcting codes and encoding strategies adapted to different noise models. Design and benchmark decoding algorithms, including approaches based on machine learning. Build numerical simulations to evaluate performance under noise and assess computational cost and scalability. Implement optimization methods to improve code and decoder performance. Maintain well-documented, tested, and reproducible research software. Contribute to research discussions, technical reports, and scientific publications. Compétences A PhD in computer science, physics, applied mathematics, electrical engineering, or a related field. Strong programming skills, particularly in Python, and experience developing scientific software. A solid foundation in linear algebra, probability, and numerical optimization. Avantages Subsidized meals Partial reimbursement of public transport costs Leave: 7 weeks of annual leave + 10 extra days off due to RTT (statutory reduction in working hours) + possibility of exceptional leave (sick children, moving home, etc.) Possibility of teleworking (90 days / year) and flexible organization of working hours Social, cultural and sports events and activities Access to vocational training Social security coverage Rémunération Base of 2692€ gross / month. Wage according to the profile. L’autorisation d’accès à une zone est délivrée par le chef d’établissement, après avis ministériel favorable, tel que défini dans l’arrêté du 03 juillet 2012, relatif à la PPST. Un avis ministériel défavorable pour un poste affecté dans une ZRR aurait pour conséquence l’annulation du recrutement. Inria mène plus de 300 projets de recherche et d’innovation avec ses 3500 scientifiques, ingénieurs et personnels d’appui, en partenariat avec les universités et l’écosystème numérique (entreprises, entrepreneurs, acteurs publics). items.desc: Ever seen your code pull weeds? Here, you will. At Track32, the models you build don’t end up in a slide deck. They run on weeding machines in the field, on drones flying through greenhouses, and in the hands of growers who use them every single day. We are a small, independent AI and computer vision team, born at Wageningen University. We work with farmers, machine builders, universities and research institutes, and we love a good technical challenge. Right now we are looking for a new teammate to build it with us. Your playground Object detection and tracking, instance segmentation, 3D vision and spectral imaging Images from drones, satellites, smartphones, camera rigs, vehicles and even microscopes Signal and tabular data, and clever combinations of all of the above Taking a model from first idea to a working product, in the cloud or on a machine in the field Freedom to test new technologies and make them work Every project or product is different, and that is exactly the fun of it. You might be our person if you have experience with machine learning and deep learning, ideally in computer vision, write Python with ease and know your way around PyTorch and OpenCV, use AI assistance to be more productive, love turning messy data into insights people can act on, have a degree in AI, Computer Science, or a related field, or learned it the hard way through experience, have 2+ years of experience (or a fresh graduate with great projects to show) Bonus points for: C++, signal analysis, tabular data AI, and curiosity about agriculture and sustainability. You don’t need to know a tractor from a combine. You just need to want to learn. What’s in it for you Real impact: your work ends up in real machines, fields and greenhouses A small team with short lines, where your ideas count and you own your work 25 holiday days, pension, travel allowance Training and conference budget Room to grow, through your own projects, publications or mentoring Regular team events. We work hard, we celebrate wins together, and we make sure there is room for family, travel, workouts or whatever makes you happy Sounds like you? Let’s talk! Send your CV and a few lines about what excites you to info@track32.nl. We reply within 3 working days. After that: a casual intro call, a technical chat with the team, and a meeting with Joris (CTO) and Simon (CEO). If so, why not join us and make a difference. The Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) is an executive agency of the Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs, and works on behalf of the Scottish Government and Welsh Government. Our diverse teams of over 3,000 skilled and committed professionals come together to provide research, advice and support to UK Government for safeguarding animal, public and plant health for benefit of the environment and economy. APHA is a brilliant place to work where our people feel valued, have a voice and can be their authentic selves. We value difference and diversity, because it helps us be more innovative and make better decisions. We are dedicated to being an inclusive employer, offering equitable opportunities for all individuals. Our goal is to build a diverse workforce, and we hope to attract applications from all backgrounds and underrepresented groups. The Science Directorate (SD) delivers high quality, high impact and highly relevant multidisciplinary science. Our People are diverse, talented, engaged and inspired to deliver innovative outcomes. The Virology department is a multi-disciplinary team with a statutory remit in named reportable, endemic, notifiable and exotic diseases for the delivery of research, diagnostic services and surveillance programmes. As a research scientist within the Mammalian Virology workgroup, you will be involved with planning, managing, and delivering research and development into the pathogenesis of and immunity against RNA (ribonucleic acid) viruses in the Emerging Virus Research unit (EVRU). You will generate expertise for both inside the agency as well as for national and international stakeholders. You will support National Reference Laboratories for swine and equine viral diseases and be part of the disease emergency responses in the Virology Department. Job description Main areas of work will include: Execute research to enhance the control of veterinary viruses, specifically through understanding their pathogenesis and immunity Manage research projects; design and execute approaches for scientific investigations, ensuring completion of project objectives and milestones to the customers satisfaction; delivery of science in accord with relevant Quality Assurance standard ISO9001 and within budget Communication of science through participation in internal and external meetings, and to ensure a high-quality programme of scientific approaches published in peer reviewed literature with high impact. Support the Workgroups senior scientist team, through deputising and delegated tasks, and contribute to strategic planning Develop and seek opportunities for the initiation of (collaborative) research proposals, both nationally and internationally and draft applications for funding bodies. Maintain and enhance links across the national and international stakeholder community through provision of expertise and influencing. Provide consultancy to stakeholders such as Defra, and the Agriculture and Horticulture Development Board (AHDB) and also the industry. Liaise with APHA scientific and the Quality Assurance Unit e,g, as commentator for external quality assurance schemes Supervise and provide training for members of staff, students, and visitors in the workgroup. Manage technical knowledge relating to host-pathogen interaction mechanisms, feeding into the Virology department. Ensure that self and team maintain safe operation of the laboratory, including containment level 3 and 4 high containment laboratories, ensuring staff are aware of and adhere to appropriate safety procedures and emphasise a culture of continuous improvement in health and safety. Participate in the disease emergency response in the event of a disease outbreak and be part of the on-call rota Person specification Experience and skills: You will need to demonstrate the following: Knowledge of and practical experience with immunology, in the virology context relevant to the role Knowledge of characterising the immune response using approaches such as RNA Sequencing and/or using imaging technologies Experience of working in a research environment including experience with animal studies Good written and oral communication skills to deliver outputs such as manuscripts, presentations, funding applications and reports …

items.desc: ¡¡Buscamos a quien quiera hacer que la IA quepa en un dispositivo... y funcione de verdad!! Estarás en el equipo de Intelligence of Things, especializado en llevar la inteligencia artificial a los dispositivos edge. Los dispositivos edge son sistemas que procesan los datos allí donde se generan, en el propio producto o en la máquina, con recursos limitados de cómputo, memoria y energía. En el equipo investigamos y desarrollamos las técnicas que permiten ejecutar modelos de IA en estos dispositivos, desde la optimización y el particionado de modelos hasta su despliegue y evaluación en hardware real, y trabajamos para que cada vez más inteligencia, incluida la IA generativa, pueda integrarse y ejecutarse directamente en el borde. ¿Qué te aportaremos? Un contrato indefinido de lunes a viernes, junto con un horario flexible y con un calendario muy . Posibilidad de teletrabajar hasta 2 días a la semana e incluso un tercer día en alguna de nuestras sedes más cercanas a tu domicilio . Salario acorde a formación y experiencia (42.000 - 50.000 brutos/año). Trabajar en un entorno joven y donde se respira y se palpa la tecnología del futuro . Tener a tu disposición personas con gran conocimiento en la materia dispuestas a ayudarte en tu desarrollo . Tener a tu disposición laboratorios de primer nivel. Tus funciones serán: Desarrollar e integrar aplicaciones en C++ sobre sistemas Linux, con foco en plataformas edge y de recursos limitados. Optimizar el software y los modelos de IA, incluida la IA generativa, para que se ejecuten de forma eficiente en estos dispositivos. Adaptar, desplegar y validar modelos de IA en hardware edge. Participar en proyectos con clientes industriales, desde el desarrollo hasta la transferencia de resultados. Participar en la elaboración de propuestas de investigación y en proyectos de investigación nacionales y europeos. Documentar el trabajo técnico y contribuir a entregables, demostradores y, cuando proceda, publicaciones. Requisitos: Para disfrutar en este equipo necesitarás: Imprescindible Grado & Máster en Ingeniería Informática, Telecomunicaciones o Electrónica (o áreas afines). Experiencia en desarrollo de aplicaciones en entornos Linux. Dominio de programación en C++ y sensibilidad por el rendimiento y el uso eficiente de recursos. Conocimientos de IA (modelos, frameworks de entrenamiento e inferencia, despliegue en dispositivos). Ganas de aprender, autonomía y capacidad para trabajar en equipo. Nivel de inglés suficiente para trabajar con documentación técnica y comunicarte en entornos internacionales.

items.desc:
As a Forward Deployed Engineer II (FDE II) on the Custom Model and Optimization team, you embed directly with strategic customers to build, optimize, and run custom generative AI models in production alongside their engineering teams. You own complete model workstreams end-to-end from defining the evaluation bar and preparing data, through training and inference optimization, to production deployment. 
FDE IIs on this team works at the intersection of models and systems. They customize state-of-the-art open-weight and foundation models for new domains, languages, and modalities; migrate and optimize training and inference workloads on AWS Trainium and operate those models as production services. They are autonomous contributors who take on projects where the business goal is clear, but the path is not. They make design trade-offs with appropriate guidance, limit short-term workarounds, coach others on producing high-quality code, and train new team members. 
Key job responsibilities
Embed within customer ML and engineering teams: Understand the customer's business, data, model stack, and operational constraints. Translate ambiguous goals into a measurable evaluation bar and a technical plan for your workstream such as model selection, customization approach, and serving architecture. Requires up to 25% travel. 
Customize and post-train models. Adapt open-weight and foundation models to customer domains through continued pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, and reinforcement learning (including RLHF, RL with verifiable rewards, and multi-turn agentic RL). Build the data pipelines, synthetic data generation, and evaluation harnesses that prove a customized model out performs the baseline on the customer's own quality, latency, and cost bar. Apply these techniques to high-value patterns such as coding agents, domain foundation models, and multi-adapter serving. 
Build large-scale training and inference systems. Design and implement distributed training and RL post-training pipelines using frameworks such as PyTorch FSDP2, Megatron-LM, Miles, and verl. Build RL interaction harnesses using NeMo Gym or OpenEnv to connect agent workflows, tools, environments, and reward functions to training. Develop production inference stacks with engines such as SGLang and vLLM, and optimize throughput, latency, memory footprint, and cost per token through quantization, parallelism, speculative decoding, and batching. 
Optimize models on AWS chips. Migrate and tune training and inference workloads for AWS Trainium using the AWS Neuron SDK. Profile performance, close accuracy-parity gaps against GPU baselines, and develop custom kernels where needed. Benchmark rigorously and turn results into decisions customers can act on. 
Accelerate impact beyond the engagement. Codify reusable fine-tuning recipes, evaluation frameworks, benchmarking tools, and optimization patterns that accelerate future deployments. Feed field learnings back to AWS service teams, including Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker AI, and AWS Neuron. Identify opportunities to expand model customization and optimization within your customer engagement.

items.desc: Applied Geometry Applied Geometry is an AI research lab building biological superintelligence: AI that can make discoveries in biology and health beyond the reach of the best human research teams. Our ambition is to compress years of scientific discovery into days and transform our ability to understand and cure disease. We're training frontier models to do science across biology, drug discovery and clinical medicine. We believe the next frontier of AI requires systems that can reason from incomplete evidence, generate and test hypotheses, and pursue complex research programmes. Our Approach We're building on the methods that have driven extraordinary advances in coding and mathematics, extending them to the harder problems of biology and human health. We develop reinforcement learning environments grounded in real scientific data and expert knowledge, giving AI agents the tools to tackle consequential biomedical problems and using their performance to improve the underlying models. As these systems become more capable, we're training them to sustain coherent research over longer periods: uncovering disease mechanisms, designing experiments and developing new therapies. Our goal is to build AI researchers whose discoveries exceed what their creators could have anticipated. We've raised a large funding round from leading Silicon Valley investors to achieve this goal. What you'll do Train AI agents through reinforcement learning to solve complex, long-horizon problems in biology and scientific research. Build challenging RL environments in which agents reason over biological data, use scientific tools, generate hypotheses, design experiments, and interpret results. Develop reward functions and evaluation frameworks that distinguish genuine scientific progress from shortcuts and reward hacking. Build scalable infrastructure for agent rollouts, distributed training, and evaluation so that a small, elite team can run ambitious experiments quickly and reliably. Own the full research loop: design experiments, implement methods, diagnose failures, and turn promising results into reproducible improvements. Work closely with scientists to translate difficult biological questions into tasks with meaningful objectives and verifiable outcomes. Help define Applied Geometry’s technical stack, research standards, and engineering culture from the ground up. Contribute to our mission of building biological superintelligence to accelerate discovery and ultimately cure disease. What we're looking for High agency — You thrive in ambiguity, move fast, and take ownership of hard problems. You have strong opinions and update them when the evidence changes. Deep RL and post-training expertise — You understand reinforcement learning from first principles and have hands-on experience training models or agents. You can reason clearly about exploration, credit assignment, reward design, and training stability. Exceptional engineering ability — You can turn research ideas into reliable, performant code. You're comfortable debugging across the stack, from learning dynamics to distributed systems and GPU performance. Research judgement — You design experiments that answer important questions, identify why an approach is failing, and decide what to try next. You distinguish meaningful capability gains from benchmark artefacts. Experience building agentic systems — Ideally, you have worked on tool use, multi-step reasoning, RL environments, or training agents to complete long-horizon tasks. Scientific curiosity — You want to build intelligence that can do consequential scientific work. Prior biology experience is valuable but not required; intellectual curiosity and the ability to learn quickly are essential. What’s in it for you We want Applied Geometry to the best place in the world to do ambitious AI biology work. Early hires will receive exceptional support and significant ownership. Benefits include: Competitive, top-of-market compensation. Significant equity package to share in the upside of building a category-defining company. Comprehensive private medical & dental coverage. A significant budget to purchase best-in-class equipment, research tooling, software, and the infrastructure you need to do your best work. Access to the compute and petabytes of proprietary biomedical data required to train ambitious models. Opportunities to attend leading AI, biology, and scientific conferences - fully-funded. Regular team meals, a stocked office, and a working environment designed for elite perfotmance. Flexible time off with no strict limits. Compensation Range: £150K - £300K

items.desc: Why this role is exciting Rohlik is the leading Central European e-grocer. More than a million customers buy their groceries from us through Rohlik.cz, Knuspr.de, Kifli.hu, Gurkerl.at and Sezamo.ro, choosing from over 17,000 items, delivered within a couple of hours in 15-minute windows. We are building the autonomous grocer. Maia, our AI assistant, already talks to customers and builds their orders; agents are moving into our buying and logistics; vision models are learning to watch quality. The next frontier is physical: robots taking over more and more of the work in our fulfilment centres, until fresh food moves from producers to households at a cost nobody else can match. We are setting out to record how our own people handle groceries and to turn those recordings into a training corpus for manipulation policies. Our warehouses already log what happened on every pick and every quality check, so the recordings can carry labels most datasets never get. Making that hold is part of the job. You decide what makes an hour of footage trainable — before we bank hundreds of them. What You Will Own And Deliver The capture spec. Cameras, mounts, calibration, and what disqualifies an episode. You write it before we buy the fleet and enforce it after. When the spec and the floor disagree, you go to the floor and find out which one is wrong. Ground truth. Hand pose is the signal that transfers from human video to robot policies, and warehouse reality — work gloves, occlusion, cold halls — is exactly where the published models struggle. You own how we measure that and how we close the gap. The evaluation harness. The corpus only counts if a policy can train on it. You build the harness that decides which hours make the bank, and you hold the trainability bar as the volume grows. The first training runs. Once hours bank, you post-train open robot-learning models on our data and run the first task evaluations. Judgment before spend. The field moves monthly. You read what is published, reproduce the claims we depend on, and steer our capture before the money is spent, not after. The scope This is a seat on a small, newly created team: an operations lead who runs capture on the floor, a data engineer who owns the pipeline, and you: the machine-learning voice in the room. This is not a research-scientist role, and no publication record is required. The job is to make a corpus trainable and to train the first policies on it. What We Are Looking For PyTorch, and computer vision with real 3D geometry. Camera calibration, pose estimation, SLAM fundamentals. You have debugged an extrinsic calibration at least once in your life and know why it drifted. You can read a paper and reproduce it. Our pipeline is assembled from published work, and your job is knowing which claims survive contact with a chilled warehouse hall. You know what policies train on. Familiar with the current robot-learning stack and policy classes well enough to know what the training side will demand of the data before the data exists. Dataset instincts. You have trained on data you collected yourself, and you know the failure modes that only show up at training tim.. Comfortable as the only ML voice. You make the call, write it down, and revisit it when the pilot data says otherwise. AI is how work gets done here. Our engineers use Claude Code and Devin daily, and we expect you to direct agents for the unglamorous parts — harness code, data plumbing, reproduction scripts — while keeping the quality bar exactly where it was. Particularly relevant. Hand-pose estimation or egocentric video in production; multi-camera rigs and time sync; experience post-training robot-learning models; ROS 2. What Success Looks Like In 90 Days You have written the capture spec and we set up the first rigs against it. Your pilot gates have numbers, the first hours have passed your harness, and you can tell the people who sign the budget, with data, what the next hundred hours should look like. Are we a good fit? Take this role if you would rather own the spec that decides whether a dataset becomes an asset or a write-off than tune someone else's model on someone else's data, if a fulfilment centre at 6 a.m. sounds like a lab to you, and if you want the shortest possible line between your technical judgment and a capital decision. Read our culture code and are we a good fit?. What We Offer The physical-AI side of the autonomous grocer, with the capture spec and the first training runs yours from day one A data asset few teams in the world get to build, in fresh groceries, a domain as hard as manipulation gets Off-the-shelf hardware, a managed cloud estate, and a mandate that has already started Benefits — see what we offer Are you in? Instead of a cover letter: pick a published human-video-to-robot-policy pipeline you rate, and tell us where it breaks on a warehouse floor where every hand wears a work glove.

Today, we help clients with total transformation-inspiring complex change, enabling organizations to grow, building competitive advantage, and driving bottom-line impact. We work in a uniquely collaborative model across the firm and throughout all levels of the client organization, generating results that allow our clients to thrive. Working across industries and disciplines, we combine our experience and expertise to tackle the biggest challenges faced by society today. We go beyond what was once thought possible, creating new and innovative solutions to the world’s most complex problems. Leveraging BCG’s global network and partnerships with leading organizations, BCG X provides a stable ecosystem for talent to build game-changing businesses, products, and services from the ground up, all while growing their career. Together, we strive to create solutions that will positively impact the lives of millions. As a Forward Deployed AI Scientist and Senior Forward Deployed AI Scientist, you'll be part of our rapidly growing team. You'll have the chance to apply data science methods and analytics to real-world business situations across a variety of industries to drive significant business impact. You'll have the chance to partner with clients in a variety of BCG regions and industries, and on key topics like climate change, enabling them to design, build, and deploy new and innovative solutions. Additional responsibilities will include developing and delivering thought leadership in scientific communities and papers as well as leading conferences on behalf of BCG X. Successful candidates are intellectually curious builders who are biased toward action, scrappy, and communicative. The fisrt use case will be the reconstruction of vital signs (breathe,heart). Contract duration (months) 6 months Job Description Perceiving and analyzing the environment around us is a major challenge in many promising industrial sectors. In this context, artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms have undoubtedly demonstrated their effectiveness for tasks related to vision, with various sensors (camera, lidar, etc.). Today, there is a growing interest in the use of AI for radar sensor data (radio detection and ranging). Radar is indeed a sensor that stands out due to the nature of its data, its operability (low light, bad weather, etc.), and its cost. However, they produce sparse data with low spatial resolution, making them difficult to exploit with traditional algorithms. Recently, artificial neural networks based on a graph representation of data (Graph Neural Networks - GNN) have shown good accuracy on sparse and noisy sensor data [1]. Consequently, the use of GNN for radar data exploitation seems very promising [2]. The range of applications is wide, including intelligent vehicles (cabin monitoring), medical devices (vital sign measurements), gesture detection [3], or surveillance devices (fall detection). In a rapidly evolving context with strong industrial interest, the intern will implement and propose innovative methods for processing data from a radar sensor. They will rely on AI algorithms based on GNNs currently being developed within the laboratory. The student will be integrated into a dynamic multidisciplinary team and will benefit from upskilling in artificial neural networks. # CEA-List Methods / Means artificial intelligence, deep learning, artificial neural networks, graph neural networks, computer Applicant Profile Desired profile: Student in the final year of engineering school or Master 2 Desired skills : A strong motivation to learn and contribute to research in artificial intelligence. In-depth knowledge of computer science and programming languages (Python). Knowledge of artificial intelligence and experience with artificial neural networks (libraries Pytorch or Tensorflow) are a plus. The recruitment interview may refer to the three publications cited. Industrialisation des pipelines CI/CD Concevoir, déployer et maintenir des pipelines GitHub Actions. Implémenter les contrôles et scans de sécurité dans les chaînes de publication. Sécurité des agents IA et des infrastructures MCP Participer à la sécurisation des serveurs MCP et des registres fédérés. Within the user program more than 1000 scientists visit the MLZ every year to perform experiments in the physical, chemical, biological and materials sciences. In addition, JCNS is actively pursuing a research program in the field of soft matter science and condensed matter physics. Over the past years, AI has moved from a side experiment to something their engineering teams actively ask for: a way to read their test data
items.desc: ENGIBEX is a Belgian R&D engineering consultancy, founded fourteen years ago, with around 95 people. Most of us are engineers with a master, PhD or postdoc background, working on our clients' R&D projects in powertrain electrification, embedded software, mechanical design, simulation, test and validation. We work in two modes. Most of our engineers work on site within a client team. In a smaller number of cases, including this one, we take a work package: ENGIBEX owns a topic end to end and is accountable for the result, not just for the headcount. Whatever the mode, ENGIBEX is your employer. Your contract, your salary, your car and your career path sit with us, and they do not end with a project. 💼 Job Description The project Our client is an automotive R&D centre in Limburg, Belgium, specialised in hybrid transmissions. They design, develop and validate their own products, with their own test facilities. They are not a software company, and that is precisely the point. Over the past years, AI has moved from a side experiment to something their engineering teams actively ask for: a way to read their test data faster, to find their own documentation, to compare one programme against the history of all the others. The requests now come in faster than one person can absorb. ENGIBEX runs that AI portfolio as a long-term work package. We scope the topics with the client, build the tools, deploy them and maintain them. The team and how we work The first ENGIBEX AI engineer has been in place since mid 2026 and owns the existing tools. You will be the second. The client's R&D organisation is built on pairs: two people per discipline, so that topics can be shared, covered during absences and swapped when interests change. This role creates the second seat on the AI side. Concretely, That Means You and your colleague split the portfolio between you, based on interest and availability, and you can rotate topics over time. You report technically to the client's virtual engineering leader, on a daily basis. Your ENGIBEX business manager follows the project closely, with regular touch points, and formal project reviews with you and the client several times a year. You are not alone on an island: you have a peer on the same topics, an ENGIBEX technical network behind you, and the possibility to bring in additional ENGIBEX support when a topic needs it. What you will work on The scope grows with the demand. Today it covers three families of topics. Anomaly detection on test-bench data Transmissions are run through accelerated durability tests on dedicated test benches, instrumented with a large number of sensors. The goal is to detect a developing failure from the signals, early, while the test is still running. A model already exists and works offline on historical data. The current challenge is the step that nobody in the market seems to have taken on this kind of application: moving it online, so that it monitors a running test in real time, surfaces anomalies on a dashboard, and eventually raises alerts, without ever interfering with the test itself. That involves retraining on new transmission families, separating real anomalies from legitimate operational events, proving the accuracy to the test engineers who will rely on it, and then scaling it from one test bench to many. Internal LLM assistant The client runs an internal, retrieval-based assistant on their own technical documentation, used by several hundred engineers. It has no access to the internet and is fed entirely by internal documents. The work here is a mix of product and engineering: retrieval quality, document indexing, access management and permissions, new use cases requested by teams, deployment hygiene, and the unglamorous but decisive part, getting more people to actually use it. New AI tooling for the engineering teams This is the part that keeps growing, and where you will have the most freedom. Examples currently on the table: Comparing the requirements of a new programme against the history of past programmes, inside their requirements management platform, so that engineers stop rediscovering what was already decided. Predicting physical quantities in real time, such as component temperatures, from test or simulation data, to support calibration work. Applications around their simulation activities. You will not be handed a backlog of tickets. You scope the problem with the engineering teams, build the solution, deploy it, document it, and convince people to use it. Technical environment Language: Python, for everything. Data: sensor time series acquired with Vector CANape, stored in MF4, read in Python. Compute: an internal simulation cluster on Red Hat Linux with Slurm, plus a GPU workstation. Windows workstation with WSL for day to day work. Cloud: Azure for the LLM backbone. Reality check: the estate was built incrementally by different people over several years. Part of the job is to bring it to a proper engineering standard: a real …

items.card: Your Responsibilities Design and instrument an experimental setup for semiconductor die-bonding measurements. Acquire, synchronize, document, and preprocess machine telemetry, acoustic-emission data, and other high-frequency sensor signals. Develop machine-learning approaches for quality prediction, anomaly detection, and virtual metrology. Evaluate the robustness and generalization of sensing modalities and signal
items.desc: Facing the challenges of our time Help us grow and be more impactful! The Predictive Analytics group is offering a student project or internship to develop and validate an adaptive equipment-intelligence framework for semiconductor manufacturing using machine telemetry and high-frequency sensing. Using semiconductor die bonding as the experimental platform, the project will investigate whether acoustic emission and other sensor signals can provide robust information about equipment and process state across changing recipes and operating conditions. Machine-learning methods will be developed for: Quality prediction Anomaly detection and virtual metrology, with emphasis on generalization across recipes and operating conditions Uncertainty-aware adaptation using limited data from new process conditions The project will quantify which sensing modalities and signal representations remain informative under process changes and determine how much new data is required to adapt the monitoring system to a new operating regime. The project is intended for a minimum duration of six months and requires regular on-site work in Alpnach, Switzerland. Your Responsibilities Design and instrument an experimental setup for semiconductor die-bonding measurements. Acquire, synchronize, document, and preprocess machine telemetry, acoustic-emission data, and other high-frequency sensor signals. Develop machine-learning approaches for quality prediction, anomaly detection, and virtual metrology. Evaluate the robustness and generalization of sensing modalities and signal representations across recipes and operating conditions. Develop uncertainty-aware adaptation methods using limited data from new process conditions. Document methods and results and communicate findings to the Predictive Analytics team. Assist the team in various tasks Your profile Bachelor's or Master's studies in Computer Science, Data Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, Microengineering, or a related engineering field, with a focus on machine learning. Know-how Good knowledge of machine learning and engineering fundamentals Proficiency in Python Familiarity with time-series and sensor data Interest in industrial experimentation Hands-on skills to build and instrument an experimental setup Familiarity with Git and Linux is an advantage Knowledge of acoustic sensing or virtual metrology is an advantage Strong English communication skills; German is an advantage Interpersonal Skills Driven and motivated Practical, hands-on working style Good communication skills Highly collaborative Flexible and adaptable thinking and operating style CSEM mission and values We believe in a future that is imagined, shared, and created TOGETHER. At CSEM, we don’t just innovate, we envision technologies that shape tomorrow. Since 1984, our purpose has remained constant: to harness science and technology for the benefit of society. Today, with over 650 people across Switzerland, we remain committed to our mission: to develop and transfer world-class solutions in digital technologies, precision manufacturing, and sustainable energy systems. In doing so, we empower Swiss industry to innovate and remain competitive. Our strength is the excellence of our people. We believe that strong values support the successful development of our organization as well as the harmonious and balanced development of all our employees. We are A unique place between research and industry at the cutting edge of new technologies An innovative, non-profit, and employee-driven company A dynamic, multidisciplinary, and multicultural environment A solar team focused on enabling solutions to energy challenges for a sustainable world Working@CSEM means Being part of a passionate community. Incredible flexibility, attractive working conditions, and great opportunities of development. Benefit from a management style based on trust & feedback and that favors a work-life balance. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity. items.desc: Rejoignez l’équipe Stratégie et Innovation du AI Hub, de préférence à Grenoble (Schneider Electric, Intencity) ou en région parisienne (Schneider Electric, Edenn), dans un environnement collaboratif et innovant consacré aux enjeux majeurs de l’électrification et de la transition énergétique. items.title: Research Associate (m/f/d) at the Institute of Geo-Hydroinformatics
items.card: YOUR TASKS Develop AI, data-driven, and environmental models to quantify groundwater–land–climate interactions and cascading impacts Utilize satellite Earth Observation, global datasets, and big-data analytics to assess environmental changes Publish research in leading peer-reviewed journals and present findings at scientific meetings and conferences Contribute to teaching and assist with other tasks as assigned by
items.desc: Research Associate (m/f/d) Institute for Geo-Hydroinformatics Remuneration EG 13 TV-L ID 27726WB9 Start of employment 01.01.2027 Application deadline 18.11.2026 Scopefull time and fixed term until 31.12.2030 The Institute of Geo-Hydroinformatics at Hamburg University of Technology (TUHH) is seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate to investigate groundwater dynamics and their interactions with land, climate, and environmental systems at regional to global scales. Groundwater is a critical component of the Earth system, supporting ecosystems, agriculture, and water security while interacting with land-surface and atmospheric processes. Increasing groundwater abstraction and climate pressure are, however, driving substantial changes in groundwater resources worldwide, with potentially far-reaching environmental consequences. The successful candidate will develop and apply advanced modeling and data-driven approaches to investigate groundwater variability and depletion and how these changes propagate through the terrestrial system. Potential research directions include interactions with land subsidence, soil moisture and evapotranspiration, vegetation dynamics, land-surface temperature, hydroclimatic extremes, and land degradation. The project will leverage artificial intelligence, satellite Earth Observation, global datasets, geospatial analysis, and environmental modeling to identify patterns, interactions, and potential critical thresholds in coupled groundwater–land–climate systems. YOUR TASKS Develop AI, data-driven, and environmental models to quantify groundwater–land–climate interactions and cascading impacts Utilize satellite Earth Observation, global datasets, and big-data analytics to assess environmental changes Publish research in leading peer-reviewed journals and present findings at scientific meetings and conferences Contribute to teaching and assist with other tasks as assigned by the Head of the Institute Collaborate with other universities and institutes through research visits YOUR PROFILE Requirements Completed scientific university studies (masters degree or equivalent), in particular environmental engineering, civil engineering, hydrology, ecohydrology, fluid mechanics, or a related field Desired knowledge and personal skills Proven experience in large-scale modeling, big data analytics, and satellite remote sensing Excellent communication skills in English (both oral and written) Commitment to international collaboration, teamwork, and student supervision, if required OUR OFFER Opportunity to obtain academic qualifications in the form of doctorate/opportunity for further academic qualification 30 day vacation per year (5-days a week) Good public transport connections Company pension scheme, capital-forming benefits Internal offers for health promotion and special conditions in gyms At the heart of TU Hamburg’s research, teaching and transfer of technology is the guiding principle of developing technology for people. The TU Hamburg sees itself in this context as a family-friendly and sustainable university with high performance and quality standards that strives for excellence in all its research fields. Interdisciplinarity, innovation, regionality and internationality are binding principles in our actions. With currently around 8.000 students, 110 professors and 1.650 employees, the TU Hamburg is characterised by short decision-making processes and close cooperation between the board, the institutes, the deans of studies, the research areas and the administration. We identify ourselves with a modern leadership culture and cultivate appreciative interaction. Note regarding the Standard Enquiry under Section 34a of the Hamburg Security Clearance Act: The department will submit an enquiry to the State Office for the Protection of the Constitution regarding any information it holds on the person selected in the recruitment process, provided that the legal requirements are met (information on the Standard Inquiry and data protection notices ). For further information please contact Eva Bayley, Phone: +49 40 30601 2871. We value diversity, therefore all applications are welcome, regardless of gender, gender identity, ethnic origin, nationality, age, religion and belief, disability, sexual orientation and identity or social background. The TU Hamburg stands for equal opportunities as well as appreciative and respectful cooperation. Notice for severely disabled persons and people with equal status. Estamos à procura de um AI Engineer para integrar desafios tecnológicos relacionados com o desenvolvimento e implementação de soluções de Inteligência Artificial. Se tens experiência em desenvolvimento de software, Machine Learning e implementação de modelos de IA, queremos conhecer-te! O que vais fazer? Desenvolver e implementar soluções baseadas em Inteligência Artificial e Machine Learning. Conceber, treinar, testar e otimizar modelos de Machine Learning. Desenvolver aplicações e serviços utilizando Python e outras tecnologias de programação. Integrar modelos de IA em aplicações e sistemas existentes, através de APIs e outros serviços. Trabalhar com grandes volumes de dados para desenvolver e melhorar modelos inteligentes. Colaborar com equipas de Data Engineering, Data Science e Software Development. Monitorizar e avaliar o desempenho dos modelos, garantindo a sua fiabilidade, escalabilidade e eficiência. Contribuir para a evolução e melhoria contínua das soluções implementadas. O que procuramos? Formação superior em Engenharia Informática, Ciência de Dados, Matemática ou áreas similares. items.desc: < Indietro AI Engineer Roma, RM, Italia Modalità Full Time Tipo di impiego Hybrid Requisiti Ogni progetto è diverso dal precedente. E la soluzione giusta raramente è la stessa. In Data-Driven.Ai stiamo portando l'intelligenza artificiale al centro dei nostri prodotti e processi e cerchiamo un/una AI Engineer che voglia costruirla con noi, dal primo prototipo alla produzione. Non partiamo dalla tecnologia ma dal problema: machine learning classico, deep learning, modelli linguistici o una combinazione di questi, applicati a testo, immagini, documenti, dati tabellari e serie temporali. Un ruolo in un team trasversale, con autonomia nelle scelte tecniche e un impatto diretto e visibile sui prodotti. Se ti incuriosisce l'AI nel suo insieme e ti diverte imparare qualcosa di nuovo a ogni progetto, o conosci qualcuno a cui succede, trovi l'annuncio completo qui sotto. Informazioni sull'offerta di lavoro Le aziende sono piene di dati e di informazioni destrutturate da cui spesso non riescono a trarre valore. Data-Driven.Ai sviluppa applicazioni «smart by design», con algoritmi in grado di produrre, aggregare e valorizzare i dati aziendali, e implementa dashboard e cruscotti decisionali per supportare con fatti concreti le scelte delle aziende. Data-Driven.Ai è alla ricerca di un/una AI Engineer , professionista con esperienza nello sviluppo di soluzioni di machine learning e AI, interessato/a a lavorare su progetti nati da esigenze di business molto diverse tra loro, che raramente si risolvono con lo stesso strumento. Entrerai a far parte di un team trasversale, dove ogni progetto è diverso dal precedente: il tuo compito sarà capire quale approccio funziona meglio, costruirlo e portarlo in produzione. Un'opportunità per lavorare su progetti sempre diversi, toccare con mano molte aree dell'AI e crescere come profilo completo. Ti Occuperai Di analizzare insieme al business e al prodotto i casi d'uso, valutando se e come l'AI può risolverli; scegliere l'approccio più adatto a ogni problema: modelli di machine learning classico, deep learning, modelli linguistici o una combinazione di questi; progettare, sviluppare e testare soluzioni AI end-to-end, dal prototipo rapido al servizio in produzione; lavorare con dati di natura diversa: testo, immagini, documenti, dati tabellari e serie temporali; integrare modelli e servizi AI, open source o di terze parti, in applicazioni, API e flussi aziendali esistenti; misurare la qualità delle soluzioni con metriche chiare e migliorarle nel tempo, curando affidabilità, costi e performance; tenerti aggiornato/a sull'evoluzione del settore e portare nel team nuove idee, strumenti e tecniche; collaborare con sviluppatori, data scientist e figure di prodotto, condividendo conoscenza e documentando il lavoro. Cosa cerchiamo? Cerchiamo persone con solide basi di machine learning, almeno un progetto AI portato in produzione e la curiosità di affrontare problemi nuovi senza una soluzione già scritta. In Particolare, Valutiamo laurea in Informatica, Ingegneria, Matematica, Fisica o discipline affini, oppure esperienza equivalente; [3+] anni di esperienza nello sviluppo di soluzioni di machine learning o AI, con almeno un progetto arrivato in produzione; ottima conoscenza di Python e dell'ecosistema per dati e ML (ad es. NumPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Keras); solide basi di machine learning: come si addestra, valuta e confronta un modello, e quando un approccio semplice è sufficiente; esperienza pratica con più di una famiglia di tecniche AI e capacità di passare dall'una all'altra in base al problema; familiarità con le buone pratiche di sviluppo software: Git, testing, API, container (Docker); capacità di spiegare le scelte tecniche anche a persone non tecniche; buona conoscenza dell'inglese tecnico, curiosità e autonomia. Costituiscono Un Plus esperienza con almeno un cloud provider (AWS, Azure o GCP) e con i relativi servizi AI; conoscenza di pratiche MLOps: versionamento di dati e modelli, monitoraggio, pipeline di deploy; contributi a progetti open source, side project o partecipazione a competizioni (ad es. Kaggle); esperienza in contesti in cui si lavora su più progetti in parallelo. Se non soddisfi tutti i requisiti ma il ruolo ti incuriosisce, candidati comunque: ci interessano soprattutto la curiosità e la voglia di imparare. Condizioni Sede di lavoro: Roma Nord (Talenti) – modalità ibrida, con presenza in ufficio 2 volte a settimana Tipologia di contratto: CCNL Commercio RAL: range 25k-40k, commisurata all'esperienza Benefit : buoni pasto, pc aziendale Data-Driven.Ai crede nelle pari opportunità e valuta tutte le cand idature senza distinzione di genere, età, origine, orientamento o disabilità. Inviare CV dettagliato con consenso al trattamento dei dati personali D.lgs. 196/03 e GDPR UE 2016/679. Candidati Entra nel nostro Team! Farai parte di un gruppo giovane e motivato!

items.desc: Cześć! W Wirtualnej Polsce wierzymy, że nie ma jednej drogi do sukcesu - liczy się to, co wniesiesz i jak będziesz działać. Kreatywność, odwaga i innowacyjność to nasze DNA. Działamy w obszarach mediów, reklamy i e-commerce, łącząc te elementy w sposób, który angażuje i inspiruje. Tworzymy, testujemy, wprowadzamy zmiany tam, gdzie mają sens. Budujemy rzeczy od zera i szukamy nowych rozwiązań. Nad czym pracuje nasz zespół? Ile warto zapłacić za wyświetlenie reklamy? Nasze modele odpowiadają na to pytanie miliardy razy dziennie. Budujemy mózg biddera RTB, który kupuje powierzchnię reklamową dla klientów e-commerce. Pracujemy w skali, która robi wrażenie: setki tysięcy zapytań na sekundę, dziesiątki miliardów decyzji ML dziennie, a cały proces inferencji musi zmieścić się w kilkudziesięciu milisekundach. To jeden z kluczowych produktów reklamowych WP, więc jakość Twoich modeli przekłada się na przychody i marżę. Jako Data Scientist masz pełny ownership: od postawienia hipotezy i analizy danych, przez trening modeli i testy A/B, po wdrożenie na produkcję i monitoring. Sam prowadzisz swój projekt od początku do końca bez przekazywania go dalej i czekania na efekty. Mierzymy się z trudnymi problemami z obszaru real-time ML, optymalizacji i statystyki, a narzędzia AI są naturalną częścią naszego codziennego warsztatu. Jeśli zależy Ci na realnym wpływie na produkt działający w dużej skali, to miejsce dla Ciebie! Jakie działania będą należeć do Ciebie? Projektowanie i wdrażanie modeli ML rozwiązujących problemy biznesowe (predykcja, ranking, modelowanie zachowań użytkowników). Tworzenie i wdrażanie algorytmów optymalizacyjnych oraz rekomendacyjnych (np. ustalanie stawek w aukcjach, alokacja budżetów, personalizacja treści), wprost przekładających się na kluczowe wskaźniki biznesowe (np. eCPM, CTR, przychód, LTV, zaangażowanie czytelników). Udział w projektach badawczo-rozwojowych (R&D) – sprawdzanie nowych metod ML/AI (np. modele sekwencyjne, LLM, RL), testowanie hipotez i przenoszenie najlepszych pomysłów na produkcję. Projektowanie i analiza testów A/B na ruchu produkcyjnym, umożliwiających precyzyjną ocenę wpływu modeli na biznes. Współpraca z zespołami inżynierskimi, produktowymi i biznesowymi oraz dzielenie się wiedzą w zespole. Jakie kompetencje są dla nas ważne? Minimum 3 lata doświadczenia komercyjnego w budowaniu modeli ML i wdrażaniu ich na produkcję jako Data Scientist, ML Engineer lub na podobnym stanowisku. Bardzo dobra znajomość Pythona i narzędzi takich jak PyTorch, LightGBM, XGBoost czy Polars. Umiejętność pisania czytelnego kodu i testów oraz doświadczenie w pracy z Gitem i w przeprowadzaniu code review. Doświadczenie w pracy z dużymi zbiorami danych z wykorzystaniem SQL (np. w ClickHouse lub StarRocks) oraz Apache Spark, PySpark lub podobnych narzędzi. Solidne podstawy z zakresu rachunku prawdopodobieństwa, statystyki i optymalizacji, zdobyte np. na studiach matematycznych, fizycznych, informatycznych lub pokrewnych. Umiejętność samodzielnego przekładania problemów biznesowych na zadania ML i jasnego przedstawiania wyników także osobom nietechnicznym. Znajomość języka angielskiego na poziomie B2, pozwalająca swobodnie korzystać z dokumentacji technicznej i publikacji naukowych. Mile widziane: Domena: AdTech/RTB (np. OpenRTB, DSP/SSP, Prebid/GAM) lub personalizacja na dużą skalę w mediach, e-commerce albo FinTechu. Rekomendacje i deep learning: modele sekwencyjne, retrieval i ranking, LLM. Metody decyzyjne: wnioskowanie przyczynowe (uplift, testy inkrementalności), bandyci kontekstowi, RL lub teoria aukcji. Produkcja ML: serving o niskich opóźnieniach (np. C++, ONNX, TensorRT, Triton Inference Server – wystarczy jedna z tych technologii) lub MLOps (Docker/Kubernetes, MLflow, Iceberg/Delta Lake, chmura). Badania: publikacje, open source z zakresu ML lub doktorat (także w trakcie). Co zyskujesz, dołączając do WP? Pracę u technologicznego lidera i partnera pierwszego wyboru – tworzymy treści, usługi i rozrywkę, które towarzyszą milionom Polaków każdego dnia Darmowy dostęp do naszych produktów, takich jak Pilot WP czy Audioteka -chcemy, żebyś czuł się częścią tego, co tworzymy ❤️ Worksmile i elastyczny pakiet benefitów - to Ty wybierasz, co jest dla Ciebie ważne Dostęp do bezpłatnych i anonimowych konsultacji psychologicznych Możliwość pracy hybrydowej - pracujemy 3 dni w biurze oraz 2 dni z domu łącząc swobodę pracy zdalnej z tym, co najlepsze w biurze Wydarzenia, które zbliżają - od sezonowych akcji (Dzień Dziecka to nasz ulubieniec!) po webinary o zdrowiu i neuroróżnorodności Możliwość rozwoju dzięki szkoleniom w ramach programu WP Akademia Szansę na nowe wyzwania i kierunki w ramach spółek WP Holding - wewnętrzne rekrutacje są na wyciągnięcie ręki
