PhD fellow in Molecular biology, Biotechnology and Genomics - IT | Lifetech 
 PhD fellow in Molecular biology, Biotechnology and Genomics 
 Italy 
 IIT invites excellent candidates to apply to its PhD program organized in collaboration with the Open University; this international PhD program confers Doctorates in Health, Sustainable and Human Technologies .
 In order to be admitted into the ARC program, the minimum requirements are
 a Masters-level degree, which broadly corresponds to a 4/5-year undergraduate MSc/MChem/Meng-style degree or to a postgraduate Masters in the British system, or to a second level University degree in Italy;
 a grade corresponding to an upper second class (2.1) or a merit in the UK system or 100/110 in the Italian system. Candidates with lower grades but redeeming features (publications, specific expertise) are requested to contact the potential supervisors before applying;
 where English is not the applicant’s first language, a valid IELTS (International English Language Testing System) certificate. The minimum acceptable score is an overall 6.5, with no less than 6.0 in any of the four categories
 One PhD fellow position will be available from 1st of January 2027 in the Non-coding Genomics research Line led by Stefano Gustincich .
 Title of the project : The SINEUPOME . 
 Background : SINEUPs are a class of natural and synthetic antisense long non-coding RNAs that selectively increase the translation of a target mRNA without altering its transcription or stability. They were discovered through the mouse antisense Uchl1 transcript (Carrieri et al., Nature 2012), whose activity depends on an embedded inverted SINEB2 repeat, the origin of the name.
 SINEUPs have a modular architecture. A binding domain, antisense to the 5′ region of the target mRNA (typically overlapping the start codon), confers specificity. An effector domain, containing the inverted SINEB2 element or minimal functional fragments of it, drives translational enhancement. Swapping the binding domain lets SINEUPs be designed against virtually any gene of interest.
 Their effect is moderate (about 1.5- to 3-fold protein increase) and stays within physiological ranges. This makes them attractive for haploinsufficiency disorders and other conditions caused by insufficient protein dosage. They are also useful for biotechnological protein production. They can be delivered as plasmids, viral vectors such as AAV, or synthetic RNA.
 Description: 
 Rationale . Only a handful of natural SINEUPs are known, yet inverted SINE elements are abundant in antisense transcripts across mammals. A systematic analysis would reveal how widespread translational enhancement by antisense lncRNAs really is.
 Aim 1 – Computational catalogue. Mine CAGE (FANTOM5/6), total RNA-seq and nanopore long-read datasets from human, mouse and non-model mammals to annotate lncRNAs with an embedded inverted SINE (SINEB2, MIR, Alu, FLAM).
 Aim 2 – PARIS analysis. Identify lncRNA/mRNA pairs in PARIS data from a diverse array of dataset. List which candidate SINEUPs from Aim 1 are part of the duplex.
 Aim 3 – Functional validation. Test 50–100 top SINEUP candidates in HEK293 and neuronal cells, measuring protein over mRNA ratio of the targets by western blot, qRT-PCR and polysome profiling.
 Impact . A validated atlas of natural SINEUPs and their targets, plus rules linking sequence architecture to activity, would provide both a new layer of post-transcriptional gene regulation and design principles for synthetic SINEUP therapeutics.
 References
 D'Agostino S, Tettey-Matey A, Volpe M, Pierattini B, D'Agostino M, Smělá D, Ansaloni F, Broglia L, Lau P, Peruzzo O, Braccia C, Armirotti A, Scarpato M, Damiani D, Ros G, Di Carlo V, Maniscalco F, Bechara E, Tartaglia GG, Carninci P, Santoro C, Persichetti F, Pandolfini L, Simonetti A, Espinoza S, Zucchelli S, Sanges R, Bon C, Gustincich S. (2025). Internal ribosome entry sites enhance translation in trans in antisense non-coding SINEUP and circular RNAs. Nucleic Acids Res. 53(15):gkaf788.

items.desc: Job description Background Machine learning is increasingly used in aerospace for tasks that have traditionally relied on human experts or on fixed rule-based procedures. For such tasks, data-driven algorithms promise gains in speed, consistency and sensitivity. Before they can be used in practice however, they must be qualified, which means it has to be demonstrated with sufficient substantiation that the algorithm performs its intended function reliably within a defined set of conditions. The qualification approaches used in the sector today were developed for human operators and for conventional systems whose behaviour can be traced back to explicit requirements. They do not translate directly to algorithms whose behaviour is learned from data, and emerging guidance from aviation authorities names explainability as a key ingredient of trustworthy AI, while leaving open how it should be demonstrated in practice. Performance figures on a test set do not show why an algorithm reaches a decision, whether it relies on physically meaningful information, or how it behaves outside the data it was trained on. Explainable machine learning offers a wide range of methods to address this, from feature attribution and saliency methods, to example-based and concept-based explanations, but it is still an open question which of these can provide evidence that is strong enough to support qualification. This project therefore investigates how explainability methods can contribute to the qualification of machine learning algorithms for aerospace, starting from an use case, and provides a comparative assessment of several methods. Assignment The assignment will include the following tasks: A literature study on the qualification of machine learning algorithms in safety-critical sectors and on explainability methods for machine learning (e.g., attribution and saliency methods, example-based and concept-based explanations, interpretable models, uncertainty quantification), including the ways in which explanations themselves are evaluated. A use case provided by NLR, for instance automated defect detection, and identification of the substantiation needed to qualify the algorithm, translated into criteria that explanations should meet. Implementing several explainability methods for the use case and analysing them against these criteria, for example their faithfulness to the model, their robustness and their usefulness to domain experts. Assessing how the resulting explanations can serve as evidence in the qualification of the algorithm, and formulating recommendations for the use of explainability in qualification. Results The final outcomes of this assignment will be: § A structured assessment, as part of a literature study, of explainability methods for machine learning and their suitability for qualification in aerospace, together with a justified selection of the use case. § An implementation and comparative evaluation of several explainability methods on the selected use case, with recommendations on how explainability can support the qualification of the algorithm. § A technical report, either an MSc thesis following the guidelines of your faculty or an internship report, describing the approach, results, and conclusions of the work. Duration For an MSc thesis, the standard duration of a thesis at your faculty applies (typically 9 months). For an internship, the duration is 6 months. Profile You are an MSc student in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Applied Mathematics or a similar master. You have a strong background in machine learning, preferably deep learning. Knowledge of explainable AI is a plus. You have experience with programming in Python and with machine learning libraries, for instance PyTorch or scikit-learn. You have an affinity with aerospace, inspection or certification, and are motivated to bring machine learning closer to qualified use in practice. What we offer A challenging graduation project/internship in a high-tech result orientated work environment Weekly supervision and availability of the technical staff for support An internship allowance Working in an actual R&D project as part of the team Internship results to be used in the current and future projects About NLR Royal NLR has been the ambitious research organisation with the will to keep innovating for over 100 years. With that drive, we make the world of transportation safer, more sustainable, more efficient and more effective. We are on the threshold of breakthrough innovations. Plans and ideas start to move when these are fed with the right energy. Over 800 driven professionals work on research and innovation, from aircraft engineers to psychologists and from mathematicians to application experts. Our colleagues are happy to tell you what it's like to work at NLR. This assignment will be managed by the Avionics Systems and Maintenance Engineering (ASAM) department. Interested? items.desc: In YouGov Shopper , we believe that constant innovation is the key to improve the pertinence and quality of the data that we receive from our consumer panel members and app users. To achieve this goal, we have developed a coding framework that automatically enriches shop receipts and consequently reduces work for our panelists. As a Junior Data Scientist , you’ll be part of a cross-functional team of machine learning engineers, developers, and fellow data scientists. Together, you’ll help design and build new components of our coding framework, enabling richer insights by enhancing consumer panel purchase data. Here’s a Breakdown Of What You’ll Do Development and evaluation of NLP and ML models for tasks such as text classification, clustering, entity recognition, and semantic search. Conduct exploratory data analysis and create clear visualizations to understand patterns and trends. Be active as a member of our Agile Team, participate in the definition of tasks, share your findings, raise risks and uncertainty, challenge priorities during our plannings. Present your achievements to the team and to broader audience during agile ceremonies (sprint reviews, system demos…). Learn more about the various areas in Yougov Shopper by working on cross-team projects. Stay up to date with basic advancements in machine learning and NLP, applying new techniques under guidance. Create and improve current methods and tools, contribute to refine best practices around Data Science. These are the essentials you’ll need to get an interview: 0–2 years of professional experience in data science, applied ML, or a related field (internships, academic projects, or research experience welcome). Solid foundation in statistics, probability, and basic machine learning techniques. Proficiency in Python and familiarity with common data science libraries (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, matplotlib). Interest in and some exposure to NLP techniques (tokenization, embeddings, transformers, or classical NLP methods). Nice-to-have Skills Exposure to deep learning frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow). Familiarity with NLP libraries such as Hugging Face Transformers, spaCy, or NLTK. Experience working on academic projects or Kaggle competitions involving NLP or ML. Understanding of basic cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure) for data and ML workloads. Familiarity with version control tools (Git) and collaborative coding practices. Tools & Technology Jupyter, Python and Python best practices and coding standards. Python frameworks as pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, stats models . git, GitLab, basic CI/CD awareness. Collaboration & documentation: JIRA, Confluence, Teams, Miro. Why join YouGov? Join our global team to help us achieve our social mission: to make millions of people’s opinions heard for the benefit of our local, national, and international communities. Understanding diversity of opinion requires diversity of background. Although our global panel of millions of people worldwide powers our research, our biggest asset is our people. If our research is to be truly representative of what the world thinks, we need people from all walks of life to be part of the team to bring their perspective to the work we do. Life at YouGov We are driven by a set of shared values. We are fast, fearless, and innovative. We work diligently to get it right. We are guided by accuracy, ethics, and proven methodologies. items.desc: At Lely, we believe in achieving a sustainable, profitable and agreeable future for dairy farmers by combining robotisation, engineering and farming expertise. It all started with a dream cherished by two brothers in Maassluis 75 years ago, and ever since, we have worked to become innovative market leaders in automated systems for dairy farmers across the globe. With a team of over 2,800 professional specialists, we work constantly to bring about revolutionary solutions for the agro industry. We are based at our Maassluis Campus, a building which features the highest sustainability performance possible, not just in the Netherlands, but on a global scale. Our overall objective: making dairy farming interesting, also for the coming generations. Vacatureomschrijving At Lely, we develop smart robotics solutions that support and improve the daily work of dairy farmers. As a Junior Machine Vision Engineer, you will be part of the Computer Vision team and work on technology that quite literally forms the “eyes” of our robots. Together with colleagues from computer vision, mechatronics, and animal science, you will develop solutions that enable robots to better understand their environment and respond accordingly. You will contribute to applications in the field of image recognition and algorithms, with the ultimate goal of improving the lives of both farmers and cows. You will work in a small, close-knit team where collaboration, learning, and experimentation are key. From time to time, you will visit farms to see your work in practice and gather valuable feedback from the field. Your main responsibilities: Researching, designing, and implementing computer vision algorithms. Working on image recognition applications using deep learning and neural networks. Testing and validating algorithms in close collaboration with colleagues and in real-life environments. Contributing to iterative improvements within an Agile/Scrum working environment. Collaborating with specialists from different disciplines to develop robust and reliable solutions. Functie-eisen You are at the start of your career or have a few years of experience and are curious about how computer vision and AI are applied in real-world products. You enjoy learning, asking questions, and developing technology together with others. You bring: A completed bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Informatics, or a comparable field. A strong interest in computer vision, deep learning, and neural networks (for example through internships, projects, or a thesis). Basic programming experience in C++ is a must, Python is a plus. Familiarity with tools and frameworks such as OpenCV, PyTorch, or similar is a plus. Affinity with Agile/Scrum ways of working. Good command of the English language; Dutch is a plus or you are willing to learn. A curious, collaborative mindset and the motivation to continue developing yourself. Aanvullende informatie Working at Lely means contributing to sustainable progress within one of the most innovative organizations in the Netherlands. You help make the agricultural sector future-proof. We make sure you have the space, resources, and support you need to grow and do your best work. An international environment where collaboration, initiative, and diverse perspectives are valued A culture that encourages learning, experimentation, and ownership of ideas. Excellent working conditions, including up to 8 weeks of vacation per year and a good pension scheme. A full-time salary range between €4,100 and €5,800 gross per month, with room for growth within the scale. Control over your own development, with access to a wide range of courses through the Lely Academy Daily access to excellent sports facilities on the Lely Campus: an indoor gym, outdoor padel courts, basketball and volleyball courts, table tennis, and table soccer. You can join Hyrox workouts or sign up for personal training - and challenge your colleagues during an active break. Fresh coffee and tea from our own barista (with milk from our farm) and a healthy, affordable company restaurant Work-life balance A healthy work-life balance thanks to our hybrid work policy: you work at least three days a week on Campus, with flexible working hours and plenty of room to spend extra time on site (between 06:00 and 20:00). A free shuttle bus will take you to and from the metro in Maassluis, so your workday starts and ends smoothly. Moreover, we love to celebrate. Whether it's an anniversary or our Christmas party, at Lely, we know how to celebrate! For a feel of the atmosphere, check out this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6WA3e0WHbxE We are also proud that our efforts and vision have been rewarded by winning the Rotterdam Entrepreneur Award 2025! items.desc: MP DATA est une société spécialisée dans l’acquisition, le traitement, et la valorisation des données. Depuis sa création en 2015, MP DATA accompagne ses clients, majoritairement industriels, dans le management de leur performance et l’exploitation de leur données. Les collaborateurs incarnent au quotidien les valeurs d’Excellence, de Partage et d’Engagement. Ils associent savoir-faire technique, méthodologie et passion et mettent leurs compétences au service de missions et projets. MP DATA accompagne ses clients sur toute la chaine au travers de 5 pôles d’expertise : Conseil & Stratégie, Data Architecture, Data Science, Data Engineering et Recherche Opérationnelle. Chez MP DATA, la priorité des équipes commerciales est de chercher des missions en fonction des envies des collaborateurs. Les consultants sont accompagnés dans tous leurs projets, de la mobilité géographique au changement de secteur d’activité en passant par le développement de nouvelles compétences. Rejoindre MP DATA, c’est la garantie de travailler sur des sujets passionnants avec un cadre technique fort. En tant que Data Scientist, vous serez responsable du développement de modèles avancés et de leur intégration dans des pipelines de production, en collaboration étroite avec les Data Engineers, ML Engineers et équipes métier. Vos missions incluront : Développement & Modélisation Concevoir, développer et optimiser des modèles de machine learning , deep learning ou de modélisation mathématique . Réaliser l’analyse exploratoire des données (EDA), le prétraitement, la sélection de features et la validation statistique. Mettre en place des expérimentations reproductibles et comparer différentes approches (benchmarks). Qualité, Tests & Documentation Effectuer des tests unitaires , tests de performance et validation des modèles. Participer aux phases de test, recette et mise en service des modèles. Rédiger de la documentation technique claire, structurée et exploitable. Fournir des livrables professionnels : modèles performants, code commenté, notebooks reproductibles, guides utilisateurs. Intégration & Collaboration Présenter vos résultats (métriques, choix techniques, limites, recommandations) aux chefs de projets et parties prenantes métier. Accompagner et former les utilisateurs finaux à la compréhension et à l’usage des modèles développés. Veille technologique & Innovation Assurer une veille continue sur les méthodes IA, les frameworks ML/DL, et les bonnes pratiques de modélisation. Proposer des améliorations, de nouvelles approches et participer activement à la construction de l'expertise IA de MP DATA. Diplômé(e) d’une grande école d’ingénieur (Centrale, Mines, Supaero, Supelec, INSA, ISAE, etc.) ou équivalent, vous disposez d’au moins 1 an d'expérience en Data Science et d’une solide base en mathématiques appliquées, statistiques et apprentissage automatique. Vous êtes reconnu(e) pour : Votre rigueur scientifique et votre capacité d’analyse. Votre autonomie, votre curiosité et votre sens de l’initiative. Votre capacité à vulgariser vos travaux auprès de profils techniques ou métier. Votre goût pour la résolution de problèmes complexes dans des environnements industriels. With more than 10,000 professionals across 40+ offices worldwide, we provide solutions combining trading and workflow automation , market data , and advanced business intelligence. Our Graduate Development Program is a three-year journey designed for recent graduates who look beyond the obvious, challenge existing processes, and are driven to automate and reinvent the way things work. Tasks evolve according to your abilities and interests, ensuring the experience is as individual as you are. What You'll Do Across phases, you will become the owner of full data transformation and reporting pipelines, working at the intersection of business processes and technology. items.title: Ingénieur R&D IA & Perception pour les Systèmes Industriels (F/H)

Vous contribuerez à transformer ces technologies en composants logiciels réutilisables pour des applications telles que la détection d’objets, l’inspection visuelle, la compréhension de scènes 3D ou l’estimation
items.desc: Au cœur de l’innovation de Dassault Systèmes, vous rejoindrez une équipe R&D dédiée au développement de nouvelles technologies d’IA appliquées à la robotique, à la perception et à la simulation, dans l’environnement DELMIA / 3DEXPERIENCE. Votre mission consistera à exploiter les jumeaux virtuels et les données synthétiques générées par simulation pour développer, entraîner et évaluer des modèles de perception adaptés aux enjeux industriels. Vous contribuerez à transformer ces technologies en composants logiciels réutilisables pour des applications telles que la détection d’objets, l’inspection visuelle, la compréhension de scènes 3D ou l’estimation de pose 6D. Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes IA, Simulation, Robotique et Cloud afin de construire une chaîne complète, de la génération de données jusqu’à l’intégration de services de perception dans les solutions DELMIA / 3DEXPERIENCE. Vos missions Développer des capacités de perception par l’IA : concevoir et expérimenter des modèles de vision par ordinateur pour la détection, la segmentation, le suivi d’objets, l’inspection industrielle, la compréhension de scènes et l’estimation de pose 6D. Exploiter les données synthétiques : définir les besoins en simulation de capteurs et contribuer à la génération, à la structuration et à la validation de jeux de données issus des jumeaux virtuels. Entraîner et évaluer les modèles : collaborer avec les équipes IA sur les workflows d’entraînement et de fine-tuning, l’évaluation des performances et la réutilisation de modèles existants. Concevoir des pipelines de perception réutilisables : prototyper et intégrer des algorithmes pouvant être exposés sous forme de services logiciels ou d’API. Garantir la qualité des résultats : définir des métriques, des jeux de test et des protocoles de validation adaptés aux scénarios industriels. Contribuer à l’adaptation robotique : travailler avec les équipes Robotique pour exploiter les résultats de perception dans l’adaptation des robots, la mise à jour des trajectoires et la validation des processus. Industrialiser les solutions développées : participer au déploiement de services de perception évolutifs, côté serveur, intégrés à l’écosystème DELMIA / 3DEXPERIENCE. Vos Qualifications Diplôme d’ingénieur ou Bac+5 en intelligence artificielle, vision par ordinateur, traitement d’image, robotique ou domaine connexe. Solides compétences en vision par ordinateur, perception ou machine learning appliqué. Maîtrise de Python et d’un framework de deep learning tel que PyTorch ou TensorFlow. Expérience avec des données image, vidéo, profondeur (RGB-D) ou des jeux de données synthétiques. Bonne compréhension de la préparation des données, des métriques d’évaluation et de la validation des modèles. Capacité à développer des prototypes robustes et à les transformer en composants logiciels réutilisables. Compétences appréciées Expérience en estimation de pose 6D, inspection industrielle ou perception robotique. Connaissance de la génération de données synthétiques, de la simulation de capteurs ou du transfert simulation-réalité (sim-to-real). Familiarité avec NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, Omniverse, OpenCV, ROS / ROS 2 ou des environnements similaires. Connaissance des environnements 3D, de la CAO, des jumeaux virtuels ou de la calibration de caméras. Expérience avec les infrastructures GPU Cloud, le déploiement de modèles ou le MLOps. Nous rejoindre c'est aussi Intégrer une entreprise scientifique au cœur de l’innovation technologique, portée par une forte croissance depuis plus de 40 ans Principaux avantages et bénéfices : Environnement multiculturel Cadre de travail convivial axé sur le bien-être et la santé (salles de sport & de musique, conciergerie…) Engagement en faveur de la diversité et de l’inclusion Politique dynamique de développement de carrière : plan de formation, mobilités internes, etc Inclusion statement As a game-changer in sustainable technology and innovation, Dassault Systèmes is striving to build more inclusive and diverse teams across the globe. We believe that our people are our number one asset and we want all employees to feel empowered to bring their whole selves to work every day. It is our goal that our people feel a sense of pride and a passion for belonging. As a company leading change, it’s our responsibility to foster opportunities for all people to participate in a harmonized Workforce of the Future.

items.card: responsibilities include developing and integrating machine learning models, implementing neural network architectures and NLP solutions, and building robust APIs and services for AI orchestration and governance. items.desc: Company Description Intrascope enables organizations to standardize and control how AI is used across the business, without locking teams into a single model or provider. As companies move from individual AI experimentation to structured, scalable use, Intrascope offers a managed AI environment that unifies fragmented AI usage across employees, teams, models, and projects. The platform allows organizations to access multiple commercial, private, and local models, manage company and project knowledge, and centrally govern users, roles, permissions, and policies. Intrascope also provides visibility into AI usage and costs, supporting hybrid AI environments that balance cloud and local deployments based on security and data needs. The product is designed for teams that want the freedom to choose the best AI tools while giving the company one place to manage them. Role Description This is a full-time remote role for an AI Engineer at Intrascope. The AI Engineer will design, build, and optimize AI systems that support a managed, multi-model AI environment, focusing on reliability, scalability, and security. Day-to-day responsibilities include developing and integrating machine learning models, implementing neural network architectures and NLP solutions, and building robust APIs and services for AI orchestration and governance. The role involves collaborating with product and engineering teams to translate business requirements into technical solutions, improving pattern recognition and model performance, and ensuring compliance with organizational policies and data standards. The AI Engineer will also monitor system performance, contribute to documentation and best practices, and support continuous improvement of the platform’s AI capabilities. Qualifications Strong foundation in Computer Science concepts and principles, including data structures, algorithms, and system design. Experience with Software Development , including proficiency in a modern programming language (e.g., Python, Java, or similar), version control, testing, and API development. Hands-on experience with Neural Networks and Pattern Recognition for building and optimizing machine learning models in production environments. Practical expertise in Natural Language Processing (NLP) , including working with modern NLP frameworks and large language models. Familiarity with AI/ML frameworks and tools (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch, Hugging Face, or similar) and experience deploying models in cloud or hybrid environments. Understanding of AI governance, security, and responsible AI practices, including data privacy and compliance considerations. Ability to work effectively in a remote, cross-functional team, with strong communication and collaboration skills. Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

items.desc: Nous recherchons un profil hybride Data Scientist et Software Engineer , de séniorité Intermediate , pour rejoindre notre équipe Software, actuellement composée de deux feature teams (chacune avec un Engineering Manager, un Product Manager, plusieurs Software Engineers et Data Scientists), d’une équipe Data Platform et d’un Designer. Les candidats avec peu d’expérience en web , mais une forte appétence pour apprendre, comprendre le fonctionnement d’une application web moderne, et contribuer au produit côté front-end et back-end seront tout de même considérés avec attention. Le poste est ouvert à Paris , avec la possibilité de télétravailler 2 jours par semaine . La rémunération dépendra du niveau d’expérience et du périmètre de responsabilités. POURQUOI CANDIDATER ? En nous rejoignant : Tu contribueras à améliorer l’efficacité de la production électrique en France et dans le monde, sur un produit concret qui a de l’impact. Tu travailleras sur un logiciel en production, utilisé au quotidien, et conçu pour durer (robustesse, qualité, passage à l’échelle). Tu auras l’opportunité de développer une double compétence précieuse : Data Science appliquée + développement web . items.title: Ingénieur R&D en IA générative et simulation physique 3D (F/H)
items.card: Vos missions Votre mission consiste à développer des approches innovantes d’IA générative intégrant les lois et contraintes de la physique, afin de produire des modèles 3D industriels répondant à des critères de performance précis. En combinant les capacités des modèles génératifs avec la puissance des solveurs de simulation traditionnels, vous contribuerez à créer des solutions capables de générer des conceptions
items.desc: Au sein de la R&D Technologies V+R Experiences, basée à Aix-en-Provence, vous rejoindrez une équipe qui explore les technologies de pointe associant Deep Learning, IA générative et géométrie computationnelle pour repousser les limites de la conception industrielle. Dans un contexte d’innovation scientifique et technologique, vous contribuerez au développement des Industry World Models, des modèles capables de représenter et de comprendre des processus industriels complexes en combinant des données multimodales et des facteurs physiques. Ces avancées ouvrent de nouvelles perspectives pour automatiser et accélérer les processus d’ingénierie avancés. Votre terrain de jeu : faire converger IA générative, simulation physique et modélisation 3D pour concevoir la prochaine génération de solutions d’ingénierie. Poste en CDI basé à Aix-en-Provence. Vos missions Votre mission consiste à développer des approches innovantes d’IA générative intégrant les lois et contraintes de la physique, afin de produire des modèles 3D industriels répondant à des critères de performance précis. En combinant les capacités des modèles génératifs avec la puissance des solveurs de simulation traditionnels, vous contribuerez à créer des solutions capables de générer des conceptions plus pertinentes, cohérentes avec les contraintes physiques et adaptées aux exigences des applications industrielles. Au quotidien, vos missions seront les suiavntes : Identifier les cas d’usage à fort potentiel en collaboration avec les responsables produits de la plateforme 3DEXPERIENCE et comprendre les besoins des métiers de l’ingénierie. Explorer les approches scientifiques les plus prometteuses en réalisant une veille de l’état de l’art et en évaluant les solutions techniques envisageables, avec les équipes CATIA et SIMULIA, Corporate Research et les autres experts de la R&D. Concevoir et expérimenter de nouvelles méthodes en développant des prototypes, des jeux de tests et des métriques permettant d’évaluer la pertinence, la qualité et les performances des modèles générés. Développer le couplage entre IA générative et simulation physique afin d’intégrer les contraintes issues des solveurs dans le processus de génération de modèles 3D. Transformer les prototypes en solutions industrielles en assurant leur robustesse, leur validation et leur intégration dans les produits Dassault Systèmes, dans le respect des exigences de qualité et des délais. Contribuer à l’innovation collective en partageant vos travaux scientifiques et en confrontant vos idées à celles d’équipes pluridisciplinaires pour faire émerger de nouvelles solutions. Vous interviendrez sur l’ensemble du cycle de développement, de l’exploration scientifique à l’intégration dans les produits, avec un objectif concret : transformer les avancées de l’IA en technologies utiles aux ingénieurs et aux industriels. Vos Qualifications Pour réussir dans ce rôle, vous disposez d’une solide formation scientifique et d’un intérêt marqué pour les approches innovantes en intelligence artificielle. Formation et expertise technique Diplôme de niveau Bac+5, obtenu en école d’ingénieur ou à l’université, dans un domaine pertinent : informatique, mathématiques appliquées, intelligence artificielle ou domaine scientifique connexe. Expérience en Deep Learning et en IA générative, idéalement appliqués à la vision par ordinateur, à la géométrie algorithmique ou à la génération de contenus 3D. Maîtrise de Python et de PyTorch, ainsi que de bonnes compétences en programmation C++. Capacité à comprendre, concevoir et mettre en œuvre des méthodes algorithmiques complexes. Un doctorat en Deep Learning ou dans un domaine scientifique connexe constitue un atout pour approfondir les problématiques de recherche du poste. Une connaissance des technologies MLOps et des environnements Cloud est un plus. Approche scientifique et qualités professionnelles Curiosité scientifique et intérêt pour l’exploration de nouvelles approches en IA, au-delà des solutions déjà établies. Capacité à analyser des travaux de recherche, à évaluer leur pertinence et à les adapter à des problématiques industrielles concrètes. items.desc: Job Description Background Machine learning is increasingly used in aerospace for tasks that have traditionally relied on human experts or on fixed rule-based procedures. For such tasks, data-driven algorithms promise gains in speed, consistency and sensitivity. Before they can be used in practice however, they must be qualified, which means it has to be demonstrated with sufficient substantiation that the algorithm performs its intended function reliably within a defined set of conditions. The qualification approaches used in the sector today were developed for human operators and for conventional systems whose behaviour can be traced back to explicit requirements. They do not translate directly to algorithms whose behaviour is learned from data, and emerging guidance from aviation authorities names explainability as a key ingredient of trustworthy AI, while leaving open how it should be demonstrated in practice. Performance figures on a test set do not show why an algorithm reaches a decision, whether it relies on physically meaningful information, or how it behaves outside the data it was trained on. Explainable machine learning offers a wide range of methods to address this, from feature attribution and saliency methods, to example-based and concept-based explanations, but it is still an open question which of these can provide evidence that is strong enough to support qualification. This project therefore investigates how explainability methods can contribute to the qualification of machine learning algorithms for aerospace, starting from an use case, and provides a comparative assessment of several methods. Assignment The Assignment Will Include The Following Tasks A literature study on the qualification of machine learning algorithms in safety-critical sectors and on explainability methods for machine learning (e.g., attribution and saliency methods, example-based and concept-based explanations, interpretable models, uncertainty quantification), including the ways in which explanations themselves are evaluated. A use case provided by NLR, for instance automated defect detection, and identification of the substantiation needed to qualify the algorithm, translated into criteria that explanations should meet. Implementing several explainability methods for the use case and analysing them against these criteria, for example their faithfulness to the model, their robustness and their usefulness to domain experts. Assessing how the resulting explanations can serve as evidence in the qualification of the algorithm, and formulating recommendations for the use of explainability in qualification. Results The Final Outcomes Of This Assignment Will Be A structured assessment, as part of a literature study, of explainability methods for machine learning and their suitability for qualification in aerospace, together with a justified selection of the use case. An implementation and comparative evaluation of several explainability methods on the selected use case, with recommendations on how explainability can support the qualification of the algorithm. A technical report, either an MSc thesis following the guidelines of your faculty or an internship report, describing the approach, results, and conclusions of the work. Duration For an MSc thesis, the standard duration of a thesis at your faculty applies (typically 9 months). For an internship, the duration is 6 months. Profile You are an MSc student in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Applied Mathematics or a similar master. You have a strong background in machine learning, preferably deep learning. Knowledge of explainable AI is a plus. You have experience with programming in Python and with machine learning libraries, for instance PyTorch or scikit-learn. You have an affinity with aerospace, inspection or certification, and are motivated to bring machine learning closer to qualified use in practice. What We Offer A challenging graduation project/internship in a high-tech result orientated work environment Weekly supervision and availability of the technical staff for support An internship allowance Working in an actual R&D project as part of the team Internship results to be used in the current and future projects About NLR Royal NLR has been the ambitious research organisation with the will to keep innovating for over 100 years. With that drive, we make the world of transportation safer, more sustainable, more efficient and more effective. We are on the threshold of breakthrough innovations. Plans and ideas start to move when these are fed with the right energy. Over 800 driven professionals work on research and innovation, from aircraft engineers to psychologists and from mathematicians to application experts. Our colleagues are happy to tell you what it's like to work at NLR. This assignment will be managed by the Avionics Systems and Maintenance Engineering (ASAM) department. Interested? Apply now and help us advance the next generation of predictive solutions in maternal and reproductive health.

It's great at deducing the mechanics that govern a system; yet, standalone, it's just one query-answer cycle. This role harnesses the full potential of that core intelligence by embedding it in a sophisticated agentic system capable of tackling multi-step, long-horizon tasks. As our Harness Engineer, you own the path from a raw ML model to an intelligent, largely autonomous system: harnesses, inference algorithmics, context curation, and hierarchical querying. You will work in the seam between research and product, giving free reign to your creativity when designing the system and exercising discipline and diligence when handing it over to the productization team. Tasks Turn research models into sophisticated agentic systems capable of a large degree of autonomy. Build harnesses, inference algorithms and systems, smart context curation. Build release criteria that show quantitatively when an agent is ready to ship. Build developer-facing abstractions around our agentic systems. Work closely with researchers to expose failure modes; receive product feedback from customers and turn it into better systems. Sound judgment around evaluation, observability, reliability and production trade-offs. The ability to work directly with customers, researchers and product stakeholders. A pragmatic, outcome-oriented mindset: you optimize for dependable capabilities that users can actually adopt. We are primarily hiring at senior level. items.desc:
Mission 
 The South–North Laboratory for Sustainable Construction and Conservation (SONO Lab) at EPFL is recruiting a full-time PhD Student (100%) within the School of Architecture, Civil and Environmental Engineering (ENAC), based at the EPFL Fribourg associated campus.
 SONO Lab investigates low-carbon, climate-responsive and socially inclusive approaches to building design, construction and conservation. Its research combines architectural design, environmental assessment, digital methods, full-scale experimentation, building-performance monitoring and participatory approaches, with a particular focus on collaborations between Europe and Africa.
 The successful candidate will contribute to REGEN4BE—Regenerative Design for the Built Environment, a Horizon Europe project developed within the New European Bauhaus framework. REGEN4BE seeks to make regenerative design measurable, interoperable and scalable through digital tools, innovative materials, participatory processes, Living Labs and policy development. Its outputs include a Regenerative Evaluation Framework and the Regenerative Design Intelligence Platform (REDIP). Fribourg is one of the project’s European demonstration and replication sites.
 Within REGEN4BE, the candidate will develop and scientifically validate interoperable digital workflows linking Building Information Modelling (BIM), Building Energy Modelling (BEM), Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA), embodied and operational carbon, circularity and material-reuse indicators, building monitoring, sensor data, Post-Occupancy Evaluation (PoE), and feedback from building operation into future design decisions.
 The methods will be developed and tested through the REGEN4BE Fribourg demonstration activities, using Smart Living Lab data and infrastructure in close collaboration with the Building2050 team.
 As an integrated strand of the doctoral thesis, the candidate will apply and adapt the REGEN4BE framework to selected earth-block and Limestone Calcined Clay Cement (LC3)-based housing systems in African contexts. Building on SONO’s projects and partnerships, this research will examine how local materials, passive environmental strategies, construction processes, whole-life carbon, circularity, repairability, measured building performance and residents’ experience can inform regenerative design.
 The European and African research strands will form one coherent doctoral project. The candidate will contribute to a generic interoperability framework within REGEN4BE and assess its transferability and necessary adaptation across different materials, climates, construction cultures and levels of digital infrastructure.
 Main duties and responsibilities 
 As a PhD Student, you will take scientific responsibility for developing and completing your doctoral dissertation, formulate original research questions, and establish a rigorous methodology. You will conduct computational, experimental and field-based research in collaboration with academic, technical, institutional, software-development and industry partners. Your responsibilities will include collecting, managing, analysing and interpreting quantitative and qualitative data, preparing articles for peer-reviewed journals, presenting findings at conferences, workshops and project meetings, contributing to REGEN4BE deliverables, demonstrations and dissemination activities, and participating in teaching and, where appropriate, the supervision of student projects.
 Within REGEN4BE, you will contribute to the development and scientific validation of the Regenerative Design Intelligence Platform (REDIP) and its building-data and performance-assessment workflows. You will develop and test interoperable methods linking BIM, openBIM and IFC with building-energy models, Life-Cycle Assessment, whole-life-carbon calculations, circularity indicators, monitoring data, occupant feedback and Post-Occupancy Evaluation. You will investigate data continuity, traceability, uncertainty and interoperability across the design, construction and operational phases of buildings, and define information requirements and data structures for exchanging geometry, materials, environmental indicators, measured performance and occupant feedback across digital environments.
 You will establish protocols for assessing the reliability, accuracy, completeness, reproducibility and usability of the proposed workflows. Using Smart Living Lab datasets and infrastructure, you will undertake full-scale testing, data collection, model calibration and scientific validation in Fribourg. You will compare predicted and simulated performance with measured environmental conditions and occupant experience, and collaborate with Building2050, relevant EPFL laboratories and ENAC research platforms, including PL-MTI where applicable. You will also support the scientific specification, testing and validation of APIs, connectors, data pipelines and interfaces in coordination with the project’s software-development …

 Our team and mission 
 The End-To-End Systems Engineering Division (TEC-SE) is responsible for supporting projects for the Engineering of E2E systems, the associated security aspects, E2E systems integration/verification activities (SIV), and service preparation. To serve these functions, the Head of the End-To-End Systems Engineering Division defines and executes the associated technology developments and studies, as well as the verification and validation laboratory facilities, and supports the preparation of the relevant engineering standards.
 The E2E Systems Division consists of five sections and associated laboratory facilities:

 E2E System Comms Section.
 The role will be within the Navigation Systems Implementation and Validation Section, which provides expert advice and engineering support to ESA projects, programmes, and studies in the fields of radio navigation and Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS).
 Moonlight is one of ESA's ongoing programmes, under which a Lunar Communications and Navigation System (LCNS) constellation is being developed to provide communication and navigation services for lunar environment.
 The role includes advanced lunar navigation algorithms development capable of estimating a user's Position, Velocity, and Time (PVT) using measurements from a single navigation satellite orbiting the Moon. The resulting capability will support the provision of navigation services during the initial deployment phase of the Moonlight system, when only a single navigation satellite may be available before the full constellation is established.

 conducting research and developing innovative algorithm(s) for Position, Velocity and Time (PVT) estimation in the lunar environment using measurements (i.e. doppler and code) from a single Moonlight navigation satellite;
 developing, implementing and validating the PVT algorithm(s) through simulation and performance assessment activities;
 performing sensitivity analyses to assess the impact of key error sources, including satellite orbit determination and timing synchronisation (ODTS) and receiver clock errors;
 investigating and analysing the use of additional information sources available in the lunar environment, such as Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) and communication signals from the ESA Pathfinder satellite, to enhance navigation performance;

 Our team and mission 
 The CAVES and PANGAEA team specialises in training programmes that equip astronauts and mission developers with scientific, expeditionary and behavioural skills. items.desc:
Location 
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands 
 Our team and mission 
 The internship opportunity is within the Galileo System Engineering Unit, Galileo System Engineering Service, Galileo Project Office, in the Galileo and EGNOS Programme Department. ESA is the design authority of Galileo in support of the EU and the System Development Prime.
 Galileo is Europe’s own global navigation satellite system, providing a highly accurate, guaranteed global positioning service under civilian control. Galileo is already the most precise satellite navigation system in the world, with more than four billion users.
 Our team oversees the definition and specification of the Galileo System releases, known as System Builds, responding to increasing mission needs in terms of position accuracy, availability, integrity, assurance, robustness and emergency response. This encompasses the definition of the new Galileo Second Generation satellites (with the first batch under development), the updates of the current Galileo (1st Generation) fleet, the necessary updates of the Ground Segment, and the interface with service facilities and external entities.
 We are a multidisciplinary, enthusiastic and diverse team and work hand-in-hand with other Galileo and ESA discliplines, from radionavigation and security engineers to ground and space segment engineers.
 Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int 
 Field(s) of activity for the internship 
 Galileo is a large and complex system with hundreds of functions, thousands of requirements, and an infrastructure distributed across the whole world. Galileo has new system releases and updates coming on a yearly basis. Implementation of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning tools at System Level is a priority for the Galileo Programme in order to ensure knowledge transfer, modelling of current and future evolutions of the Galileo System and fast data access for decision-making processes (design, qualification and anomaly resolution).
 As a means to manage this complexity, the Galileo System Engineering team has put in place a Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) approach linking those functions to one another in a graphical manner. The MBSE system model is available to the full Project team: from engineers and testers to security accreditors and managers. This system model opens up new opportunities to link all the design elements and artefacts with their verification and validation across the whole lifecycle. Linking all design aspects will improve the system design and behavioural understanding by our Project team, and will maximise the success of its deployment.
 Elements to be linked with the system model range from requirements, analyses and simulations, to performance prediction and early validation and finally, to real measurements. 
 It is a massive amount of data to connect and we believe that artificial intelligence/machine learning can help in this endeavour. This is part of a growing trend in Systems Engineering known as AI-for-Systems Engineering, or AI4SE.
 As an intern, you will have the following tasks:
 exploring the AI4SE (AI-for-Systems Engineering) approach in the context of the Galileo MBSE system model;
 defining and implementing practical use cases in which artificial intelligence and machine learning enable the MBSE system model to be queried, expanded and connected to other databases (requirements, simulations, test results, configuration, field measurements) in a better, and more efficient way;
 developing Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning tools, methodologies, scripts and digital threads to support these capabilities.
 In these tasks, you will engage with state-of-the-art Galileo professionals from ESA and industry. This would allow our Project team to digitally navigate through the system design seamlessly and minimise the risks associated with developing and deploying new Galileo system releases.

 Our team and mission 
 ​​The Ground Systems Engineering and Innovation Department is responsible for all the ground systems engineering and support activities required to support mission operations and implement innovation.

 Field(s) of activity for the internship 
 You can choose among the following topics: 
 1) Topic 1: Data Foundation Platform Adoption for Missions Operations 
Spacecraft and their associated ground data systems generate vast amounts of data during the monitoring and control process. This data is stored, processed, and analysed within the mission operations ground segment to ensure spacecraft health, correlate events, and support the development of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms. The Data Foundation Platform is a key initiative supporting the digital transformation of mission operations through trusted, governed, and accessible data. As the platform continues to evolve, increasing awareness, user engagement, and adoption across mission teams is critical to ensuring that its capabilities deliver value to the organisation.
In this topic, you will explore the Agency's data foundations and structures, focusing on how governed and accessible data can enable advanced mission operations, analytics, and AI. You will contribute to data governance activities related to data ownership, quality, lineage, accessibility, and compliance, while supporting the adoption of the Data Foundation Platform. Collaborating closely with operational teams and stakeholders, you will identify new use cases, help onboard data products and datasets, and assess how data-driven solutions can address operational challenges. Through this experience, you will gain hands-on experience with modern data platform concepts, stakeholder engagement, data engineering practices, and the promotion of data-driven innovation within mission operations.
You are invited to express your interest in specific areas of the topic. 
 2) Topic 2: Artificial Intelligence for Space Operations 
 Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming a key technology in modern spacecraft operations applications. It is highly relevant to support automation, correlate data and execute pattern recognition and even enable digital assistants for operators, helping them operate the spacecraft and ground systems, including ground stations. 
As part of this topic, you will contribute to the AI programme of the Directorate. 
Spacecraft and ground segment operations still depend heavily on manual expert effort: interpreting telemetry, judging when something needs attention, working out what to do about it, and writing up the outcome. AI offers a way to support each of these steps and, more importantly, to connect them.
 A system able to recognise unusual or degrading behaviour in telemetry can pass that insight downstream to planning and scheduling tools, which propose and sequence candidate actions; those actions, in turn, can be tested and refined against simulation engines (whose fidelity and representativeness can themselves have been enhanced with AI and digital twin solutions), closing the loop back to a sharper read on system state and better-informed decisions. None of this is useful, though, if it stays locked inside modelling pipelines that only specialists can query: generative AI, spanning text, code, and other modalities, can turn telemetry, engineering documentation, and analysis outputs alike into structured knowledge that operators interact with directly: asking questions in natural language, generating reports and summaries, or even drafting supporting code or configuration, rather than assembling insights by hand across disconnected tools.
 The internship will explore how these strands …

The programme aims to promote the standardisation of seamless global connectivity for various industries and applications, including telemedicine, autonomous vehicles, aviation and maritime services. 
As an intern, you will work in a dynamic and multidisciplinary environment at ESA's European Centre for Space Applications and Telecommunications (ECSAT) in the United Kingdom. You will engage with experts in satellite communications, artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and emerging digital technologies through activities associated with the AI Hub and the 5G/6G Hub. These centres provide facilities for innovation, experimentation and demonstration activities aimed at enabling seamless global connectivity.
 Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int 
 Field(s) of activity for the internship

Depending on your interests and background, your activities may include:
 supporting technical studies on future communication network architectures, services and applications;
 developing and evaluating AI models for communication systems and network management;
 experimenting with mixed reality technologies, robotics and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) as part of use-case development;
 assisting with the preparation, execution and analysis of trials and technology demonstrations;
 contributing to the development and operation of the AI Hub and the 5G/6G Hub;
 supporting workshops, demonstrations and engagement activities involving industry and academic partners.
 You will also have the flexibility to define and pursue your own research project within the team's areas of activity. Through this internship, you will gain practical experience in satellite-enabled connectivity, future networks and AI, while developing skills in research, experimentation, systems engineering and stakeholder engagement in an international and multidisciplinary environment.

 Field(s) of activity for the internship 
 Topic of the internship: AI-based Automation of Product Assurance and Quality Engineering 
 Product Assurance activities increasingly rely on information distributed across multiple repositories and tools, including Jira, Confluence, Git-based repositories, SonarQube, software release documentation, and configuration management systems. As projects grow in complexity, a significant amount of effort is devoted to repetitive activities such as collecting metrics, reviewing documentation, preparing reports, verifying data consistency, assessing quality, and consolidating information from different sources.
 This internship will investigate how recent advances in Artificial Intelligence and Automation can be applied to support and automate process assurance and software quality. You will analyse existing workflows and identify areas where AI can provide benefits in terms of efficiency, quality, consistency, and traceability. Particular attention will be given to activities such as the automatic creation of Jira tickets from user inputs, engineering artefacts or meeting outputs, the generation of Scrum sprint summaries, the production of software release notes, the assessment of Jira ticket completeness and quality, the extraction and interpretation of software quality metrics from SonarQube, and the verification of the completeness and consistency of software release documentation. Additional investigations may include auditing Configuration Item Data Lists (CIDLs) and Verification Control Documents (VCDs), analysing compliance with established processes, identifying inconsistencies between documentation and project repositories, and developing AI-driven assistants capable of supporting Product Assurance engineers in their daily activities.

items.desc: Intern in the Galileo and Egnos Programme Department - AI for Galileo System Engineering and MBSE Job Requisition ID: 20998 Date Posted: 1 November 2026 Closing Date: 30 November 2026 23:59 CET/CEST Publication Method: External Only Type of Appointment (learn more): Directorate: Resilience, Navigation and Connectivity Workplace: Noordwijk, NL Location ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands Our team and mission The internship opportunity is within the Galileo System Engineering Unit, Galileo System Engineering Service, Galileo Project Office, in the Galileo and EGNOS Programme Department. ESA is the design authority of Galileo in support of the EU and the System Development Prime. Galileo is Europe’s own global navigation satellite system, providing a highly accurate, guaranteed global positioning service under civilian control. Galileo is already the most precise satellite navigation system in the world, with more than four billion users. Our team oversees the definition and specification of the Galileo System releases, known as System Builds, responding to increasing mission needs in terms of position accuracy, availability, integrity, assurance, robustness and emergency response. This encompasses the definition of the new Galileo Second Generation satellites (with the first batch under development), the updates of the current Galileo (1st Generation) fleet, the necessary updates of the Ground Segment, and the interface with service facilities and external entities. We are a multidisciplinary, enthusiastic and diverse team and work hand-in-hand with other Galileo and ESA discliplines, from radionavigation and security engineers to ground and space segment engineers. Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int Field(s) of activity for the internship Galileo is a large and complex system with hundreds of functions, thousands of requirements, and an infrastructure distributed across the whole world. Galileo has new system releases and updates coming on a yearly basis. Implementation of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning tools at System Level is a priority for the Galileo Programme in order to ensure knowledge transfer, modelling of current and future evolutions of the Galileo System and fast data access for decision-making processes (design, qualification and anomaly resolution). As a means to manage this complexity, the Galileo System Engineering team has put in place a Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) approach linking those functions to one another in a graphical manner. The MBSE system model is available to the full Project team: from engineers and testers to security accreditors and managers. This system model opens up new opportunities to link all the design elements and artefacts with their verification and validation across the whole lifecycle. Linking all design aspects will improve the system design and behavioural understanding by our Project team, and will maximise the success of its deployment. Elements to be linked with the system model range from requirements, analyses and simulations, to performance prediction and early validation and finally, to real measurements. It is a massive amount of data to connect and we believe that artificial intelligence/machine learning can help in this endeavour. This is part of a growing trend in Systems Engineering known as AI-for-Systems Engineering, or AI4SE. As an intern, you will have the following tasks: exploring the AI4SE (AI-for-Systems Engineering) approach in the context of the Galileo MBSE system model; defining and implementing practical use cases in which artificial intelligence and machine learning enable the MBSE system model to be queried, expanded and connected to other databases (requirements, simulations, test results, configuration, field measurements) in a better, and more efficient way; developing Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning tools, methodologies, scripts and digital threads to support these capabilities. In these tasks, you will engage with state-of-the-art Galileo professionals from ESA and industry. This would allow our Project team to digitally navigate through the system design seamlessly and minimise the risks associated with developing and deploying new Galileo system releases. To serve these functions, the Head of the End-To-End Systems Engineering Division defines and executes the associated technology developments and studies, as well as the verification and validation laboratory facilities, and supports the preparation of the relevant engineering standards. The E2E Systems Division consists of five sections and associated laboratory facilities: Navigation Systems Definition Section; Navigation Systems Implementation and Validation Section; Systems Security Engineering Section; Telecommunication Systems and Techniques Section; E2E System Comms Section. The role will be within the Navigation Systems Implementation and Validation Section, which provides expert advice and engineering support to ESA projects, programmes, and studies in the fields of radio navigation and Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS). Moonlight is one of ESA's ongoing programmes, under which a Lunar Communications and Navigation System (LCNS) constellation is being developed to provide communication and navigation services for lunar environment. The role includes advanced lunar navigation algorithms development capable of estimating a user's Position, Velocity, and Time (PVT) using measurements from a single navigation satellite orbiting the Moon. The resulting capability will support the provision of navigation services during the initial deployment phase of the Moonlight system, when only a single navigation satellite may be available before the full constellation is established. Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int Field(s) of activity for the internship Advanced lunar navigation algorithms development capable of estimating PVT using measurements from a single navigation satellite orbiting the Moon. Your tasks will include: conducting research and developing innovative algorithm(s) for Position, Velocity and Time (PVT) estimation in the lunar environment using measurements (i.e. doppler and code) from a single Moonlight navigation satellite; developing, implementing and validating the PVT algorithm(s) through simulation and performance assessment activities; performing sensitivity analyses to assess the impact of key error sources, including satellite orbit determination and timing synchronisation (ODTS) and receiver clock errors; investigating and analysing the use of additional information sources available in the lunar environment, such as Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) and communication signals from the ESA Pathfinder satellite, to enhance navigation performance; evaluating the algorithm performance under different lunar operational scenarios, including the initial Moonlight deployment phase when only a single navigation satellite may be available. Based in the School of Geography and Environmental Science at the University of Southampton, you will work
items.desc: We have an exciting opportunity for a Research Fellow to join the UKRI-funded PRECISE (Precision Ecology for a Changing World) project. You will help establish Precision Ecology, which seeks to predict the effects of conservation interventions in specific ecological contexts. Moving beyond average effects, the project will predict site-specific responses to environmental management and restoration, supporting effective conservation decisions. Based in the School of Geography and Environmental Science at the University of Southampton, you will work with researchers at Southampton, the UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology (UKCEH) and the Norwegian Institute for Nature Research (NINA), and international collaborators in statistics, causal inference and ecological modelling. You will play a leading role in developing and evaluating methods for causal inference and causal prediction in ecology. Using benchmark datasets produced through ecological simulations and large observational datasets assembled by project partners, you will investigate how sampling strategies and data characteristics affect the performance of alternative causal-inference and machine-learning workflows. You will identify which approaches perform best under different conditions and translate the findings into practical guidance. You will create reproducible, open-source software, analytical workflows, tutorials and guidance. With project partners, you will develop best-practice frameworks for analysing observational datasets and designing ecological studies and monitoring programmes. The role focuses on methodological development, study design and causal prediction, rather than ecological simulation modelling. You should hold a PhD, or have equivalent professional experience, in a relevant quantitative discipline. We welcome applicants with strong causal-inference and quantitative expertise who want to apply these approaches to ecological questions. Ecological experience is desirable but not essential, provided you are willing to develop relevant ecological and spatial knowledge. You Should Have Strong quantitative-modelling skills and experience analysing complex observational data. Programming and data-analysis experience using R, Python or related software, including reproducible, well-documented workflows. Understanding of causal inference and its application to observational data. Understanding of reproducible research and Open Science principles. Evidence of independent research and communication through publications, software, reports or equivalent outputs. Excellent organisational, communication and collaborative skills. Experience in applying causal inference methods, machine learning, geospatial or ecological analysis, or high-performance computing would be advantageous. The School of Geography and Environmental Science is committed to fostering a culture of equality, diversity and inclusion. We particularly encourage applications from suitably qualified candidates belonging to groups under-represented within University academic posts, including, but not limited to, people from Black and minority ethnic groups and disabled people. We are a signatory to the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers and provide opportunities for career development and mentoring. The School offers family-friendly policies, flexi-time and flexible working. We are a Disability Confident employer and hold a Bronze Athena SWAN award. For further information, contact Dr Becks Spake at r.spake@soton.ac.uk. The expected start date of this role is 1st February 2027. In your application please include a covering letter that uses clear examples to show how your knowledge, experience and skills meet the essential criteria in the person specification.

items.desc: Overview At Zebra, we are a community of innovators who come together to create new ways of working. United by curiosity and a culture of caring, we develop smart solutions that anticipate our customer’s and partner’s needs and solve their challenges. Being part of Zebra Nation means you are seen, heard, valued, and respected. Drawing from our unique perspectives, we collaborate to deliver on our purpose. Here you are part of a team pushing boundaries today to redefine the work of tomorrow for organizations, their employees, and those they serve. You’ll have opportunities to learn and lead in a forward-thinking environment, defining your path to a fulfilling career while channeling your skills toward causes you care about—locally and globally. Come make an impact every day at Zebra. What We're Looking For We are seeking a skilled and motivated Computer Vision Engineer to join our team. In this role, you will bridge the gap between high-level machine learning research and high-performance production environments. You will be responsible for building robust SDKs, automating deployment pipelines, and ensuring our models run efficiently across a diverse hardware landscape, from edge SoCs to powerful cloud GPUs. Responsibilities SDK Development (C++) Design, develop, and maintain high-performance software development kits (SDKs) to expose computer vision capabilities to end-users and internal products. Model Deployment and Integration Port, convert, and deploy machine learning models across various hardware targets, including Qualcomm SoCs, Intel CPUs, and NVIDIA GPUs. Performance Optimization Use hardware-specific toolkits to optimize model throughput without sacrificing accuracy. Evaluation & Benchmarking Conduct rigorous testing and evaluation of models on target hardware to ensure performance metrics meet expectations. Automation Build and maintain automation scripts and CI/CD pipelines using Python to streamline the model testing and deployment life cycle. Education Bachelor's or master's degree in Computer Science, Electrotonic Engineering, or related technical field. Qualifications Deep understanding of C++14/17/20, including STL, memory management, and multi-threading. Strong ability to write clean, maintainable Python for automation, and data processing. Hands-on experience with at least one of the following frameworks: SNPE/QNN (Qualcomm) , OpenVino (Intel), TensorRT (Nvidia), TensorFlow Lite Familiarity with Docker for creating consistent development and deployment environments. Bonus Understanding Deep Learning fundamentals (CNNs, Transformers, Object Detection). Experience with model conversion and quantization (i.e. PTQ, QAT). items.desc: About us We’re building a future where property teams spend less time managing software and more time creating better places to live and work. Vessla is the next generation of agentic OS for property operations, connecting to the systems property teams already use to enable bleeding edge AI capabilities across all of them. Vessla’s agents find the information that matters, apply each organization’s operating rules and carry out work through connected software. The hard part is making this work reliably. That means deep integrations, a detailed understanding of each business, rigorous evaluation and clear boundaries on what agents can do. Our founding team brings experience building and deploying advanced AI systems at QuantumBlack, McKinsey, NASA, Andon Labs and Legora, to tackle that challenge. The role Join our early team and help define how AI agents get used in an industry that shapes everyday life. You’ll have a direct hand in what we build, how it works and how customers experience it, with the scope to take an idea from a user conversation all the way into production. You will get a chance to work on: Agent infrastructure: Build the orchestration and tools that let agents carry out complex work reliably Integrations and data models: Connect the software and information that building operations depend on Agentic evaluation systems: Develop ways to test agent behavior, understand failures and improve performance Customer discovery: Work directly with end-users to uncover problems worth solving and test solutions Product and design: Shape an interface that makes powerful capabilities intuitive and gives users visibility and control You’ll take meaningful ownership from the start, with room to shape your focus around your strengths, interests and the problems where you can make the greatest difference. Our stack includes Python, TypeScript, Langfuse, AWS and TanStack. Who we’re looking for You’ve built LLM systems and understand where, and why, they fail You enjoy talking to users and turning their problems into thoughtful product decisions You care about building maintainable software while moving quickly You bring ideas, challenge assumptions and take the initiative to try things out We keep the path from idea to working product short. items.desc: Reference:*****CSHAMRE1Job title:Research Engineer - HPC memory systems (RE1)About BSCThe Barcelona Supercomputing Center - Centro Nacional de Supercomputación (BSC-CNS) is the leading supercomputing center in Spain. It houses MareNostrum, one of the most powerful supercomputers in Europe, was a founding and hosting member of the former European HPC infrastructure PRACE (Partnership for Advanced Computing in Europe), and is now hosting entity for EuroHPC JU, the Joint Undertaking that leads large-scale investments and HPC provision in Europe. The mission of BSC is to research, develop and manage information technologies in order to facilitate scientific progress. BSC combines HPC service provision and R&D into both computer and computational science (life, earth and engineering sciences) under one roof, and currently has over **** staff from 60 countries. Look at the BSC experience: [BSC-CNS YouTube Channel](#) [Let's stay connected with BSC Folks!](#) We are particularly interested for this role in the strengths and lived experiences of women and underrepresented groups to help us avoid perpetuating biases and oversights in science and IT research. In instances of equal merit, the incorporation of the under-represented sex will be favoured. We promote Equity, Diversity and Inclusion, fostering an environment where each and every one of us is appreciated for who we are, regardless of our differences. If you consider that you do not meet all the requirements, we encourage you to continue applying for the job offer. We value diversity of experiences and skills, and you could bring unique perspectives to our team.Context And MissionThe Memory Systems group in the Computer Science Department at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center is offering a full-time research engineer position for a project that explores advanced memory systems for AI applications. The performance of AI models is typically limited by the memory wall. In this project, we aim to (re)move this wall by designing memory systems tailored to the requirements of AI models. We will explore systems based on HBM, DDR, GDDR devices, and Compute Express Link (CXL) memory expanders.
