The successful candidate will join a UKRI-funded project testing new retrofit materials and manufacturing approaches at Energy House 2.0, one of the world's largest climate-controlled building research facilities. Inside its two environmental chambers, full-scale homes are tested under controlled conditions from -23°C to +53°C, with simulated wind, rain, snow and solar radiation. Working alongside the Energy House 2.0 Technical Director, you'll plan and run experiments on real buildings. That means designing test programmes; installing and managing sensor networks; carrying out in-situ measurements such as heat flux and U-values, whole-house heat transfer coefficient (HTC), airtightness and thermal imaging; and, assessing how retrofit measures change energy use, comfort and moisture risk. You'll then use that data to build, calibrate and validate building performance models, closing the gap between predicted and measured performance. You'll work directly with industry partners to test their products and systems, and turn the results into peer-reviewed publications, technical reports and clear evidence that manufacturers, stakeholders and policymakers can act on. We're looking for someone with a PhD (or equivalent postgraduate experience) in building physics, building engineering or a related field. You should have hands-on experience of experimental measurement and data analysis, and confidence with modelling or simulation tools. Above all, you'll need the collaborative skills to work across academic and industry teams. If you want your research to shape how the UK retrofits its homes, we'd like to hear from you. There are two fixed-term contracts available, one for 48 months and one for 53 months. Embark on an exciting journey at Amazon as a Specialised Software Development Engineer! Join our cutting-edge teams working on innovative technologies that impact millions of customers worldwide. 
Shape the future of autonomous systems at Amazon! Join elite teams developing cutting-edge robotics and computer vision solutions that power Prime Air drones and revolutionize warehouse automation. Collaborate with world-class engineers and scientists to build and deploy state-of-the-art systems that push the boundaries of what's possible in robotics and computer vision. Your work will directly impact millions of customers and transform industries on a global scale
Applicants will be reviewed on a rolling basis and are matched to teams aligned with their experience plus location and availability preferences prior to interviews. Applicants will remain under consideration until we have assessed all potential team matches or finished recruiting. 
Key job responsibilities
Job Description
As a SLAM Intern, you will join our team to advance the localization and mapping capabilities of our last-mile delivery robot. Your work will directly shape how our robot perceives and navigates complex urban environments from benchmarking existing approaches to prototyping novel algorithms and validating them on hardware. This role offers hands-on experience in spatial perception, algorithm development, and real-world deployment within a dynamic and collaborative environment. We are committed to finding and nurturing exceptional talent; our internships are a key pathway to recruiting outstanding graduates who can make a significant impact in our team.
Important Notice: For this position, we are only able to accept applications from citizens of Schengen Area countries. This restriction does not apply to ETHZ and EPFL students who are required to complete compulsory internships as part of their studies.
What you'll be doing
Work closely with senior engineers to integrate SLAM modules with hardware components and contribute ideas to enhance system robustness and accuracy.
Support the team in benchmarking, evaluating, and developing novel state-of-the-art localization and mapping algorithms for robotic applications.
Engage in continuous learning and gain exposure to recent developments from the SLAM and computer vision literature.
A day in the life
As a Specialised Software Development Engineer, you'll immerse yourself in challenging projects that push the boundaries of technology. 
Your day might involve fine-tuning perception algorithms for drone navigation, developing simulation scenarios to test edge cases in warehouse robotics, or collaborating with and learning from hardware engineers to optimize software for new sensor configurations. 
You'll work closely with as well as learn from roboticists, ML scientists, and systems engineers to solve complex challenges in autonomy and participate in design reviews for new robotic features.
- At least a BSc in Computer Science, Robotics, Engineering, or equivalent discipline.
- Previous coursework or projects related to computer vision, SLAM, or 3D geometry.
- Experience with C++ and / or Python.
- Eagerness to learn and contribute in a team environment.
- Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
- Proven experience implementing or extending SLAM systems.
- Exposure to state of the art dense visual SLAM or multi-view stereo approaches.
- Familiarity with sensor fusion techniques involving cameras, LiDAR, or IMUs.
- Knowledge of relevant frameworks or libraries such as OpenCV, GTSAM, Ceres, Eigen, or similar.
- Experience with ROS/ROS 2 and real-world robotic data collection.

items.desc:
Introduction 
 Within ASML’s EUV Factory organization in Veldhoven, the team is responsible for managing and reviewing customer infrastructure documentation required before system installation. These documents describe critical requirements related to utilities, facilities, cooling, power, and other installation interfaces. Today, reviewing and validating these large document packages is a manual process that can take up to three weeks and requires extensive expert effort. Because even small mistakes can lead to quality risks, delays, and significant costs, the team is looking for opportunities to improve both speed and accuracy. During this internship, you will explore how Artificial Intelligence can help automate document reviews and support faster, more reliable decision-making.
 Your assignment 
 In this internship, you will investigate how AI can be applied to automate the review of customer requirement documentation. You will develop a proof of concept that demonstrates how AI can identify inconsistencies, implementation errors, and review findings that currently require significant manual effort. Working closely with stakeholders across multiple teams, you will evaluate where automation adds value and where expert review remains necessary. Your main responsibilities will be:
 Develop a proof of concept for AI-supported document review
 Build Python-based solutions to detect inconsistencies and errors
 Evaluate which review activities can be automated and which require expert input
 Validate the performance and reliability of AI-generated review results
 Collaborate with stakeholders to gather requirements and feedback
 Deliver recommendations for scaling and implementing the solution
 This is a bachelor/master (non-thesis) internship for minimum 5 months, minimum 4 days per week (4 days on-site, flexibility where needed). The start date of this internship is as of February 2027.
 Your profile 
 To be suitable for the internship, you:
 Are pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Software Engineering, or a related field
 Have experience with Python programming
 Have knowledge of AI, machine learning, or AI-powered development tools through projects, coursework, or personal initiatives
 Are analytical, independent, and proactive in driving your work forward
 Have strong attention to detail and are comfortable working with technical documentation
 Communicate clearly in English and collaborate effectively with different stakeholders
 Other requirements you need to meet: 
 You are enrolled at an educational institute for the entire duration of the internship, and you are at least 18 years old at the start of the internship; 
 If you are a non-EU citizen, studying in the Netherlands, your university is willing to sign the documents relevant for doing an internship (i.e., Nuffic agreement); 
 You attach your cover letter with a clear motivation on why you are interested in this internship assignment in particular; 
 You need to be located in the Netherlands to be perform your internship. In case you are currently living/studying outside of the Netherlands, your application shows the willingness to relocate.

Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to access such controlled technology prior to beginning work. You will help transform complex and noisy machine data into meaningful insights that support system reliability and performance. Your work will contribute to identifying recurring failure patterns and enabling more effective failure classification. This internship offers the opportunity to combine artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data mining in a highly innovative engineering environment.
 Your assignment
 During this internship, you will develop methods to analyze machine event logs and identify patterns related to machine failures. You will design and evaluate machine learning approaches that classify failure modes and uncover valuable insights from historical machine data. The results of your work may support engineers in understanding failure behaviour across multiple systems and improving future diagnostics. 
 Your main responsibilities will be:
 Develop algorithms to clean, compress, and structure noisy machine event data.
 Identify recurring failure signatures using data mining and machine learning techniques.
 Build and evaluate supervised and unsupervised classification models.
 Validate findings using historical data and expert feedback.
 Investigate similarities and differences between failure patterns across machines.
 Assess the practical value of the proposed solution for engineering use cases.
 Present results and recommendations to engineers and researchers.
 This is a master's thesis/non-thesis internship for a minimum of 6 months, 5 days per week (3 days on-site). 
 The start date of this internship is as of February 2027 or earlier, depending on your availability.
 Your profile
 To be suitable for the internship, you:
 Are pursuing a master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Electrical Engineering, Systems & Control, or a related technical field.
 Have experience with Python and machine learning techniques.
 Have knowledge of data analysis, classification methods, feature engineering, and model evaluation.
 Are analytical and enjoy solving complex technical challenges using data.
 Are collaborative, proactive, and able to communicate technical findings clearly.
 This internship is based in the Eindhoven region of the Netherlands. You will work closely with experienced engineers and researchers while contributing to meaningful challenges in the semiconductor industry. The assignment provides an opportunity to apply your academic knowledge to real-world engineering problems and gain hands-on experience in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data-driven decision-making. If you are excited about turning complex data into actionable insights, we encourage you to apply for this internship.
 Other requirements you need to meet: 
 You are enrolled at an educational institute for the entire duration of the internship, and you are at least 18 years old at the start of the internship; 
 If you are a non-EU citizen, studying in the Netherlands, your university is willing to sign the documents relevant for doing an internship (i.e., Nuffic agreement); 
 You attach your cover letter with a clear motivation on why you are interested in this internship assignment in particular; 
 You need to be located in the Netherlands to be perform your internship. In case you are currently living/studying outside of the Netherlands, your application shows the willingness to relocate. 
 Inclusion and diversity 
 ASML is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values and respects the importance of a diverse and inclusive workforce. It is the policy of the company to recruit, hire, train and promote persons in all job titles without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, or gender identity. We recognize that inclusion and diversity is a driving force in the success of our company.

items.desc:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works.

Enterprise deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Engineer, you will partner directly with Digital Native companies to design, build and deploy AI-powered products and systems. Working alongside customer product and engineering teams, you will take ideas from early experimentation through evaluation, production launch and scale, connecting technical decisions to user experience and measurable business impact.

You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations.

This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.

This role is based in London. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees

In this role, you will:

 - Partner directly with Digital Native customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

 - Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes.

 - Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators.

 - Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.

 - Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution.

 - Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact.

 - Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback.

 - Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

 - Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting.

 - Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or production engineering—not only program or stakeholder management.

 - Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.

 - Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment.

 - Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.

 - Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.

 - Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.

 - Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous environments.

 - Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; experience in a particular industry or with OpenAI products is not required.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. items.desc:
ABOUT US
 Teton is redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology and a great product experience. As populations grow older and staff shortages increase, healthcare systems are under pressure. Our mission is to decrease the cost of healthcare while improving the quality of care.
 Our product enables care teams to intervene, prevent and operate more efficiently. Our ambient sensors in resident rooms capture activity, sleep, respiration, gait and more. These signals are used both to react fast to risk events, like falls, and for long-term health analysis, so care teams can take action.
 Teton is scaling fast, operating in the Nordics, the UK, DACH and the US. We recently raised a $20M Series A. You can expect travel to the US to meet users and team members.
 We focus relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, deploying solutions at speed that make a tangible difference for carers. We are an aspiring meritocracy, biased towards action and always striving to raise the bar. If you are driven by impact, speed and levelling up, this might be the place for you.
 The position is onsite at our office in London, United Kingdom. If you are looking for a 9-to-5 job, perform best with structure and struggle to deal with unknowns, this is not for you. We believe close collaboration within a hard-working, high-agency team enables the fastest and most efficient iteration cycles, helping us build an impactful product that healthcare professionals truly love to use.
 THE JOB
 We're looking for a talented and driven Software Engineer to join our Mobile team, building the tools that care workers rely on during every shift. Our app runs 24/7 in care facilities, delivering real-time alerts and monitoring residents. This isn't a typical app dev role. You'll work across the full stack, from React Native UI to backend infrastructure, in an environment where reliability directly impacts patient safety.
 In this role, you will focus on:
 Feature Development: Own features end-to-end, from design discussions through implementation to production rollout across multiple markets and languages.
 Reliability & Debugging: Keep our real-time alert pipeline rock-solid. Debug push notification delivery on Android and iOS, investigate ANR issues, and troubleshoot weird bugs in care environments with unreliable Wi-Fi.
 Backend, Infrastructure & Systems: Work across backend services, databases, cloud infrastructure and internal platforms to support the systems our app depends on. You will not just consume APIs; you will help shape, improve and fix the systems behind them.
 Testing & Validation: Build automated test coverage (e.g. Maestro for E2E) across a range of devices and OS versions. Validate that alerts arrive when they must.
 Developer Experience: Improve shared components, internal tooling and build pipelines so the team ships faster with fewer surprises.
 QUALIFICATIONS
 Strong TypeScript skills. This is the language for everything we build.
 Solid experience with React Native and Expo in production.
 Comfortable working across the stack: you've touched databases, queues or cloud infrastructure, not just UI.
 Experience with native iOS or Android development (Kotlin/Swift) is a strong plus, as we occasionally need to go below the managed Expo layer.
 Familiarity with real-time systems, push notifications or TanStack is a plus.
 AWS or equivalent cloud platform experience.
 Previous startup experience and/or shipping a product where you owned the outcome.
 Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work both independently and in a team.
 WHAT WE OFFER
 Participation in our warrant program (stock options).
 A small team where your decisions directly shape the product.
 A London-based office with close collaboration, no async-only culture.
 Work on software that healthcare workers depend on every day. The impact is tangible and immediate.
 JOIN OUR TEAM
 We're looking for individuals who share our vision and value ownership and entrepreneurship over a conventional job.
 At Teton, you'll have the chance to make a real impact with your work.
 If you're ready for more than just a job, come aboard and be part of our mission to transform healthcare.

They write the version of an algorithm they are most comfortable with, and Quadrants rebuilds it into kernels that run as if an expert had hand-tuned them. Performance is the
items.desc: What Quadrants is Quadrants is an open-source translation layer that turns ordinary Python into optimized machine code at runtime, across CPU (Arm64, x86) and GPU (AMDGPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan) backends. CUDA is the primary target, with x86 the strong runner-up, especially for real-time simulation. The others drive adoption and support fast prototyping for research. The ambition is explicit: build the best “Python compiler” in the world for physics and performance-critical numerical computing. We are fully committed to it, and we intend to beat leading alternatives like Nvidia Warp, Numba, or Triton. It’s a standalone project with its own roadmap, built in the open. Genesis, our physics simulator, is its first and top-priority user, the source of its hardest workloads and its benchmarks. But Quadrants is general-purpose infrastructure for anyone writing performance-critical numerical Python, not an internal tool that happens to be public. The bet: high-performance code should feel natural to write. Engineers write plain Python in a NumPy or PyTorch style, and Quadrants makes it fast. The role You own Quadrants end to end: the API, the IR and lowering, the optimization passes, the numerical primitives, and the roadmap. Our ultimate objective: engineers write for readability and maintainability, never for performance. They write the version of an algorithm they are most comfortable with, and Quadrants rebuilds it into kernels that run as if an expert had hand-tuned them. Performance is the compiler’s job, not theirs. Getting there is a frontier problem, part research and part engineering, and we intend to define the state of the art on it, relentlessly pushing the limit further. It calls for two things at once: the low-level GPU and compiler skill to make a single kernel optimal, and the ability to keep the whole system coherent as it grows. The core tradeoff is settled: usability comes first. When usability and performance collide, usability wins, unless the cost is severe. We will limit what the system supports to go fast (static shapes and fixed-size allocation baked into kernels, say), but never the convenience of the API itself. Experts who want maximum performance and full control over the generated code get lower-level escape hatches, down to inline assembly, C, or PTX. What you’ll own API & authoring experience. The surface that physics and numerical-computing engineers write against, and, as an open-source library, the product’s face to the world. Idiomatic, natural to Python users, never a separate language bolted onto Python. Clean decorators, legible constraints, sharp errors, real escape hatches. IR, lowering & backends. A stable IR that lowers to multiple backends, with room to grow and the door kept open for differentiable simulation. Today the computation graph is expressed through Quadrants’ own constructs. Recovering it automatically from ordinary Python is hard, and a long-term goal rather than today’s reality. Optimization. Turn naive code into strong execution plans: vectorization, register and shared-memory usage, barriers and atomics, cooperative threading, dead-buffer and redundant-traffic elimination, dropping needless synchronization. Move low-level optimization off users and into the platform. Primitives. Cholesky, eigendecomposition, matmul, reductions, solver kernels. Each owned with its correctness, benchmarks, and regression tracking. Watching Genesis and the compiler together. Hunt for performance wins on both sides, in Genesis and in Quadrants itself. Propose API changes that cut duplication, improve readability, and reduce platform-specific special-casing. Less to maintain, more that simply works. The project as a product. Benchmark real workloads, track performance over time, catch regressions early. Stay close to users (Genesis first), find friction and missing abstractions, drive adoption, set direction. Who you are You reason about whole systems and have taste for where complexity should live. You measure before you optimize, and you reach for memory traffic and launch overhead before FLOPs. You have opinions about API design. You write tests and benchmarks as you go, not afterward. The ground that judgment stands on: GPU. What optimal looks like and why: access patterns, registers, shared memory, barriers, atomics, threading. CPU intuition a plus. Python & API taste. Idiomatic Python. A feel for what’s natural to Python users. APIs that free users rather than constrain them. Compilers. The path from authoring to kernels (IR, lowering, optimization), weighed against maintainability. And how you work: proactive and largely self-directed. You fetch context across the company instead of waiting for it. You’re comfortable talking to the engineers who use what you build, and at ease designing in the open for users you’ll never meet. Ready to grow into leading a small team (a couple of people, near term). What great looks like People adopt Quadrants from outside Genesis. …

items.desc: WholeHelp vient d'être rachetée par Sage. Et ce n'est que le début. Avec Sage Experience, on rend l'IA accessible à tout type d'entreprise, sur de vrais cas d'usage. Pas des démos de laboratoire : interroger ses chiffres en langage naturel, automatiser les tâches qui font perdre des heures, connecter ses outils, créer des écrans sur-mesure. Le tout branché sur les logiciels de gestion Sage que les PME utilisent déjà. Nos produits SaaS sont pensés nativement pour l'IA, et ils tournent déjà chez les clients. Le poste Un assistant qui répond sur les données comptables réelles des entreprises, là où une réponse fausse a un prix. Tu le rends juste, mesurable, sûr et sobre en coûts. Et tu fais parler les données d'usage de toute la plateforme. Tu n'as pas de ligne produit : tu portes l'IA et les données de Sage Experience pour toutes les lignes. Côté IA : tu développes le cœur des modules IA qui s'appuient sur nos services MCP : Ask, l'assistant IA qui répond sur les chiffres de l'entreprise ; la création d'écrans sur-mesure ; et les workflows qui automatisent les tâches. Côté données : tu mets en place le suivi de toute la plateforme, de la collecte des données jusqu'à leur analyse. Usage des outils IA, mais aussi usage de la plateforme en général : tu as la liberté de choisir quoi mesurer et comment, pour sortir les statistiques qui aident vraiment l'équipe produit à décider. Les évaluations, le suivi des coûts et toute la chaîne de données sont à construire : c'est toi qui les poses. Ce que tu vas faire Construire les évaluations des fonctions IA, jouées dans la CI à chaque modification, pour qu'aucune évolution ne dégrade une réponse Améliorer la qualité des résultats : instructions, outils exposés aux agents, analyse des échecs et des retours utilisateurs Développer en TypeScript le cœur des modules IA : conversation et contexte, moteur des workflows, génération de pages et de documents, streaming et reprise sur erreur Tenir les garde-fous : confirmation humaine avant toute écriture dans un logiciel, journalisation de chaque appel, protection contre l'injection de prompt, isolation entre organisations Tenir les coûts et challenger les modèles : suivi de la dépense, optimisation des tokens, comparaison des modèles sur nos évaluations, opportunité de modèles auto-hébergés Mettre en place la collecte des données d'usage sur toute la plateforme : plan de marquage, schéma d'événements commun à toutes les lignes, pseudonymisé et sans contenu métier, conforme au RGPD Construire les flux et le modèle de données analytiques, de la collecte jusqu'à l'entrepôt, avec leurs contrôles de qualité Définir les indicateurs de suivi de la plateforme : adoption, activation, rétention, usage par fonctionnalité et par ligne, usage et coût des outils IA Construire les tableaux de bord et analyser les données pour sortir des statistiques utiles : ce qui marche, ce qui bloque, où investir L'équipe Tu rejoins une équipe de 10 à 15 personnes. Product Builders et développeurs travaillent ensemble au quotidien, sur une même stack : TypeScript, Node ou Bun côté serveur, React côté client. Tu travailles avec toutes les lignes produit. Toi Tu as mis en production des applications à base de grands modèles de langage : appels d'outils, agents, MCP, streaming. Tu sais dire comment tu as mesuré la qualité d'une fonction d'IA, et tes évaluations bloquent la CI quand ça régresse. Tu connais les risques : injection de prompt, y compris par les données, fuite de données. Tu confies les calculs aux outils, jamais au modèle. Tu raisonnes par la mesure sur les coûts et le choix des modèles. Tu as déjà construit une chaîne de données de bout en bout : collecte d'événements, flux, modélisation, entrepôt, tableaux de bord. Tu es solide en SQL et en modélisation analytique, à l'aise en Python ; tu définis un indicateur avant de l'écrire, et tu en connais les biais. Tu codes en TypeScript, avec des tests automatisés. Un plus : avoir servi des modèles ouverts (serveurs d'inférence, GPU), ou une première approche des données de gestion (ERP, comptabilité). Pas besoin d'être expert : l'équipe et les experts métiers sont là pour ça. Ce poste n'est pas pour toi si tu n'as jamais livré de fonction d'IA générative en production, ou jamais construit une chaîne de données jusqu'à son analyse. Ici, l'IA tourne chez de vrais clients, sur leurs vrais chiffres. Lieu du poste : Télétravail hybride (92800 Puteaux)

Réaliser une revue de littérature sur les méthodes de quantification de l'incertitude appliquées
items.desc: Vos missions au quotidien Le département Model Risk Management veille à la qualité et à la pertinence des modèles développés au sein du Groupe, ainsi qu'au suivi du risque de modèle de la banque. L'équipe est entre autres en charge de réaliser des benchmarks afin de tester les limites des modèles des entités auditées. Réaliser une revue de littérature sur les méthodes de quantification de l'incertitude appliquées aux systèmes multi-agents décisionnels fondés sur des Large Language Models (LLM), et les implémenter sur des architectures agentiques open source. Vous serez notamment amené à : Effectuer une revue de littérature sur les méthodes d'incertitude, de calibration et de propagation de l'incertitude dans les systèmes multi-agents Apprendre à manipuler des frameworks agentiques open source et construire une architecture simple composée de plusieurs agents collaboratifs Implémenter et évaluer différentes méthodes de quantification de l'incertitude afin de détecter les erreurs, anticiper les échecs et améliorer la fiabilité des décisions prises par les agents Intégration des travaux réalisés durant le stage dans le protocole de revue interne de l'équipe Documenter l'étude et animer des ateliers interactifs pour présenter les avancements aux membres de l'équipe Vous acquerrez une vision spécifique en gestion du risque de modèle au sein des établissements bancaires, ainsi qu'une expérience significative dans le domaine de la data science. Vous mettrez en exergue vos qualités rédactionnelles et de présentation. Durée du stage : 6 mois. Et si c'était vous ? Compétences requises et qualités appréciées : De formation Bac + 4/5 - École d'Ingénieurs ou équivalent universitaire, vous avez de solides connaissances théoriques et opérationnelles en Machine Learning et en Deep Learning (e.g. étapes d'apprentissage d'un modèle) Vous justifiez de bonnes connaissances en Python Doté de qualités rédactionnelles, vous savez rédiger des notes synthétiques et présenter vos résultats sous format PowerPoint ou de Web apps. Autonome, rigoureux, curieux, vous êtes force de proposition Un fort esprit d'équipe, de l'enthousiasme et un bon relationnel vous permettront de vous insérer rapidement dans l'équipe Plus qu'un poste, un tremplin Rejoignez-nous pour faire grandir vos ambitions ! Dès votre arrivée, vous serez intégré dans nos équipes et apprendrez chaque jour aux côtés de nos experts qui vous accompagneront dans vos missions. Progressivement, vous gagnerez en autonomie sur vos projets pour faire de cette expérience un vrai accélérateur de carrière. Vous découvrirez également toute la diversité de nos métiers, dans un secteur qui évolue et innove en permanence. A la fin de vos études, diverses opportunités pourront s'offrir à vous, en France et à l'international. Pourquoi nous choisir ? Attentif à votre qualité de vie et conditions de travail , vous bénéficiez d'avantages : Télétravail possible selon le rythme de votre service Prise en charge de 60% de votre titre de transport Billetterie à prix réduits de notre Comité d'Entreprise (concerts, cinéma, sport) Offre variée de restaurants d'entreprise et de cafétérias à tarifs compétitifs ainsi que des titres restaurants dématérialisés quand vous êtes en télétravail Créer, oser, innover, entreprendre font partie de notre ADN. Si vous aussi vous souhaitez être dans l'action, évoluer dans un environnement stimulant et bienveillant, vous sentir utile au quotidien et développer ou renforcer votre expertise, nous sommes faits pour nous rencontrer ! Vous hésitez encore ? Sachez que nos collaborateurs peuvent s'engager quelques jours par an pour des actions de solidarité sur leur temps de travail : parrainer des personnes en difficulté dans leur orientation ou leur insertion professionnelle, participer à l'éducation financière de jeunes en apprentissage ou encore partager leurs compétences avec une association. Les formats d'engagement sont multiples.

Gemeinsam übernehmen wir Schlüsselaufgaben in großen nationalen und europäischen Konsortien rund um unsere drei Kernbereiche: Translationale Studien & Analytik, Forschungsökosysteme und Digitale Anwendungen & Plattformen. In der Arbeitsgruppe Applied Health Data Science (Leitung: Dr. Katharina Appel) arbeitest Du an relevanten Fragestellungen mit echtem Impact. Schwerpunkte: Prädiktionsmodelle, Clinical Decision Support und LLMs. Eigene Ideen sind ausdrücklich willkommen. Wir freuen uns über Deine Bewerbung – sehr gern auch, wenn Du noch nicht „fertige:r Clinical Data Scientist“ bist und den Weg mit uns gehen möchtest. Deine Aufgaben : Eigenständige Planung und Durchführung von Forschungsprojekten inkl. Studiendesign, Ethik, Protokoll, Datenschutz. Datenkuratierung und -harmonisierung, DSGVO-konformer Umgang mit Gesundheitsdaten. Datenanalysen mit Verfahren der Statistik und Data Science sowie Interpretation der Ergebnisse. Publikationstätigkeit, Konferenzbeiträge und Förderung von Open Science/Reproduzierbarkeit. Koordination und Leitung von (Teil-)projekten inkl. Zeit- und Ressourcenplanung, SOPs und QM. Verfassen von Förderanträgen und Einwerben von Fördermitteln inkl. Arbeitspaketen, Meilensteinen und Budgetplanung. Wissens- und Technologietransfer in Klinik, Öffentlichkeit und zu Fördergebern ...ist Dein Profil gefragt Daten-, Gesundheits- oder Naturwissenschafter:in bzw. Absolvent eines verwandten Studiengangs mit abgeschlossenem Master; idealerweise mit Bezug zu medizinischen Fragestellungen. Erfahrung in wissenschaftlichem Arbeiten und Interesse an Themen der digitalen Medizin und Data Science. Kenntnisse in Statistik, Data Science und Programmierung (R, Python) Engagierte, strukturierte, selbstständige, sorgfältige Arbeitsweise und Teamfähigkeit. Sicherer Umgang mit gängigen Office-Tools. Sehr gute Sprachkenntnisse in Deutsch und Englisch (Wort und Schrift). Aufgrund gesetzlicher Bestimmungen ist ein gültiger Nachweis der Masernimmunität / Masernschutzimpfung notwendig. ...wird Dir viel geboten Tarifvertrag TV-G-U, E 13 (die Angabe bezieht sich auf eine Vollzeittätigkeit) mit einfügen 30 Tage Urlaub, 40 Stunden / Woche, Jahressonderzahlung, betriebliche Altersvorsorge Kostenloses Landesticket Hessen Forschung mit Relevanz und Gestaltungsraum: Spannende und abwechslungsreiche Tätigkeiten in einem interdisziplinären und gut vernetzten Forschungsumfeld und einer zeitgemäßen Arbeitsumgebung Gezielte Entwicklung & Mentoring mit individuellen Fortbildungsoptionen und Unterstützung bei Publikationen und Drittmittelanträgen, inkl. Kongressreisen Flexible Arbeitszeit und familienfreundliche Regelungen mit der Möglichkeit zur „Mobilen Arbeit“ (bis 50% der monatlichen Arbeitszeit) nach Absprache Vielfältige Weiterbildungsangebote über die Goethe-Uni Ein Arbeitsplatz in angenehmer Arbeitsatmosphäre in einem freundlichen und dynamischen Team Einblicke: Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn FAQ´s für neue Beschäftigte Werde ein Teil unseres Teams! items.desc: Turn complex ideas into intuitive, accessible digital experiences. Bring your Figma expertise and curiosity for AI to KPMG and help shape the future of product design. Apply today! Young professional Staff Amstelveen Your challenges As Product Designer - UI & AI Experiences in Amstelveen, you create accessible, scalable interfaces for a digital platform used across KPMG. You combine strong product-design fundamentals with curiosity about AI to turn validated user needs into intuitive, development-ready experiences within a hybrid working environment. Your challenges Translate product requirements, experience direction and validated user needs into intuitive, visually consistent interfaces for complex web applications. Develop responsive designs and interactive prototypes that cover key workflows, states and edge cases. Maintain and evolve the Figma Design System through reusable components, patterns, variables, tokens and clear documentation. Embed accessibility in interface design and review implemented functionality for visual, responsive and interaction quality. Shape understandable and trustworthy AI-enabled experiences, including user control, feedback, transparency and recovery patterns. This is what you bring You have a bachelors (required) or masters (preferred) in product design, user-interface design, interaction design, visual design, Human-Computer Interaction or a related discipline. You bring relevant experience role: at least 3 years , designing digital products or complex web applications. Your portfolio demonstrates high-quality user-interface design, responsive experiences and digital products that have been implemented and released. You have strong Figma expertise, including components, libraries, auto layout, variants and reusable patterns, and experience contributing to a Design System. You understand visual hierarchy, typography, responsive design and digital accessibility, and you can prepare detailed designs for developers and review implemented interfaces. Not sure whether to apply because you don’t meet every requirement? If this role excites you and you see yourself in the profile, we’d love to hear from you. Because we believe talent grows and shows up in many different ways. What will you do? You take hands-on ownership of interface design and Design System delivery for a digital platform that enables KPMG teams to create engaging, interactive experiences for clients and internal audiences. Working in a multidisciplinary digital product team, you translate product direction and validated user insights into detailed, scalable and development-ready experiences. You design new and existing functionality across relevant workflows, states, edge cases and screen sizes. Using Figma, you create clear interface designs and interactive prototypes that make proposed solutions tangible before development. You balance visual quality, usability, accessibility and technical feasibility, while maintaining a consistent experience across the platform. A key part of your role is evolving the product Design System. You create and improve reusable components, variants, patterns, styles, variables and design tokens, and document how they should behave and be used. This helps the team avoid unnecessary one-off solutions and makes the product easier to scale and maintain. You prepare clear specifications for development, including responsive rules, component behaviour and interaction details. During implementation, you review the resulting interfaces and identify gaps in visual consistency, responsiveness, interaction quality and accessibility early enough to resolve them effectively. As the platform introduces more AI-enabled capabilities, you also help shape experiences such as guided creation, recommendations, intelligent assistance and AI-supported editing. You prototype emerging concepts and create interaction patterns that make AI functionality understandable, useful and trustworthy, with appropriate transparency, user control, feedback, correction and error handling. Experience with software-as-a-service (SaaS), enterprise applications, HTML and CSS, browser-based design quality assurance, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, or AI-assisted design and prototyping tools is beneficial. Direct experience designing AI-enabled functionality is an advantage, but strong product-design fundamentals and a clear interest in developing this capability are equally valuable. This is what we offer Gross salary between €3,100 and €4,700 per month depending on your work experience, variable performance based reward, a fixed expense allowance and a fixed working from home allowance per working day. Pension accrual without a compulsory personal contribution. 30 vacation days (on a full-time basis) and the option to buy more days or sell your vacation days. At KPMG we work hybrid, so you can work from home, from the client or at the office. A completely furnished home office. Reimbursement of your travel …

items.desc: Job description As an applicant, you are expected to build cortex-inspired neural networks for problems in semi-supervised and unsupervised learning. Your primary responsibilities will involve implementation and optimization on various hardware platforms, including neuromorphic hardware. The goal of this work is to develop brain-like network architectures and carry out high-performance, large-scale implementations. Your responsibilities will include studying relevant literature, designing and simulating large-scale neural network models on various hardware platforms, including neuromorphic hardware. You will also be expected to actively participate in academic discussions with advisors at KTH and to write scientific articles. Qualifications Requirements A doctoral degree at advanced level (higher education) in Computer Science or a related field. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made. As an applicant, you should have strong programming skills and the ability to develop scalable code for running on supercomputers. You should also have a deep understanding of artificial intelligence and machine learning, particularly regarding neural networks. It is essential that you are knowledgeable and well-informed about issues related to diversity and equal opportunity, with a particular focus on gender equality. Applicants must have a good command of English and strong verbal and written communication skills, since this is required in the daily work. Preferred qualifications We would prefer that you have prior experience developing and simulating large-scale brain-like neural networks with local learning rules. It is advantageous if you have strong collaborative skills and can also demonstrate independence in research and development. Knowledge of and proficiency in GPU programming, as well as experience running large-scale computational simulations, are desirable qualifications. Furthermore, we would prefer that you have teaching ability and prior experience of developing and leading activities and staff. Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills. Join us at KTH KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority. Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH. Trade union representatives Contact information to trade union representatives. You are responsible to ensure that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad. The application must include: CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge. Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages. Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Max two pages long. Your complete application must be received by KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time). About the employment The employment is valid for a limited time according to the agreement - for up to 6 months, with access according to agreement. If this applies to the specific position, a security clearance will be conducted for the applicant in accordance with the same law with the applicant's consent. In such cases, a prerequisite for employment is that the applicant is approved following the security clearance. items.desc: Tessl is a fast-growing Series A startup based in London, founded by Guy Podjarny, who previously founded Snyk. We’ve raised more than $100 million from world-class investors, including Index Ventures, Accel, GV and Boldstart. In 2025, Tessl ranked #2 in Sifted’s B2B SaaS Rising 100 and #20 in its AI 100. We’re building the context layer for AI coding agents and a platform for AI-native software development. As an early member of the team, you’ll help shape how we build and scale a company operating at the forefront of AI and software development. Overview of the role We're hiring a Research Engineer to join our AI Research (AIR) team. You'll work on the components that make the outer loop real: how agent harnesses orchestrate model behaviour, how we evaluate what's actually working, how pipelines turn production traces into the next round of improvement, and how we diagnose the failure modes that matter to real users. These aren't four separate workstreams — they're parts of one system, and we want people who see them that way. We expect you to sit close to customers — joining calls, watching sessions, reading traces — and to let real workflows shape your research priorities. You'll have meaningful autonomy and the resources to run substantial experiments where the bar for success is shipped impact. You'll report to our AI Research Lead, and collaborate closely with engineering, product, and design. What we're looking for We're explicitly building coverage across four skill areas. You don't need to be strong in all of them — but you should bring depth in at least one: Agent harness and orchestration design — how tools, context, and control flow combine to make a useful agent. Agentic eval methodology — task and repo-level evals, dataset curation, the craft of measuring what actually matters. Outer-loop and pipeline thinking — feedback loops, training-data flywheels, bandit-style optimisation, anything that goes beyond a single agent session. Failure-mode analysis — instrumenting agents, reading traces at volume, surfacing patterns engineering can act on. Essential 4+ years shipping AI/ML products in a startup or applied industry setting, with recent hands-on experience with LLMs and agentic systems. Demonstrated depth in at least one of the four skill areas above. Strong product and customer instincts: comfort joining customer calls, watching session recordings, and letting real workflows shape what you work on. Sharp evaluation judgement: benchmarks where they exist, vibes and quick prototypes where they don't, and the taste to know which is appropriate. Experience building datasets for evaluation or training, including the pipeline work that goes with it. Deeply curious about agents and excited about reshaping how software is built. Nice to have A Masters or PhD in a relevant computational field. Direct experience with coding agents or code-generation systems. Background in RL, bandits, or other outer-loop optimisation frameworks applied to LLMs. Experience building synthetic data, dataset infrastructure, or internal tooling that other engineers actually used. A project you can show us (GitHub links welcome) and a thoughtful answer to "Why Tessl?" What you'll do No two weeks will look the same. A flavour: Sit in on a customer session, understand how their agents are failing, design an eval that captures it, and drive a fix through to shipped improvement. Close a piece of the outer loop end to end: production signal in, dataset out, eval scored, harness change shipped, metric moved. Own a slice of our eval infrastructure: dataset curation, harness configuration, runner, analysis, and the comms back to engineering. Prototype a new harness or context configuration and measure whether it actually moves the needle on real customer tasks. Dig through pages of agent traces, build the tooling you need to make sense of them, and brief the team on what you found. Partner with product and engineering on near-term shipping problems by bringing research rigour. Pull a recent paper apart, work out what's actually transferable to our platform, and turn it into a concrete experiment. You’ll be successful if… In your first 3 months, you might have shipped a new eval suite for a real customer workflow, improved an agent harness based on trace analysis, or built a pipeline that turns production failures into reusable test cases. Salary and benefits Competitive salary commensurate with experience. Health insurance extending to partners and dependents, pension contributions, and the rest of what you'd expect. Our office is a couple of minutes from King's Cross — pet friendly, with regular team lunches, drinks, and socials. We're hybrid, with Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday as the primary in-office days. Application process Intro call to understand "Why Tessl?" and to tell you a bit about us. A call with our AI Research Lead to understand your ways of working and how you use agents. A 4 hour technical take-home exercise …

You care about code modularity, structure and aesthetics and have firsthand experience in how software is built across teams and environments Equally comfortable contributing to a mature codebase with strict CI criteria or hacking up a quick prototype to prove/disprove an assumption Proven experience leveraging the best AI coding tools and agents to accelerate and enhance your own work and efficiency Comfortable with fast-paced, high-autonomy environments: you’ve ideally thrived in an early-stage startup before You have demonstrated usage of AI tools in your day-to-day work , and be excited about experimenting, learning, and harnessing the potential of new AI tools and approaches to transform software engineering Nice to have Background in AI products or developer tools Experience in rapid prototyping environments Programming polyglot experienced in several languages of different paradigms (e.g.: JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, C or C++, Haskell, etc.) Experience collaborating with AI researchers and bridging between research-focused and engineering-focused teams Experience building & scaling REST APIs , particularly those conforming to JSON:API Comfortable working on infrastructure (e.g., setting up CI pipelines, navigating Kubernetes) If you have a personal or open-source project you’d like to share, we’d love to see it (GitHub links welcome!) Salary and benefits Office: Our brand new 10,000 sq. ft office is in the AI hub of Kings Cross, London. We have generous catering and have regular social events such as team lunches, drinks and more. We require all staff to be in our London HQ at least 3 days a week on our anchor days of Monday, Tuesday and Thursday. Benefits : 25 days holiday, health insurance, including dental and vision, which extends to partners and dependents, as well as a company-matched pension. We also provide a commuting stipend for those who live outside London, and a cycle to work scheme. We care deeply about the warm, inclusive environment we’re building at Tessl and we value diversity – we welcome applications from those typically underrepresented in tech. items.title: Specialist in Emergency Medicine
items.card: you will be working alongside our 17 Consultants in Emergency Medicine and a strong team of Speciality Doctors and Speciality Trainees providing clinical services to the Mansfield, Ashfield, Newark, and surrounding areas in Nottinghamshire from two trust sites, King’s Mill Hospital in Sutton-in-Ashfield, and Newark Hospital in Newark. You will be fully supported in your day to day working within a team where we have
items.desc: We are looking for a motivated and committed individual to join a forward-thinking organisation, which is committed to providing healthier communities and outstanding care for all. Providing outstanding care, promoting health and wellbeing whilst continuously learning and improving are just some of our strategic objectives in our five-year plan, with these in mind if you are looking for an exciting opportunity to join our friendly and supportive Emergency Department then look no further. If successful you will be working alongside our 17 Consultants in Emergency Medicine and a strong team of Speciality Doctors and Speciality Trainees providing clinical services to the Mansfield, Ashfield, Newark, and surrounding areas in Nottinghamshire from two trust sites, King’s Mill Hospital in Sutton-in-Ashfield, and Newark Hospital in Newark. You will be fully supported in your day to day working within a team where we have a full complement of substantive Registered Nurses, Health Care Assistants and Admin and Clerical staff. We also have a highly motivated team of Advanced Clinical Practitioners and Emergency Nurse Practitioners. We offer plenty of opportunities to become involved in teaching and audit and we have regular cohorts of medical students who require training for critical illness and musculoskeletal modules. We also run in-house ALS/ATLS/EPLS and Ultrasound courses that attract attendees from across the region. The over-riding purpose is to support the provision of the highest quality patient care through personal actions and continuous improvement. Whilst on duty a doctor has clinical and professional responsibility for their patients. It is also the duty of a doctor to: Keep patients (and/or their carers if appropriate) informed about their condition. Involve patients (and/or their carers if appropriate) in decision making about their treatment. Maintain professional standards and obligations as set out from time to time by the General Medical Council (GMC) and comply with GMC’s guidance on ‘Good Medical Practice’ as amended or substituted from time to time. A doctor is responsible for carrying out any work related to and reasonably incidental to the duties set out in the Job Plan such as: The keeping of records and the provision of reports. The proper delegation of tasks. Maintaining skills and knowledge. Doctors will be expected to be flexible and to cooperate with reasonable requests to cover for their colleagues’ absence where they are safe and competent and where it is practicable to do so. You would be joining a multi award winning team (HSJ Winner for Emergency Care in 2017, 1 st place Royal College of Emergency Medicine, Improvement Project of the Year 2018, HSJ Patient Safety shortlist for Best Partnership Solution for improving patient safety in 2019), who were graded as Outstanding for Leadership in the latest Care Quality Commission assessment in 2018. Consistently providing examples of best practice and excellence, the team is proud to have been featured in several NHSI and ECIST information videos. The Emergency Department performs well against the 4-hour and our Ambulance Turn Around target and is consistently within the top 20 Trust’s nationally for our performance. We are a level 2 trauma unit and actively contribute to the regional trauma network. We run a single front door model where we have 24/7 co-located primary care service, where we stream circa 20-22% of attendances from ED to primary care. We have a fully integrated frailty and discharge service at our front door, including therapy and social care. Our new, recently built Same Day Emergency Care Unit (SDEC) running 7am – midnight 7 days a week supports the Emergency Department with several pathways supporting admission avoidance and improving flow throughout. Our highly regarded High Intensity Service User programme is led by Nurse Specialists and supported with Consultant input to work with patients who frequently attend ED with the aim in reducing the frequency they use the service. Please see the attached job description and person specification for a full outline of the main duties and responsibilities

items.desc: Are you a caring, enthusiastic and hard working person looking to make a big impact? We are looking for dedicated and caring Radiology Department assistants to support our Community sites. This role will be based at Haslemere Community Hospital, Milford Community Hospital and Cranleigh Village Hospital when required. The post holder therefore needs to have a car and a valid driving licence. This is a patient focused role. You will assist out-patients during their time in the radiology department from transferring the patients to and from the departments, greeting them on arrival, assisting with their preparation for the examinations, and helping to provide a pleasant experience. You will also take on some admin roles which may include, booking patients in for the appointment, stock management and room preparation for Ultrasound, and X ray examinations. Training for all will be provided. You should have excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to work well within a team. Enrolment in Care Certificate training will be included. Royal Surrey is a compassionate and collaborative acute and community Trust. Recognising that our 5,000 colleagues are our greatest strength, we offer a comprehensive health and wellbeing programme alongside a strong commitment to developing your career. Our diverse and welcoming Royal Surrey family ensures you feel valued from your initial interview and throughout your time with us. We are clinically led and provide joined-up care by bridging hospital and community services, alongside delivering regional specialist cancer care. Our main acute hospital site is in Guildford, with community sites at Milford, Haslemere and Cranleigh, and services delivered in patients’ homes across Guildford and Waverley. We work in partnership with Ashford & St Peter’s Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust through a collaborative Group Model, supporting joined-up services, workforce flexibility and development opportunities. The Care Quality Commission (CQC) has rated us as Outstanding. We are proud of our achievements and continue to invest in our people and infrastructure. To learn more about life at Royal Surrey, please watch our short video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R96pMboIYdo Adverts may close early, so you are encouraged to apply as soon as possible. The Radiology Department Assistant will provide a high-quality support service to the Radiology team across three community sites, ensuring the smooth, safe, and efficient delivery of diagnostic imaging services. The post holder will support patients throughout their visit while maintaining a professional, compassionate, and patient-centred approach

items.desc: About EDITED EDITED is the world’s leading AI-driven retail intelligence platform. We empower the world’s most successful brands and retailers with real-time decision making power. By connecting internal business and external market data, EDITED infuses intelligence into every retail decision. We help retailers increase margins, generate more sales, and drive better business outcomes through AI-powered market and enterprise intelligence that fuels automation. At EDITED, we foster a dynamic and inclusive culture where creativity thrives and collaboration is at the heart of everything we do. Our environment is dynamic and supportive, encouraging team members to take initiative, innovate, and continuously grow. We value diversity, transparency, and a shared commitment to excellence, creating a workplace where everyone's voice is heard and contributions are recognised. We believe that achieving a positive work-life balance is key to driving innovation and success. Our flexible working options—including hybrid working, flexible hours and a work from anywhere policy—empower our team to perform at their best. The Opportunity We're seeking a motivated and curious Junior Data Scientist to join our team. In this role, you'll work alongside experienced data scientists and engineers to deliver actionable insights and build data-driven solutions across EDITED. You'll learn key methodologies, contribute to impactful projects, and develop your technical and analytical skills in a supportive environment. What You'll Do As A Junior Data Scientist: Deliver Data Science Projects: Assist in designing, building, and maintaining data science models and pipelines to solve core business problems. Data Analysis & Exploration: Analyze complex datasets to extract meaningful insights, trends, and patterns supporting retail intelligence. Collaborate & Learn: Work closely with senior team members, receiving mentorship and feedback to continuously refine your technical skills. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with product and engineering teams to integrate data products into production systems. Maintain Data Quality: Validate and clean data sources to ensure high reliability and consistency across models and reporting. Solid understanding of foundational data science concepts and statistical methods. Proficiency with Python and standard data science libraries (e.g. Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-Learn). Strong problem-solving ability and enthusiasm for learning new technologies. Clear written and verbal communication skills. Curiosity to learn in an ever changing, fast paced environment. What We’re Looking For In A Junior Data Scientist It’s important for us to look for candidates that strive for excellence with a positive attitude, a strong sense of ownership and work ethic, and a passion to consistently develop and improve their knowledge and skillset. If you’re excited about the role of Junior Data Scientist and the opportunity to work at EDITED, we encourage you to apply even if you only match some, rather than all, of the requirements. Essential : 1+ years of experience (or strong academic/project background) in data analysis or machine learning. Good working knowledge of Python. Understanding of core machine learning concepts and statistical analyses. This year, we were recognised as one of the top companies to work for in the UK. You can utilise our flexible working policy to ensure you can work around your schedule - this means starting & finishing when it suits you best! AWS, Azure o GCP); Conoscenza dei framework di AI Governance, con attenzione a etica, bias detection e fairness, e capacità di operare nel rispetto delle principali normative e linee guida di compliance (es. GDPR, AI Act); GROW YOUR CAREER WHERE TECHNOLOGY MEETS OPPORTUNITY Dai alla tua carriera l’accelerata che sta aspettando: fai l’application ed entra in una realtà unica nel suo genere. items.desc: About Reply: Reply specialises in designing and implementing solutions based on new communication channels and digital media. Structured as a network of highly specialised companies, Reply supports leading European industrial groups in sectors such as Telco & Media, Industry and Services, Banking and Insurance, and Public Administration, helping define and develop business models enabled by new paradigms such as AI, Cloud Computing, Digital Media, and the Internet of Things. Reply’s services include Consulting, System Integration, and Digital Services. Role Overview: As a Graduate AI & Cloud Consultant at Go Reply, you will step into a versatile role that bridges the gap between high-level business strategy and cutting-edge cloud innovation. You will be instrumental in supporting our clients to stay at the forefront of technology by optimising their digital strategies and solving complex business challenges. You will work alongside a diverse team of specialists across data science, security, and platform engineering to build highly resilient and scalable solutions based on Google Cloud Platform. From day one, you will be immersed in a vibrant work environment where you’ll help integrate Cloud and AI technologies into some of the world’s largest organisations across sectors as varied as retail, telecommunications, government, and sport. Beyond project work, the role is defined by a culture of continuous learning and community. You will sharpen your skills through extensive training opportunities, including GCP certifications, as well as participation in Hackathons, Code Challenges, and Lab Camps. We are hiring for Summer/ Autumn 2027! Responsibilities: Designing and implementing solutions leveraging Google Cloud data analytics, AI and machine learning capabilities. Working closely with them to understand their business needs and design tailored solutions that leverage the power of Google Cloud Platform. Building and managing our customers' cloud environments to enable application deployments on GCP. Conducting client-facing presentations and effectively communicating technical concepts and solutions to stakeholders. Collaborating with cross-functional teams to ensure delivery excellence and adherence to project timelines and quality standards. Engaging in requirements gathering, workshop delivery, stakeholder management and data and business analysis. Producing consistently high quality deliverables which are compelling, accurate, and engaging both to clients and your team. Contributing to the development and enhancement of Go Reply's internal offerings, including best practices, methodologies, and knowledge sharing assets. About the Candidate: A Bachelor's degree (2.1 or higher) is required in IT, Computer Science or in a Technology-related field. Excellent communications skills, with an impact at any level of the organisation. A passion for technology and a strong interest in becoming a cloud specialist. We expect a familiarity and competency with modern programming languages and software engineering practices. London based, office role. Flexibility regarding local travel. Reply is an Equal Opportunities Employer and committed to embracing diversity in the workplace. We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type regardless of age, sexual orientation, gender, identity, pregnancy, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, disability, medical history, skin colour, marital status or parental status or any other characteristic protected by the Law. items.desc: Trainee AI Engineer Locatie: Rijswijk Uren: Fulltime maar bespreekbaar Opleidingsniveau: HBO / WO Salaris: Afhankelijk van kennisniveau Ben jij nieuwsgierig naar AI en zie je meteen wanneer iets slimmer kan? Wil je begrijpen hoe een organisatie werkt én zelf bouwen aan oplossingen die collega’s dagelijks helpen? Start als Trainee AI Engineer bij Aethon en ontwikkel je op het snijvlak van technologie en business. Jouw uitdaging Een recruiter die steeds dezelfde informatie overneemt. Een planning waarvoor collega’s meerdere systemen moeten raadplegen. Of een rapportage die iedere week opnieuw handmatig wordt samengesteld. Jij wilt weten: waarom doen we dit zo, en kan het beter? Als Trainee AI Engineer onderzoek je samen met collega’s hoe onze bedrijfsprocessen werken. Je stelt vragen, brengt knelpunten in kaart en vertaalt die naar praktische toepassingen met AI en automatisering. Daarbij kijk je eerst naar het probleem en vervolgens naar de technologie die daarbij past. Je werkt aan kleine, concrete verbeteringen en leert deze stap voor stap uit te bouwen tot betrouwbare oplossingen. Denk aan een interne AI-assistent die informatie vindbaar maakt, het verwerken van documenten of het automatiseren van terugkerende administratieve taken. Je houdt je onder andere bezig met: In gesprek gaan met collega’s binnen bijvoorbeeld recruitment, planning, sales en ondersteunende afdelingen om hun werk en uitdagingen te begrijpen. Bedrijfsprocessen in kaart brengen en kansen herkennen om tijd te besparen, fouten te verminderen of de dienstverlening te verbeteren. Ideeën vertalen naar een concreet voorstel: wat lossen we op, voor wie en wat levert het op? Prototypes bouwen met AI-tools, eenvoudige code en low-code- of no-codeplatformen. Leren werken met taalmodellen, API’s, data en koppelingen tussen systemen. Oplossingen testen met gebruikers en verbeteren op basis van hun feedback. Samen met IT letten op dataveiligheid, privacy en een goede aansluiting op bestaande systemen. Collega’s helpen nieuwe toepassingen te gebruiken en meten of deze daadwerkelijk resultaat opleveren. Jouw talent Jij bent tech savvy: je maakt nieuwe tools snel eigen, probeert graag iets uit en wilt begrijpen hoe het werkt. Tegelijkertijd heb je oog voor de mensen die ermee moeten werken. Je kunt goed luisteren en technische mogelijkheden in begrijpelijke taal uitleggen. Je hoeft nog geen ervaren AI-engineer te zijn. We zoeken iemand met een goede basis, nieuwsgierigheid en de motivatie om te leren door te doen. Daarnaast: Beschik je over hbo- of wo-werk- en -denkniveau, bijvoorbeeld vanuit Business IT & Management, Informatica, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science of Technische Bedrijfskunde. Kun je een proces logisch ontleden en doorvragen tot je begrijpt waar het echte probleem zit. Heb je al geëxperimenteerd met AI of automatisering, bijvoorbeeld tijdens je studie, stage of een eigen project. Heb je basiskennis van programmeren, bijvoorbeeld in Python of JavaScript, of kun je met eigen projecten laten zien dat je dit actief leert. Vind je het interessant om te ontdekken hoe data, applicaties en API’s samenwerken. Werk je zorgvuldig en controleer je of een oplossing ook in de praktijk goed functioneert. Neem je initiatief, vraag je hulp wanneer dat nodig is en sta je open voor feedback. Communiceer je helder in het Nederlands en kun je Engelstalige technische documentatie begrijpen. Ervaring met bijvoorbeeld n8n, Make, Power Automate, SQL of het bouwen van een AI-assistent is mooi meegenomen. Je hoeft deze tools nog niet allemaal te beheersen. Laat ons vooral zien wat je al hebt geprobeerd, wat je daarvan hebt geleerd en wat je graag wilt bouwen. Wij bieden jou Een start van je carrière waarin je technologie leert toepassen op echte vraagstukken. Je ziet hoe jouw werk collega’s helpt en krijgt de ruimte om ideeën te onderzoeken, te bouwen en te verbeteren. Voor dit traineeship bieden we je: Een salaris van [bedrag] bruto per maand op basis van [uren] uur. Een traineeship van [duur], met een concreet leer- en ontwikkelplan. Begeleiding door [functie/team], met vaste momenten voor technische feedback en persoonlijke ontwikkeling. Tijd en ruimte om je te verdiepen in AI, automatisering en bedrijfsprocessen. Praktijkprojecten waarbij je van eerste idee tot ingebruikname betrokken bent. Samenwerking met collega’s uit verschillende onderdelen van de organisatie. Over Aethon Bij Aethon verbinden we talent aan organisaties in maatschappelijk belangrijke sectoren, waaronder zorg, kinderopvang, overheid, onderwijs en woningcorporaties. Technologie helpt ons om die verbinding steeds beter te organiseren. Als Trainee AI Engineer draag jij daaraan bij. Door het dagelijkse werk slimmer in te richten, geef je collega’s meer ruimte voor de mensen en organisaties die op hen rekenen. Enthousiast? Laat ons zien wie je bent en wat je nieuwsgierig maakt. Heb je al iets gebouwd met AI of automatisering? Een studieopdracht, eigen experiment of eenvoudig prototype is …

items.desc: Ready to accelerate your career and help shape the future of Energy Tech? At Schneider Electric, we’re not just imagining the future of energy, we’re creating it. Recognized as the World’s Most Sustainable Company by TIME and Statista , we are your energy technology partner, electrifying, automating and digitalizing industries, businesses and homes to drive efficiency and sustainability for all. 12 months. Two missions. One global community. Not just another graduate program, this is an accelerator for your career. Our new flagship global talent program gives early-career engineers the opportunity to put AI and emerging technologies into action, tackle meaningful challenges and discover different parts of our organization through two six-month missions. Learn more: Energy Tech Accelerator Graduate Program Highlights Permanent contract: from day one Program duration: 12 months | 2 x six-month missions Location: Complete both missions in Grenoble, France while joining an international graduate community connected across Boston, Paris/Grenoble, Dubai, Bangalore and Shanghai. Start date: 1 March 2027 Your 12-month Accelerator journey Depending on your starting assignment, you may experience the two missions in either order. MISSION A | Invent the Future Your mission could take you into: Sustainability Advisory Services, Corporate Strategy or our AI Transformation Office , where you could contribute to: Explore what’s next: Research emerging trends, technologies and customers’ needs to uncover new opportunities and help our customers become more sustainable and efficient. Turn complexity into insight: Analyze data, structure strategic or sustainability challenges and help turn insights into recommendations. Make things better, faster: Analyze processes and identify opportunities to simplify, improve, and accelerate the way we work, creating greater business or operational impact. MISSION B | Deliver the Mission Together Your mission could take you into Software & Services, Innovation & Technology, Industrial Automation or Commercial Operations , where you could contribute to: Put the customer at the center: Gather insights from users, experts and stakeholders to understand needs and help refine solutions. Turn technology into solutions: Contribute to digital offers and services and explore how software-defined solutions can improve customer experience and solve real problems. Explore AI as an enabler: Identify where AI could create value and connect technology with real business and customer needs. Start Big. Accelerate your potential Dedicated leadership development: Learning, mentoring, and career coaching to accelerate your leadership skills. Signature experiences: Global onboarding, a global hackathon and attending highly visible leadership or customer events. Global exposure: Build relationships across our international community, with opportunities for immersive international business travel Is this You? Curious and eager to understand how things work Analytical, with a passion for solving complex problems Excited by AI, digital technology and the energy transition Energized working across cultures, in a global environment Collaborative, adaptable and ready to step outside your comfort zone What You Need You graduated in 2024, 2025 or 2026, with at least a Master’s degree or equivalent qualification corresponding to five years of higher education (Bac+5 / European Qualifications Framework Level 7) ideally in Engineering, Computer Science, Data Analytics or a related discipline Your academic background includes exposure to AI, and you’re excited to apply into real-world challenges You already have the legal right to work in France. You can work and communicate effectively in English You are available to start in March 2027 There’s more than one path to great things Your degree matters. Your potential matters more . Whether through an internship, personal project, study abroad or nonprofit work, we want to know what drives you, how you learn, and what you are curious to explore next! Your Journey Continues Your career with us starts on day one, primarily on-site, with flexibility options in line with local office working norms. After your 12-month program, you’ll move into your next role based on your strengths, aspirations and opportunities within the business. Be ready to explore new career paths and locations as your career grows. Ready to accelerate? Join our new global Energy Tech Accelerator program. Apply online by 1 December 2026. €1000 salary range Looking to make an IMPACT with your career? When you are thinking about joining a new team, culture matters. At Schneider Electric, our values and behaviors are the foundation for creating a great culture to support business success. We believe that our IMPACT values – Inclusion, Mastery, Purpose, Action, Curiosity, Teamwork – starts with us. IMPACT is also your invitation to join Schneider Electric where you can contribute to turning sustainability …
